reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really nice place…. Far better than others nearby beaches etc
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely place….. nice bars and restaurants. Museum and gardens…. Very nice place to visit for few days. Beach is wonderful and near The Dunes. Will go again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but often windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach. Found glass and needle on the beach. Wear shoes and be careful. If it blows, it blows a lot here. Toilet costs money. Lunches are expensive. But it is so nice with the dunes and the beach itself. Big waves all the times we were there

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day in a turquoise paradise.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful turquoise sea and beautiful beach with great Italian takeaway restaurants. I recommend the boat teip from Puerto Mogan. The walk from Puerto Rico to Amadores along the sea is breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach is one of those places that stick with you: wide, scenic and dominated by dunes that create an almost desert landscape, unique in the Canaries. It is perfect for long walks, relaxing in the sun and enjoying truly spectacular sunsets.The water is clear and the beach is well maintained, although at times it can be a bit crowded, especially in areas closer to services. However, just move slightly to find quieter corners and enjoy all the beauty of the place.Overall it is a beach that is definitely worth a visit: suggestive, wide and with an atmosphere that invites you to slow down and breathe. A little jewel of Maspalomas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Eden
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lot of place, white sand and everything what you need. Sunny place with a great atmosphere and beautiful water - ideal for families

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Greatest beach on Gran Canaria?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kilometre by kilometer with beach and "waterhole" and bathing possibilities all the way from one end to the other 👍 ♂️ 👍 check web camera before the trip and weather forecast for wind and strong waves

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a beautiful sandy beach several kilometers long. Great for swimming and sunbathing. Two sunbeds and an umbrella can be rented for a slim 7,50 euros per day (unfortunately until we were on the beach everything was always occupied, so again only the towels).  There are some beach bars (including toilet at the back), and some detached nudist areas. Protected dune areas are separated by ropes.Adversity, as usual, lies with visitors rather than nature. Columns of tourists march along the beach as if it were a highway in rush hour traffic. Windy sellers try to turn on their goods. Tourists ignore the barriers of the protected areas, destroying the nature reserves, and last but not least some nudist visitors, who absolutely must present their physical deficits to the world in the textile sector. It is definitely the opposite of a deserted beach, but worth it due to its length.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always beautiful dune
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went for the umpteenth time to Maspalomas, this time Bull Escorial hotel in Playa del Inglés, from there a few minutes and you are on the immense beach of Maspalomas, desert sand, beaches that reach 50 meters between the sea and the promenade, dry heat always, magnificent dunes, the experience of the Sahara in small, a must try

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Natural Beauty of the.world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning unique and a magical natural place and with a sea and climate all year round Spectacular with pleasant places where you can bathe and be relaxed, its coasts its dunes beaches and its wonderful people and delicious food all in general a visit where I will return safe always

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Noise from dealers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very nice,clean beach,but here it's like the fish market in Hamburg.Here you have no rest.Every few minutes drink dealers walk around and shout so loud that you can burst the ear drum.Then the Chinese masseurs run and whether you read books or have eyes closed,they stick the massage card in front of your nose.After that the dealers come with bags,beach towels or sunglasses.I don't know why they don't ban that.There are many bars in 100 meters where you can drink something or shops with beach towels and sunglasses.It's really so annoying.Here is no recreation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach shame about people making it cheap!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don’t get me wrong this is a beautiful beach but it’s what goes on, on the beach which is disturbing. Me and my husband were off to explore this beach and it’s is long stretch of sea and sand. Now we knew there was a naturist part and been on one before but we wanted to get to the high sand dunes. This is a naturist beach buts it’s more than that! I’m not allowed to say what is happen but theses things should not be happening on a pubic beach. Beware don’t take your children through this part of the beach. It’s disgusting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Still a great beach despite the erosion
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was our fourth visit to Playa del Maspalomas and as usual it didn't disappoint.  We got to the naturist beach at kiosk 7. Here there is a beach bar with a toilet. Sunbeds are 7.50 euros each and an umbrella is also 7.50 Euros (payment by card only).  The sunbeds are just in front of the dunes set back from the sea. They are available from 09:00 to 17:00.They have a wind break which they put up around the sunbed area when the winds are high (which is needed when the sand blows off the beach and dunes). It's a laid back atmosphere with mainly couples giving a good balance of males and females. During the week the majority of people are naked here. On the weekends there are some people wearing swimsuits who use the area. There is a gay section at  kiosk 6 where there are mainly males. It is also safe to leave your belongings unattended at the naturist beach area  if you want to go for a swim or a walk along the beach. The naturist area stretches from Kiosk 3 to 7.The one sad side I want to highlight is the apparent erosion of the beach by the sea. It has become more apparent this year.  I've shown this in the attached photos. On one particular stormy day the sea was coming in as far as the start of the sunbeds. They seem to have tried putting in flood defences further down the beach by protecting the beach with pebbles. Hopefully  this erosion is only temporary as it would be sad to lose such a lovely beach.Despite the erosion I still highly recommend this beach. It's my favourite naturist destination.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing and careful: pushy traders and brash thieves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is long and wide and there is the adjacent dune landscape, but we have seen more beautiful beaches. The sand is brownish, suffused with black sand and therefore it is not particularly inviting at the front of the waterline, as the water appears brownish-dirty due to the sand (even if it may not be at all). The beach is very crowded in many sections at peak tourist time. But now two very negative points: there are countless “flying merchants” who want to sell fake sunglasses, handbags and T-shirts and beach towels in a very intrusive way. You might expect this in other holiday destinations, but not on a beach in the Canary Islands in this massive and intrusive form. And worst of all, there's brazen stealing on this beach: We had a backpack stolen from us, lying right next to us in the sand, when we were apparently distracted for a moment by something else. And although there were plenty of people all around, the thief probably escaped just like that. The police we contacted were completely disinterested and said they could make a report for the insurance company, but otherwise they could not Enterprise. This would not surprise you in some holiday destinations if you had imagined otherwise in an EU country like Spain.
So many stones in the water... not pleasant to swim here, they only take cash for the rent of sunbeds and umbrellas. Strange I think

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mooi strand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach and dunes. Many rocks and stones in the sea.  Nice restaurants and bars near the beach. Little shade, a parasol is needed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A quiet and warm place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hello my readers, it is the second time I go and without hesitation you would return infinitely times, I was with a friend and her parents. What I like most is the crystal clear water and lying in the hammock is the best thing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Alone worth the holiday!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Alone worth the holiday! Enjoyable especially in the early morning and at sunset, when the sun seems to play with the ocean waves and golden sand dunes giving unique and always new views...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fijn strand. The sea wonderful not too hot or too cold. There are also shops and cafes along the way. Only downside is that it is often very busy if you do not arrive early enough then all the sunbeds are already taken but there is a lot of place to put your towel. Still, I would recommend it if you are in the area. A little further on are beautiful dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking in the sandstone! And celebrate the Sun Juan with Latin bands
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I took a walk in the sand dunes and it was enjoyable!And because I visited this beach "June 23" I was lucky to live the traditional celebration that takes place in the sandy beach. "Noche de San Juan"The locals from the afternoon become groups, families, friends, and have their food and drinks in order to spend many hours having fun!!We were enjoying the concert with two wonderful Latin bands (we danced a lot) and at 12 p.m. they threw fireworks and all fell into the sea to be washed off by the bad energy.Although there were thousands of people in the sandy, it was impressive that everyone was calm and in a good mood. Don't hesitate if you are a tourist to put your feast on the sand and enjoy the special evening

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dirty and neglected. Dangerous at night around the pond. We will not return.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Many years going at least once a year. Large and pleasant beach. 4 or 5 star hotels. The maintenance of the surroundings is disastrous, dirty and disgusting. The San Bartolomé town hall is completely abandoned, and they say it's the jewel in the crown. After five there is no police or surveillance. We were scared by some foreign minors unaccompanied by two older ones. During the day, the police only make sure that the dogs don't step on the beach. They are anti-pet and have made a mess of everything.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The only thing indigenous to South Island.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's all that's left of the South Island. The beach is fantastic for those of us who think that our concept of the beach is to walk it, swim and not be back and forth. I walked from St. Augustine to the Lighthouse, a good hike that must be done early, then it is too hot.They should for the little that is natural in the south island control more people who get on the dunes to take the selfie and fine. I am funny about all those German guiris who get on them and paint the monkey, when in their country, which I know well the citizens are the police themselves and there they would draw attention to whoever climbed and here they come to do what they do not do there. It is the fault of the one who indulges him. They are not only German, English, Spanish.... But this strikes me with how civic they are in your country...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Moonscape
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Actually we only went to visit the dunes because it was not beach time.The dune landscape is fantastic, it almost looks like a desert but with the sea in the background.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blessed inaction
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good weather, good food, beautiful hotel as well as the surroundings; possible buffet as well as several à la carte restaurants

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit if you like the beach :)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach is definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area, it’s easily accessible and has lots to do and see. Take a taxi to Maspalomas lighthouse & start from there!The beach caters to a lot of people; mostly families and quite a few nudists, there is a section of the beach which is specifically nudist. There are plenty of shops and places to eat along the front; make sure to grab a couple of cold drinks if you’re planning on heading to the sand dunes as it gets hot out there! Or you can just relax on the sand and take a dip in the refreshing sea. After you’ve been to the beach, take a walk back along the front and stop off for a Starbucks in the sun & then hit the Fund Grube shopping centre for everything from perfume to Pandora jewellery.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely huge beach very busy though and no sun beds free. People egnoring the do not all on the dunes. Lots of shops and restaurants

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique dune landscape
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in Gran Canaria. Super extensive and the dune landscape is unique. The beach as well as the water are always super clean. We love coming here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Recommended!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Recommended 😊 In summary....Dunes of MaspalomasRecommended entrance: behind the Hotel Riu Palace Maspalomas, via a wooden walkway that leads to a safe and easily accessible viewpoint.La Charca de Maspalomas & Maspalomas LighthouseWalk along the promenade to the lagoon and lighthouse, ideal for observing nature.Playa de Maspalomas (family area)Quiet beach with fine sand and shallow sea, perfect for children.El Senador Restaurant & Beach HouseLunch with children's menu and sea view.Park of the LighthouseShaded green area where the baby can rest or play in peace.Holiday World MaspalomasEntertainment center with rides and play areas suitable for children.Nomad Gastro MarketInside Holiday World, it offers different snack and dessert options for a delicious snack.Playa de MelonerasIdeal beach to end the day admiring the sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach and various options
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is not a beach of dreams, sand and water are normal. But there are many options for adults. Shopping options and many restaurants nearby. If you walk to the dunes there are zones of nudity that people walk without problems.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Town beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is at one end of the promenade and has a wide expanse of sand with the famous sand dunes further along.  There’s a large area with sunbeds and umbrellas to hire at reasonable rates - 7.50e for two beds and an umbrella when we visited at the end of April - sit where you like and someone will come round to collect your cash.  Plenty of cafes, restaurants and bars nearby on the promenade and I think there’s also a beach cafe further along nearer to the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The horror has a face!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is a joke! 1.5 sq km of sand dunes, completely crowded in most hours and surrounded by a Disneyland-like belt of cheap attractions and accommodation for an estimated 500,000 people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A stunning beach. The best on the island by far. It’s immense and had loads of space. Top tip - there are toilets at the back of the beach kiosks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely place.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We got a taxi from our hotel to Maspalomas today. We got out near the lighthouse. Where there is a long promenade to walk in each direction. Along the first part are several me designer shops and good restaurants. We stopped at one for coffee and cake. (Although for me the didn’t do gluten free) I had to have an ice cream. We sat outside with the ocean behind us on some lovely garden furniture. No one rushed us which was good. There are toilet blocks although where we stopped also had there own.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and clean beach which
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean and beautiful beach. Great refreshments and even toilet facilities on the beach. Sunbeds are €7.50 per day for 2 beds and parasol.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Striking dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, suggestive dunes. Free parking is available nearby.Nice promenade and bar for eating or drinking. Recommended at least one visit while staying on the island!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Ingles 2025.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's always nice at Playa Ingles. Nice people you meet. Many fine restaurants. Wide nice walkways, sidewalks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Insufficient
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach sand isn’t bad, but you can’t find sunbeds. And you’re in a lot of trouble. You need to arrive early. We didn’t like it much

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An absolutely beautiful place to visit, clean, warm, and tranquil. The sea is 19° average across the year so it’s beautiful to take a dip into!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas mon amour!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All the beaches of Gran Canaria are worth seeing and enjoying. Maspalomas is to go and get lost, climb to the top of the dunes and ecstatic looking at the blue of the sea, Atlantico, feel the heat of the blonde sand and fall in love with the landscape: sea or mountains, because if you turn, you admire the beauty of the summits. Gran Canaria a miniature continent...

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas is worth a visit. However it stormed a lot the day we were there, but still a beautiful city. There is a lot to see in Maspalomas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Personal experience for a wonderful holiday.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Canaria in general is run down. Especially the region around Maspalomas and Paya de l'ingles. There is still a lot to offer for queer, woke, and gay society. But not recommended for families, straight couples, teenagers and children. Rundown or even empty former shopping centers. All correspondingly scruffy. Just a minute. Tenerife offers 100x more.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably one of the best and impressive places to go to in Gran Canaria, for free and as far as the eye can see. We went there in the evening when the sun was slowly setting and temperatures were nice. Don’t get there when it’s hot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: GOLDEN SANDS
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach stretches from Meloneras in the West to Playa del Ingles in the East. Running parallel to the beach are many hotels and several restaurants. My wife and I walked along the Golden Sands several times when in the area and the surrounding beauty and relative silence fantastic.

Those who really make a good bet are Cassiano, suenia, pablo, giada & J.J / jayjayLoves their meeting to make the kids & adults feel welcome

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning location, it's a different world, a must visit, spotless clean , plenty of spots for drinks and food a few minutes away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach area next to Maspalomas Lighthouse
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches around the dunes are named differently depending on their location, for example, the east part to the bottom tip is English beach, from that tip to Maspalomas lighthouse is Maspalomas beach. We did not get to go, we were staying on the other side, although we did take a walk nearby. From the lighthouse of Maspalomas can be seen. It's pretty crowded. They say there's a nude area, I'm saying that if you want to go with children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view was amazing. I took a lot of pictures. Very quiet place I highly Recommendation, place not suitable for children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit the sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really impressive, superb dune with an ocean view that happiness, we brought a blanket to rest on the heights of a really great dune, we came back through the beach 🏖️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic location and fantastic weather
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We are currently in Maspalomas in September week 1. Thought it worth updating and correcting some earlier reviews.The beach is huge with plenty of room for everyone and all persuasions.We enter from the Lighthouse end and find plenty of sunloungers for families and everyone wears a costume although a few ladies are topless. Further along the beach towards Playa del Ingles is cabin  8 with tables and chairs for customers to enjoy their drinks. Shortly afterwards is a Red Cross post and this seems to signify the clothing optional area. At cabin 7 there are a number of sun loungers and parasols frequented mainly by nudists, as is the beach around it. The loungers are good value at 7.50 euros for the day but payment is by credit card.Further along is Cabin 6 which flies a Pride flag so aimed at the gay community. No dogs were seen on the beach and beach sellers/massage guys were around but certainly didn't hassle anyone. They knew how to take no for an answer and just moved on.A walk on the dunes gives a new perspective but wear shoes as the sand is scorching in the hot weather.This has just turned into our favorite place in the Canaries.E

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fabulous, vast never create crowds, its location and beauty are postcard. Part establishments, mostly free and equipped. Clean. In some places there are stones when entering the water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lot of dogs. Big change
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visit this area for many years, and love it. Recently I don't know what happened and why, but it used to be area with no dogs around at all. But now there are many, and I mean a lot of dogs around, and unfortunately a lot of dog poo on the ground now and barking at night. This is big change, as there were literally no dogs in this area, place was clean. Now the roads are dirty with dogs poo and nights are not quiet as before. Big dissapointment, starting to think of another place for the holiday. Unfortunately.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day at the beach ⛱️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a lovely day at this beach.Chose to do a shore excursion while on a cruise to the Canary islands. So glad I did.Lovely beach with good facilities.Nice restaurants that are reasonably priced.Will return one day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Immense beach to walk and sunbathe without burdens, nudist area without limits, the whole beach is... Fine sand but also area with many stones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An exotic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are incredibly beautiful. Go there at sunrise for an unforgettable experience. However for swimming it is less top, there are many pebbles!And when the wind blows hard, wear a scarf and glasses to protect your face.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice and extensive beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Possibly the best beach on the island, surrounded by dunes and nature. How inconvenient the difficulty of parking. It has access from the lighthouse area and from the English beach area. There is an area dedicated to nudism. It is worth walking along the shore contemplating the nature and vastness of the beach. Another drawback is the large volume it has, but that is inevitable on an island where tourism is overflowing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes wow!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited from Mogan and came on the bus, really good as the bus station isn’t a far walk to the beach and sand dunes.We walked to the sand dunes - how wonderful those hot! Great water areas to wash your feet after and plenty of cafes etc to get a drink and food. A high end little area of shops near to the beach which also had a supermarket. Really lovely and upmarket area Maspalomas is! Really impressed and world visit again!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The dunes of the desert
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Immense dunes, expanse of endless fine sand, children had fun rolling through the dunes some over 10 meters high, very nice place and certainly pleasant, for those on the island of Gran Canaria is a must visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very good beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very good beach with sun loungers and municipal umbrellas for rent. This makes it affordable to the pocket. Very wide and long beach with option to use your towel if you do not want to rent. I miss showering at all beach access points but, knowing there is drought I understand. Recommended beach if or if

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Suggestive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Immense beach, with the dunes of maspalomas behind. Possibility of both free beach and to rent umbrella and sunbeds for 7,50 €. Around 5 pm they start to collect umbrellas, but you can stay safely and for those arriving from that time onwards can still use the sunbeds for free. Apart from perhaps the first "lido" coming from the parking lot, the next (from kiosk n.7) are mostly nudist beaches, but not exclusive (you can therefore also stay in costume). The various kiosks have just a drink, some ice cream / snacks, so it is recommended to go equipped. We stayed in mid-August and still found it quiet.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sea and beach is great but why too few sunbeds and umbrellas?sale of liquor is minimal, toilet open until 17.00 and also the umbrellas are removed at 17.00 depending on the catering industry which can not process the mass no water activity no.... Have had better beaches there is much more to get out of this...😎😪

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Terrible, nudists and especially naked men walk around everywhere and these lie among the dunes waiting for other men to visit. Nice dunes and beach, but I feel that because of the freedom of the LBGT doctrine the island has been totally ruined. Starting point is entirely aimed at the WOKE people and sex toys are sold openly on the street and supermarket. reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fint
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place to swim, but there are long walking distances to the beach itself and the sand dunes. The duvets themselves were not as beautiful as in the pictures, there was, among other things, a lot of garbage there... but very fun to swim in the sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Okay, but nothing enchanting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Better than anything in san agustin, but a further away from the beds (7,50eur for 2 beds and 1 umbrella) to the water, in which unfortunately many large stones lie. It was clean, but it didn't invite us to swim. The restaurants all seemed like 0815 touri-bequatcher, only the surf burger stood out STRONGLY with loving furnishings - but we were not after burgers. Various "beach towel" sellers and massage providers annoy almost every second (sometimes even touching to persuade the massage, which is not even clear) that it is already annoying. From 1000/1030 it quickly became full. For the dunes it was too hot for us with a small child at 34 degrees, we can't say anything about that. all in all ok, but no reason for us to come back again, because it comes close to playa amadores here in nothing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots of sand but not on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are fantastic but the beach is not even bathing, apart from the cold water as everywhere in the Canaries, even in July, waves, difficult currents and there is no sand in the shore but stones and stones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach BUT......
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach we hired two loungers and a parasol which was a great price, but unfortunately we was absolutely hounded by men constantly trying to sell you rubbish, then there were men and women offering massages etc then a women selling drinks, than a man selling fruit / drinks absolute nightmare we couldn't wait to get of the beach and back to our hotel never again, surely something needs to be done to stop these people annoying others, how I kept my cool I don't know....... I was looking for a nice quiet relaxing time, at one point I actually pretended I was sleeping to stop these men trying to sell us rubbish l.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalamos !!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular beach in the south of the island, mountains of blonde sand in continuous motion, which makes the landscape constantly change no day is the same, you can observe these dunes from the viewpoint, it is a natural beauty

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No nudist beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are beautiful, but the so-called nudist beach is 'clothing optional'. In fact, 95% are clothed. It doesn't feel right to be naked in there. Everyone looks at you and keeps clothes on themselves. Not recommended!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful site
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Exceptional site the beach is perfect.A dream vacation.You have to do it if you go around.I highly recommend it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely sandy beach. Sea was lovely and warm. Wear swimshoes if going swimming as there are a few rocks before you get far out. Also the sand burns your feet so they are a must ! We walked to the sand dunes, nothing to see but sand really. People come around selling things whilst you are sunbathing, which is a nuisance. Paid 7.50 eur  for 2 sunbeds and parasol, which was worth it, but when you have paid, you dont expect to be harassed by sellers. Also payment was by card only. Walked along the prom, past the lighthouse and visited a few shops.  Lovely area, would definitely visit again, a lot nicer than Playa del Ingles

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand dunes, breathtaking views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is absolutely beautiful, with miles of sand dunes and plenty to explore. There is a walk you can do from the Dunes to the light house following the nature reserve path, it is mainly sand though. Please take a drink with you as it gets very hot. Breathtaking views!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is very beautiful nature that you should not skip there.not always easy to walk but still recommended. Beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kiosk 7 beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The gay beach is now one kiosk #5 further along with rainbow 🌈 flags a few hundred yards along.you can’t miss it Kiosk 7 was busy & frequented with mainly middle aged& older couples/solo mostly all nude. Sunbed+ parasol E7.50 card only. Kiosk has snacks/ice creams/ drinks/bar area with chairs and parasols plus  toilets. There’s a big LOVE sign on the beach If coming from Maspalomas lighthouse end of beach  10-15 mins walk, easier to walk along the shoreline than through the Dunes. Sand gets very hot. Take only your sandals/beach shoes to the sea when going for a swim in the sea. Naked swimmers and clothed people walkers all on shoreline, no issues. Some couples left their sunbeds & bags for a bit to head into the Dunes behind kiosk for a nude afternoon stroll.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful on the island...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach on the island of Gran Canaria....services and restaurants available, white beach with sunbeds and umbrellas at honest prices.Easily accessible by bus (Faro Maspalomas stop)Not to be missed..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, Sand, and Freedom...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Looking for a beach with a vibrant LGBTQ+ atmosphere in Gran Canaria? Look no further than Maspalomas Gay Beach! Here's your ultimate guide to experiencing this slice of paradise.Getting There:RIU Palace Passage: This route is perfect if you're staying around the RIU Palace area. Follow the designated poles and path – it's important to stay within these boundaries to avoid fines.Playa del Ingles Walk: Enjoy a scenic stroll along the beach from Playa del Ingles. Keep an eye out for the gay section around halfway. Look for the festive rainbow flags near bar number 8!Beach Bliss:Lounging in Comfort: Ditch the bulky beach bag! Convenient cabins are located along the access road where you can rent sunbeds and umbrellas for a reasonable price (around €7.50).Clothing Optional: Feel free to embrace the freedom! While nudity is common here, you can choose what makes you comfortable. Most beachgoers tend to go without clothes.A Word on Cruising: Be aware that cruising in the dunes, which used to be more prevalent, is now discouraged. Police patrol the area, so it's best to enjoy the beach for what it is – a relaxing and fun atmosphere.Final Tips:Relax, soak up the sun, and enjoy the welcoming vibes of Maspalomas Gay Beach. With its stunning location, convenient amenities, and open-minded atmosphere, it's the perfect place to unwind and have a great time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The weather didn't help, it was always cloudy in the morning. The water in the hotel pool and on the beach was cold and therefore not possible to enjoy. It's a place to visit once because the island is small.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely an absolute must with a little detour into the dunes.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastically spacious and very clean beach with a view of the adjacent dunes and the sunset. During the day, adventurous skydivers land in the adjacent dunes. Due to the enormous space, there is enough space to lie down here even in high season. The sand heats up a lot during the day, so a visit to the dunes barefoot is highly recommended, at least in the evening. The transition from the beach to the dunes can occasionally be a bit rocky.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best of Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views were amazing. We took a lot of photos! Awesome . You can't miss it if you go to Gran Canaria. Unforgettable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Dunes a must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very relaxed area with stunning views you do feel like your in the desert. Enjoyable visit as part of a walk to playa de Ingles

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent landscape and canary
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A truly peaceful, splendid place and if you want to go for a walk, there are several marked trails available. Choice of beaches for all tastes… family/gay/nudist! The only problem is the water is cold: you have to be brave to swim (but doable 😜)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice view for nice photos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice experience. You can park for free in the street of the RIU hotel. You walk under the arch of the hotel and you are there. A tip: take good sunglasses with you, as the sand blows into your eyes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hot days at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was on holiday with my partner May 2023 and came the beach a couple of times. Beautiful beach with some clothing optional areas little bars/cafes here and there. Surrounding sand dunes are something else. Can be a little rocky in places

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique surroundings. Relaxed stay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful walks along the beach, relaxed atmosphere. Walking barefoot through the dunes is just wonderful (better in the morning, afterwards it gets quite hot under your feet). Lots of opportunities to take a break at kiosks. Toilets available. We will definitely come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing  sand dunes walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing walk through the gorgeous sand dunes. Just follow the wooden stakes and you'll not get lost. Amazing  views of the sea all along

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Essential visit if you go to Gran Canarias. Very extensive beach with immense yellow sand dunes, where it is a joy to climb them and with spectacular views.On very sunny days the sand can burn quite a bit, but with sneakers or t-shirts it is easily solved.In some places nudism is practiced.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just saying awesome. Everything very careful, very clean.The sand burns quite a bit but it can be solved with flip flops or beach shoes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holidays 2023
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach on the islands, for walking or sunbathing, a wonderful place, it has spaciousness to be quiet and depending on the time of year you go, few people...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely 💯 worth seeing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was an absolute highlight for our children to climb the dunes and slide down. The view over the sea and the beach is also wonderful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: For a walk on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are unique and worth a trip. The beach is very busy in some places with walkers with and without clothes. It's inviting to go for a walk. The spot at the lighthouse is suitable for surfers. But beach experience to swim. Maybe for half a day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes and sand and wind
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large expanse of sand dunes that reaches the sea with a very large beach on the open sea, very windy with waves and cold water. It didn't excite me

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Get it right
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Siting on the beach for a few days know kiosk 3 ,weather and beach beautiful, great staff in the kiosk,one let down 3 toilets only one being used ,lock broken on the door for the time we have been visiting the beach.....low and behold a guy turned up in the middle of the day ,took 2 hours to fix it so no toilet facilities, just gone about an hour and guess what the lock doesn't work on the toilet.Its beyond me why he bothered it's the same old story when it comes to the tourist facilities, especially on the beach .I guess we are lucky the flusher works [he didn't have to touch that] for a few years coming here they're were no facilities as they were waiting to see what contract the governing body were going to offer,they only ones that were inconvenience by this was the tourist ,the ones who spend there time and money here to keep the economy going.....wake up and smell the roses lads [people running the island] people will eventually go somewhere else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a wonderful time on Holidays in Maspalomas in February 2024 where we stayed in Vista Oasis Bungalows for 1 Month. We visited the beach and restaurants most days and enjoyed evening walks along the promenade

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Island "Dessert" Experience!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very unique experience to walk over these sand dunes to the sea, making use of the well-marked pathways (distances markers included). This experience can be undertaken after walking or swimming at the beach or vice-versa after a walk toward the sea across the dunes. There is also a wonderful pathway along the top to view the whole "dessert" scene in all its glory. The latter option is ideal for the more physically challenged as walking the dunes needs considerable determination and not a little strength. I personally walked along this paved pathway to the Riu Palace Maspalomas  Hotel where there is a small viewpoint with excellent indicators of the pathways available  and the distances involved in taking each. The very adventurous head to the lighthouse!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Desert in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unforgettable experience in this amazing place. I felt like in different planet <3 Must try if you have your vacations on the Gran Canaria island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa de Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long and nice beach that is connected to the Dunes (desert). Several different places to rent sunbeds or just take your own pick and pack and take a seat. Nice views and in addition to the beach, it works well for a walk or a run!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Do not miss
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dunes impressive with their surfaces and the feeling of desert. A marked trail, otherwise don't hesitate to get lost there.Be careful not to leave your trash behind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach. Very big and with a lot of people. The weather was wonderful and I went swimming and walking for the whole afternoon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes are Incredible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Totally unique experience walking the sand dunes of this wonderful natural reserve. Expect lots and lots of sand and a fantastic beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful beach and light house however ruined by tourist traps trying to sell you rubbish and time shares. I lost count how many times I was approached on the beach by people trying to sell me beach towels. Walk past restaurants theres people trying to get you to go in or you have a look at a menu and they are already setting up a table to get you to sit down. What should be a relaxing day at the beach turns into the opposite.  Too touristy and too many people pestering. Has put me off visiting this area again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not Phew!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For the dunes, it's nothing extraordinary... when we saw the Pyla dune!!!! Not at all the impression of desert as they sell us for excursions… in the middle of town and along the tourist beach… big disappointment. Paid parking required!! Because no place to park

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everything we wanted
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everything we wanted, brilliant sun sea and sand, plenty of entertainment in the evenings with ample choices of places to eat and drinks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very average
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very average beach. Lots of black pebbles. Sand not really golden. Waves too big to swim in. Fairly pretty dunes but traveled by thousands of tourists which is a bit of a waste. And above all, very clever pickpockets try to steal from your backpacks. A couple along the main promenade average size. Woman with black and red hair, traveler type. Caucasian man.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Naked exhibitionists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did this walk with our girls a few days ago.   Naked people sun bathing in the dunes is one thing but these guys are walking butt naked on the path with their tackle swinging. Definitely an exhibition element to it.  Wouldn’t recommend for families

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Maspalomas dunes are a wonder. There are several viewpoints from the paths but you can walk into the dunes and after 5 minutes the people disappear and you get to experience the dunes almost to yourself. Beautiful !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Handsome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: To see, breathtaking panorama, easy to reach on foot or by bus, very particular and evocative with a wonderful peace

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach to escape
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Too windy, it’s usual here!What has unfortunately changed is the ban on retreating into the dunes where we were protected from the sand and the wind, it was happiness.And as always, for a small percentage of people who do not respect the place, everyone is prohibited from doing so.But of course, these people are still there.I've been coming here for a long time but it's over forever.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: one day visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular views and nature. Loved exploring the dunes then spending time relaxing on the beach. local bars and restaurants for tapas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach weather and laid back people are friendly and the water is warm for this time of year

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean beach alternative naturalists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place sandy beach goes for miles Atlantic ocean fab Beware of nudists if that's not your thing.It is a gay beach in parts and we did see mangrove areas being used for hook up place but kept on walking.We don't offend easily some may do.Relaxing places to chill  up near playa ingles part 😎

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice to have seen.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice to have seen. Not very special for a Dutchman who regularly visits the Dutch coast. Dutch dunes are also beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too many rocks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful thing about a beach is being able to walk on it barefoot, a feeling of freedom which unfortunately is lacking on this beach because due to the many stones that are not removed it is almost mandatory to wear footwear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just great. Very spacious, well-kept and you can surf. The surrounding restaurants are a bit weaker, as they are very touristy. But the environment is fantastic

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk to the lighthouse
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long beach that, among other things, leads to the lighthouse in Maspalomas. If you go from San Agustin/Playa del Ingles on the beach, it takes about 1.5 hours. At the bottom of the bend there were very large rocks that made walking barefoot a little uncomfortable, but you can walk further up from the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views were amazing...it really did feel like we're in the middle of a desert. we took loads of photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really impressive dunes that you can walk around, up, down and through. Well marked tracks to the lighthouse and the botanical gardens. Need sensible footwear as some bits are stoney and some sharp bits off the trees

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa de inglis restort
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sandy beaches but many steps to get to them. Although the German Bath and sun bathe naked it's worth walking over the sand dunes, take plenty of water as it's extremely hot. At the other end the beaches are split by rocky groins to break the waves but its very safe for kids and poor swimmers like me.take your litter with you as there are bins at the steps and water to clean the sand from your feet. A few eaterys on the beach but many places at the top. Sat and wed market well sign posted but be warned pickpockets are around and if the have no prices on products haggle hard cos a 45 euro leather wallet came rapidly down to 20. Local bus to Morgan was very simple and so was the aquarium,  pay cash or by card we used a revelute card aquarium was about 12 euros for 2 each way and Morgan was about 4 euros each. Its a long way to the view point so do it slowly and early and again warning of pickpockets. If you like dancing it's free at the kasbah shopping centre in the evening. Lots of other activities available Inc go cart racing, the buggies are mostly on winding roads with only a tiny section off road but still great fun. The downfall is they tout for tips at the end ,and I think it's wrong if you need more money ,charge more. Great hotel so we are considering going back for longer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Trip to Meloneras
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a long way to walk in loose sand if you don't have healthy legs. From RUI we took 35 minutes and from Maspalomas lighthouse it takes approx. 20 minutes to walk. Sunbeds with parasol cost €7.50. Otherwise, you can get plenty of good drinks in the kiosk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful long sandy beach with lots of public traffic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great combination together with - or better yet after - hiking through the dunes. At the western end there are many places to stop for a bite to eat, and you can also look at the natural brackish water lake.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, but the dunes a little further on are more impressive!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Through beautiful dunes and then past the beach to go to Meloneras. On the far left there is a kind of bar for the LGTBQ community and nudists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quick visit and awesome dunes.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I didn’t have much time to explore the dunes, but it really seemed like a good place to visit. You can cross the sand dunes and walk to the beach and enjoy the water if you want to, and lots of people were.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalamas Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is fantastic and large. Sea lovely for swimming and body boarding with the quite large waves. Downside is why some men on the nudest section think is it ok to openly play with themselves and get away with it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Necessary visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, wonderful, with a bit of waves almost permanently, but beautiful dunes for photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk, swim or sunbathe
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long beach with huge dunes as the backdrop.  Spotlessly clean with grey sand. I walked from Playa de Ingles to Meloneras which takes about an hour. Expect to see nudists  mingling with you as you set off to Meloneras. I didn’t swim but there were plenty of people in the water. There are a couple of  bars on the beach should you need refreshments. Take a walk in to the dunes as they are amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quite an experience, it is a mini desert.Great for walking or taking a camel ride.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brill awesome superb best place iv  ever see with my  eyes.must see but be carefull.very hot.from above and below.wind can cause
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastical area of the world.you can find a seat and watch the dunes roll with the wind.magical.not to forget expierience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice to see.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful dunes if you are in the area, definitely stop by. Sand is very hot on the feet on sunny days. Be on time, it can be very busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: windy and decadent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: almost unlivable beach: always windy and full of old nudists up to the Maspalomas lighthouse. It's just worth a walk. Lack of toilets. I do not recommend taking an umbrella and sunbed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Without a doubt one of the best beaches in the Canary Islands
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach is par excellence one if not the best beach in the Canary IslandsThere are almost seven kilometres of beach surrounded by an extraordinary dune parkOn most of the beaches you can enter the sea peacifully because the sand reaches a long distance into the waterWhen there are high waves it is wonderful to jump with them The beach has no currents so you can swin calmyThere is a beautiful promenade full of restaurants where you can eat buy taste an ice cream or simply have a coffee or a beerThere are a number of hotels of all kinds of categories and prices to stay and enjoy a few days of this wonderful beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The food and drink kiosks are now open!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For the last three years, since the pandemic, the food and drink kiosks at Maspalomas beach have been closed. Now the upgraded and renumbered kiosks are open. They serve a variety of food and drink, although more expensive than the local supermarkets (see price list in the attached photos). Whilst we were there we found only one open toilet. This was at the storage kiosk B between kiosks 5 and 6. There is an attendant there who will charge you 50 cents to use the toilet. At all the other kiosks the toilet was locked. Lack of toilet facilities is still an issue at this beach.Sunbeds and umbrellas are still cheap as 2.50 euros per item (7.50 for 2 sunbeds and an umbrella is a bargain). They fill up quite quickly at kiosk 7 with most sunbeds taken after midday, even on a weekday.The kiosk numbers are now:Kiosk 4 at the Playa del Ingles end of the beach is naturist.Kiosk 5 and 6  at the middle of the beach is populated by mainly gay beach goers and naturists. These kiosks are close together.Kiosk 7 at the Maspalomas end of the beach (where we went) was naturist.Kiosk 8 near the lighthouse in Maspalomas  is non naturist.I never walked as far as kiosk 3 in Playa del Ingles. I assume this is non naturist.This was our second time on the beach at Maspalomas. We would highly recommend this beach for naturists and non naturists too. Be warned though that the waves can be very strong and it can get very windy. At kiosk 7 the sunbed attendants do put up a wind break around the sunbeds when it does get windy which is a nice touch.With food and drink facilities now available this beach has become our favourite beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: At the beginning of the dunes…
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From the beach you can admire the lighthouse, the luxury hotels and the immense sand dunes that act as a fantastic appendage to the city of Maspalomas. Beach with sunbeds and umbrellas for a fee (€7.50). the beach staff begins to collect the umbrellas, leaving the sunbeds, as early as 4.00pm, 4.30pm. The sunbeds are therefore fully available to those arriving at that time. Many characteristic places to dine or drink. It can be reached from the city by bus or taxi (€7/8).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely Beach to visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a trip to beach as our Hotel (Vistaflor Bungalows) laid on a free bus, as did a few other hotels. We were dropped off near the Sand Dunes to the left of us as we walked South a short distance to the Beach. It was a glorious day, very hot with clear blue skies. We wasn’t quite prepared, and I would advise on taking a sun tent or a parasol. However we keep topped up with Sun Cream and kept Hydrated. The Beach was very clean. There were a few traders asking to sell blankets, hats, glasses etc, the usual. We took shelter in a few of the bars for drinks and Ice Cream, there are so many to choose from. However from experience, I can highly recommend Dunnes if you want a child friendly menu too. If your are in Maspolomas, you must visit the beach, you will not be disappointed. I have attached a few photos, but a camera phone in the sun doesn’t do it justice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach where you can walk along the shore of the beach for kilometers from Playa del Inglés to Meloneras, for me one of the best, if not the best beach in the Canary Islands.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The dunes make it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Let’s face it you are there because of the dunes. The beach itself is okay. Wavy and full of sand so it’s not clear. It’s a bit shallow at the beginning so that was nice. The way the waves come in leaves a nice pattern.  You can walk and walk and hit the dunes. There are shops and restos close by. But I’m sure there are better looking beaches elsewhere on island

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Huge sandy beach surrounded by the beautiful dunes of Maspalomas. Presence of several kiosks along the promenade by the sea. There is a series of paid sunbeds and umbrellas in one area only at a cost of €7.50 all day. Showers are free while public bathrooms have to be paid for. Near the sunbeds there are several places to eat and shop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: In the dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sublime landscape with numerous sand dunes, beautiful water, clean and pleasant beach with good places to eat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The dunes and beach of Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Splendid location: beautiful beach, beautiful and well-kept seafront (really long), try the camel ride along the dunes. A place that makes you dream.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Huge sandy beach. Large part for nudists and gays. Deckchairs and sunshades at a reasonable price. 2 deckchairs + a sunshade -7.5 euros/day. Too bad that at 5 p.m. they remove the sun visors

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely an experience to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The entrance to the Dunes is simply crazy, it looks like it was the entrance to the desert of old Egypt, a truly breathtaking cisa with its immensity

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OK but better beaches that are quieter.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although nice wide sandy beach, not enough sun beds for hire, very busy and a lot of beach hawkers flogging everything you didn't want.  Promenade and area by shops were quite nice. We only visited the once, which was enough.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Desert in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kilometers of golden sand with incredible dunes that extend from Playa del Ingles up to the Maspalomas lighthouse... breathtaking landscape with animals of different species that live inside camouflaged between the sand and the small green oases that can be found here and there ..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Probably the best beach on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is probably the very place that our imagination pictures when we hear the phrase “ocean beach.” Soft sand, rolling turquoise waves. A coastline of several kilometers, along which you just want to wander alone or holding someone’s hand. At the beginning, near the lighthouse there is beach infrastructure - sunbeds (7.5 euros for 2 sunbeds and an umbrella), cafes, showers, a first-aid post, lifeguards and quite a lot of people. Further on, there are noticeably fewer people, the dunes begin and you can be almost alone with the ocean, throwing off all conventions and the remnants of clothing. The sand glistens in the sun, there are areas where it is almost black, and others where it is very light. . After lunch, umbrellas are removed and you can use sunbeds for free. The ebb and flow of the tides are very pronounced. So even if you are vacationing in another place, it’s worth coming to this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible beach. We came twice during our holidays. Plenty of restaurants and snack bars. We had a lovely time

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very beautiful but supposedly closed to visitors...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Free parking allows you to visit.Small sandwich and drinks seller next to the site. Be careful, site apparently closed to visitors....a ranger told us that it was closed even though there was no clear sign, just a long piece of tape around a passage... Nothing clear, so lots of people who go there and are fined... Otherwise very beautiful site with a 1.5km uphill walk which is a bit stinging, provide drinks and snacks for the children when it "reopens"....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very hot sand so don’t go barefoot!   Beautiful and clean sand and it too far to walk to the water. Plenty of bars, shops and eateries nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach itself is nice we were lucky and had brilliant weather it’s sandy and easy to get on to and plenty of space. I imagine on school holidays though it will be rammed (we visited out of term time). You can rent sun beds with umbrellas whilst you’re here. There is a natural reservoir you walk along to get to the beach is a 5 min walk but the walkway itself is concrete. The only reason I have given 3 stars is there are much much better beaches in Gran Canaria so if you are spending money to come here I’d maybe look more toward the south west coast like Amadores beach-which was gorgeous and Anfi which is also so lovely much much better than Maspalomas beach. Also you are harassed by beach sellers on Maspalomas beach every 5 mins trying to sell you stuff we had an unfortunate situation with a man who agreed a price for an item took our money and then upped the price, we decided we would rather have the money back and politely declined the item and he decided then he couldn’t understand us. To save a scene I told him he could keep the couple of euro he’d got of us take his item and go. Put a downer on our trip here within the first 10 min of arriving. Such a shame because if they weren’t here I’d have probably scored 4/5 just when you’ve got your children with you it’s alittle intimidating.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No place for kids.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No good places for kids. We been in the dunes and unfortunately was many naked people. I was on shock and sad for my kids to see this miserable show... first and last time I will come to Gran Canaria.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean beach. Plenty of quality bars and restaurants. One of the best purpose built resorts we have been to.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can access this beach from the resort maspalomas near the shops and restaurants. Or you can walk behind d the dunes from San augustin  to the large RUI hotel in PLAYA DEL INGLES . There is a path to walk along and u can access the dunes at any point . They are large and you can walk along the sea edge also. A must do if you are here

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked into faro maspolomas from Playa del Ingles one morning. What a surprise when we arrived It is a beautiful centre with lovely shopssnd restaurants.  A great seafront promenade. Would definitely stay there in future rather than Playya del Ingles!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A bit disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I did not enjoy Maspalomas as much as I thought I was going to. As I only stayed four days I thought it was not worth hiring a car. It would be more relaxing to stay in the area as I thought it would offer all I needed for a short relaxing break. However all people seemed to be doing there was relaxing, sunbathing and eating. The sea front near the lighthouse has a range of shops, but you cannot spend all your time here as the clothes are mostly expensive. There is an abundance of restaurants, however once you have tried one you have tried them all. They are all mostly outdoor seating venues which serve steak, seafood, paella, pizza, pasta and chicken. All the food is decent but not wow, and it's not that cheap as I thought it would be. Once you have eaten in one, you have eaten in them all as each new restaurant reminds you of the last place you ate.Player del Ingles has the same purpose built tourist units as Maspalomas, but without the designer clothes and perfume shops. It just sells the souvineers with 'I love Gran Canaria' on, the fake designer clothes, and the restaurants are the same as in Maspalomas but slightly cheaper. In Ingles there are bars too, most of which serve food and look like the restaurants but contain a few drunk pensioners waving Dutch flags to country music from the 70s. The bus services are terrible. You can never find a taxi however and wait at an empty taxi rank for half an hour. On a Sunday its particularly bad. The water park and zoo are very far away and difficult to access. The urban area is of very low density with lots of wasteland between buildings. Mainly low-rise tourist accommodation with big open spaces of rubble between them and a dried up river. Much of the area smells of sewage. You end up having to walk a lot, not knowing where to go. There are more non English speakers than people who speak English and the afternoon range is skewed towards the older tourist and is you are under 40 years old you won't meet many tourists the same age or younger. You will just see the odd one as you go about your travels.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brilliant
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s amazing! An experience once in a lifetime. I’ve seen the dunes combined with the Atlantic Ocean. So much sun and fine sand

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Sand Dunes are so beautiful.However,was not aware that on the other side of the Dunes was a nudist beach.Was a bit of shocker,seeing people with their bits out😂

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Servatur Don Miguel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Adults only hotel right in centre for everything. Chinese across road was great. Centrium restraurant in Yumbo centre amazing food and secret garden bar tucked away above BK was stunning

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Something for everyone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Something for everyone here. Stunning dunes, great beach for walking, running (around 5k end to end) sun bathers paradise clothed or not. A few shacks along the beach where you can stop for a drink. Sea was even quite warm in Feb if you fancy a dip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: These dunes are amazing, you can't believe the enormity of them until u are there, stunning scenery, you can walk for miles, and its just beautiful. When visiting I would try go on a day that is not very windy,, they day we went it was quite windy and as you would expect the sand tends to get everywhere

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Astonishing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed the seaside walking from El Faro to Playa del Ingles (about 90 min). You need to know that a large portion of this beach is allowed for nudists. The walking from the beach crossing the Dunas reserve is great as well. Laying for sunbathing here by strong wind could be adventurous. Bars and restaurants around are offer a good choice for lunch while visiting the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a good walk from our hotel but it is well worth it. You can walk for miles on the beach. There are also paths to walk overlooking the sand dunes with great views. It is a beautiful area. A must visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: High prize shop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For me it was a good expiriance I was having fun with my parents and all was good but a little bit windy but If I was you I will not buy anything in their small shops or what is that beacuse one Fanta or CocaCola is 4€ so bring with you food. I would not recommend you go if you don't want to see naked people). But it was good beacuse you have a place to play and discover.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No good in January. Very windy, could not walk around.sand blown around. Had to get inside to escape the awful weather. Day trip. Would not stay here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A vast beach for everybody
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This three-kilometer-long golden sand beach is located next to the dunes and close to the lighthouse. It is usually windy here.The eastern end next to the Playa del Ingles beach offers family-friendly services such as lounger and parasol rental, and showers. To the west towards Maspalomas lighthouse, you will find the nudist areas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: cold
reviewsWithKeywords.text: went in january and it was 5 degrees colder than Mogan and the wind was just awful. Felt like hundreds of pins hitting your legs. Sand everywhere - just horrible and it had been like this for a week apparently and Play de ingles worse. Would not contemplate going to this area in January

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice leisure walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large sandune area between maspalomas & Playa de ingles. A great seashore walk with plenty of photo opportunities. Areas of deckchairs to rent and various watersports available. Except to see a few naturist sunbathing. You can find secluded Areas amongst the dunes for secluded sunbathing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No cash for sunbeds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excelle ya beach , just a small tip for any visitors the  sunbeds and parasols along the beach are now card payments only ,no cash accepted ,  there is a small area to the left end of the beach near the watersports centre that takes cash

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Christmas on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Never seen a beach like this before only on TV beautiful sand dunes and no litter can spend hours just walking carefree up to meloneras or just take in the views or wander along the promenade just spent Christmas here totally different Xmas and Christmas trees and decorations everywhere

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, fantastic views but beware nudist parts
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, and excellent views. The dunes are incredible and definitely a must see in Gran Canaria. Be careful when you are with children, there are nudists on the beach near the sand dunes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just beautiful. Large sandy beach and amazing sand dunes , great views.Surf school on the beach.Some nice little bars on beach promenade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach !!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a beautiful beach spread over a long stretch going up to Meloneras.  The beach had sunbeds and parasols for 5  euro. Unfortunately no Kisoks were open. During long walk one can pass through dunes and nudist section. The water sports facilities were very limited. One thing I liked most  which I used to see everyday in the morning from my hotel balcony was  that beach was cleaned thoroughly  early in the morning. One can easily spend entire day on the beach.Very good for long walk...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this beach - as always.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had 2 weeks of great relaxation on the "middle" section of the  beach.  Wasn't too windy, got quite hot, and was almost always blazing sun!I wish whatever battle is going on about the kiosks could be resolved; they are still closed.  They are very handy, and are a focal point also.  However, there is no shortage of vendors wandering the beach - though I don't think they're meant to. So, authorities, open the kiosks, or give the vendors a break!Also note; if you want to pay for sombreros/sunbeds you MUST PAY BY CARD - not cash.Great time though!  :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning views of the dunes from a distance and when walking through the path route which takes you along to the beach, be prepared and take some drinks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: First Visit  Naturist Maspalomas Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First time in October we visited the Naturist beach ,we were staying at Magnolias Natura which is superb, the free mini bus dropped us off at the beach side of the lighthouse, Disappointed with the beach found the walk quite long and tiring on the sand we reached kiosk 7 which was naturist all the kiosks were closed , but a guy comes round selling drinks.The sea  was cloudy  sandy and grey the sunbeds were comfy but looked very tiredalong with the shades. The umbrella   and beds were only 7.50 euros which was good.We had a nice time at the beach , but have been to much nicer nauturist  beaches in Greece.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Naturist Beach Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A week in playa del ingles,first holiday without the kids for a long long time.So decided to try the naturist part of the beach.Absolutely loved it to bits,hired sun loungers for €2.50 each some days,others just on the sand.Mainly Germans around us,who couldn’t have been friendlier.Lack of toilets was a negative.But can’t wait to visit again next year! 😎

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise for naturists and non-naturists alike
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The non-naturist part of the beach is near to the lighthouse (kiosk 8). Further down the beach at kiosk 6 and 7 is the naturist beach. Kiosk 7 is predominantly gay whereas kiosk 6 is a mixture of people. This was our first visit to a clothing optional beach outside of the UK and what a great experience it proved to be. The beach is best approached via the 2.5 km trail through the dunes from the Riu Palace Maspalomas hotel.  It took around 30 minutes to walk from there as you are walking through sand. This will bring you to the Kiosk 7 area of the beach. The beach is sandy (and gets very hot so wear shoes on the beach) and very clean. There is plenty of space for sunbathing either on sunbeds, on the beach itself or near the dunes.We spent our time on the sunbeds at kiosk 6. As has been stated in other reviews only card payments are accepted for umbrellas and sunbeds. It is 2.50 euros for each item (so 7.50 euros for 2 sunbeds and an umbrella). The kiosks are still closed but there are people who come around selling cold drinks and snacks. Sellers on the beach seem to be carefully controlled as you see the same sellers every day and they are un-intrusive. At kiosk 6 it was mainly naked couples, which was great, with a few clothed people. One downside was that many people tended to smoke and as the sunbeds are close together it was difficult to avoid the smoke.It is safe to leave your belongings on this part of the beach when you go in the sea. We did this and never had any problems.The sea, being the Atlantic, can be very rough at times. However this didn't take away the fun of going in the sea which was warm. There are no toilet facilities at this part of the beach which is disappointing but I'm not going to knock off any marks for this as the overall experience on the beach is fantastic. Our best naturist experience to date.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach next to the dunes; parasol hire very reasonable Nice beachside bars and restaurants Nudist beach further on

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short trip to the south of Las Palmas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sunny days all throughout our stay and the beach is clean and safe and the dunes are amazing. The water sports are reasonable and lots of shops and restaurants all over the area 🏖🍷🌞

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just Beautiful!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just returned from a wonderful week at palm Oasis.Palm oasis is set in the most beautiful grounds , the apartments are fantastic, equipped with what you need , clean and spacious.We stayed on a half board basis , buffet breakfast and evening meal . The food was fantastic , choices and variety to suit all tastes and the fact you can keep going back for more just makes it so worth while , especially when feeding 7 . The pool bar it great for lunch should you require . The staff could not be more helpful , polite and extremely hard working ! The site is a little distance from maspalomas centre but the hotel will have you a taxi in minutes and it’s around 5 euros .  This is the First holiday we’re I’ve actually had days around a pool , normally we would be going off sightseeing. Pool days in such beautiful surroundings have left us all wanting to visit again !Thank you to all at Palm Oasis !!This site certainly deserves more than 3 *

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I and my family really liked visiting this beach Very beautiful beaches. I suggest you visit, you will really like it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice place to see and take some good photos there. Even though it was too hot for me to actually walk down there I enjoyed the view from the little pathway next to it. My daughter and my partner went for a walk there and enjoyed it a lot. View worth seeing!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: El Faro a Lopesan experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited ElFaro at Maspalomas in July. Excellent location, excellent food and staff made this a wonderful break after 3 years without a holiday. The room no 1323 was a side sea view with a lovely large corner balcony looking onto the sand dunes. It is very grey everywhere inside the hotel including the paint on the ceilings which we found a bit dark. The beds were really comfy and lots of fresh towels every day and a chocolate biscuit every evening left by the maid. Only negatives were the air con was not great and the sink (grey ) was right in front of the entrance to the room and in the actual bedroom. Apart from this a really lovely hotel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lack of Kiosks and Toilets
reviewsWithKeywords.text: With the nice new kiosks placed during lockdown it was a real disappointment to not have them open. Also a huge missed opportunity to have toilets installed in the middle of the beach as it's such a long walk to get back to either end to use facilities  if you're spending the day there. For visitors please note that only card payments can be taken for sun loungers and parasols, they are no longer accepting cash and a lot of people were caught out by it. Again forcing customers to take their cards and phones down the beach it would be nice if there were some kind of locker facility by each kiosk for a small fee. Aside from this still a gorgeous clean beach and the attendants were lovely friendly people so heartily recommend a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice and clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: a lovely beach with great facilities also sunbeds are very good value for money they dont take cash so you will need a card to pay

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tacky tourist trap.. Reminded me of Benidorm
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dunes were very pretty (which is why I’ve given it 2 stars instead of 0) but the rest of the beach was a tourist trap selling tatty memorabilia and sorry attempts at English food such as fish and chips and eggs and bacon (undercooked and not very appetising) It is just for tourists basically and doesn’t show any real resemblance of Spanish culture or history. We were hoping for traditional food and tapas but it was just full of cheap market stalls with people that would constantly try and grab you and try and shove cheap looking bracelets on your hand. There was lots of fake designer bags and it had a Benidorm type of vibe, full of shouty middle aged English people. The beach was extremely overcrowded and barely had any sun loungers, everyone was just cramped on the floor (The sand was far too hot to lay on). Nothing much to do or see, there’s a chemist and a supermarket for the locals but apart from that there’s very little to do. There is a nudist beach next to the main one which was all fine and dandy as I like to sunbathe topless anyway (probably the most interesting part of the trip) but we did notice that there was a group of naked men hiding in the bushes which seemed weird and somewhat sinister for a place that openly embraces nudity. If you want to experience some culture whilst you are here, I’d recommend instead travelling to Las Palmas old town as they have art galleries, museums and cathedrals to visit etc. It is an hour bus ride away though so if you are hoping for somewhere nearer-by don’t bother.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Mini Sahara desert 🏜 it’s pretty cool. Lovely places to visit in Gran Canaria but in general island needs a bit of tlc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best place in the wold
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Calm och peacefullLovely ro Wall in the warm sand lonely from other People.Then you can take off your clothes and swim naked in the lovely sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunbeds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fortunately there is a lift down halfway to the beach or the beach would not have been accessible to my friend and I as we are very active 70and 76 year olds but going down would have been ok but coming back up would have been a struggle.
