But once down on the beach it was very nice the sun beds were very reasonable although we just assumed we would need cash to pay so made sure we had this unfortunately it was card only so had to go back to the hotel to get this.one of the visits to the beach we went later in the day and at 5oclock the attendant took away all the sun shades much to everyone’s dismay so was still very hot so we had to leave which I think was obviously what was required.all this in place we still enjoyed our visit to the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful wild beach You feel to be in a place outside the world, instead you are few meters far from bar, hotels and restaurant

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The sand dunes are a sight to behold.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Miles of golden sands, lovely sea and then there’s the sand dunes. Wow, I have never seen anything quite like it. Amazing to witness, even better to scale. You can’t quite imagine just how high and seep they are until you start to walk up one. Amazing. A word of caution though that the beach is quite popular with nudists and as a result, there are many men and women who walk around butt naked all the time here. Just bear it in mind when bringing young children here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth a visit . It is jaw dropping when you first see the dunes it is like something from a movie set or postcard such natural beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you love nature you will surely love this place, suggest to go either early in the morning if you wanna walk the dunes or late in the afternoon after 6 pm when the sand isn’t that hot .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach...HOT sand!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited for the morning with young children. They absolutely loved it, and there were a lot of families at the beach. We used the loungers, but note that you will get charged for these, around €5 I believe, per lounger. This is for the day, how ever long you stay. It was clean, and there were plenty of facilities nearby. The sand does get very hot though, so be prepared to carry children!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wind and sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is really long. The dunes make the beach very special. A negative point is if the wind is blowing: since there are dunes it can happen that there is more sand in the air.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Google and clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excelent  Passwörter along the sea. Smart restaurants and Bars everywhere. We stand in Las Palmas but next time we book in Maspalomas near the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bad burns, good ice cream
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a lovely beach and the dunes are beautiful. Didn’t go into a lot of the shops but the ones we did were good (more clothes shopping than anything else). The Pingüino Soul cafe on the boulevard is lovely - really nice pastries, ice cream and smoothies; you can takeaway and the staff are kind and helpful. Confusing system with the sunbeds - not sure how to rent those and there don’t seem to be signs anywhere? Please be warned that if you burn easily - or even don’t - that the sand can be VERY hot, to the point of burning skin off your feet (speaking from experience). Definitely wear shoes, even if they’re trainers. There are places to buy sandals near the beach also if you don’t have them. Bus station and taxi stands nearby which is good.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach and restaurants
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had two evenings down at the beach, plenty of lovely restaurants and bars. would definitely recommend

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and very clean beach. Many surfers. You can have a great walk from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingles. Beautiful views of the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely place to take a stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful walk along the prom, lots of bars, restaurants and shops to keep you busy as well.  We were there on a Sunday so it was busy with locals as well as holidaymakers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place with lots of sand 😣
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place to go for a walk. Plenty of people and some bar’s a long the first part of it.Recommended is to not wear shoes and socks 🙃

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ok but I wouldn't go back
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited from Puerto Mogan and were rather disappointed at the long bus journey through the enormous town to get to the Playa. We walked by the lagoon and then across the dunes intending to cross to Playa de Ingles at the far side but it was a bit monotonous so we cut down to the coast and then returned by the sea, with a long swim there. The sea was nice and warm for February. the sand was good for walking barefoot. There were quite a lot of people around in the dunes and it didn't feel very wild or special to us. We much preferred our trips up into the mountains.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nude men hanging around  literally!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: These are just dunes...please be careful if you have small children as lots of nude men hanging about in the bushes, when I see him he was very brash standing there wanting me to look...even tho I was with my husband..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunas, sand and ….
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place - pure and wild. Recommended for all. Take the time, out of shoes and enjoy it barefoot.This place is really for all…

reviewsWithKeywords.title: There is nothing not to like!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Coming from the north of England there is simply nothing not to like in this canary island destination. Blue skies and warm sunny days. We love it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk on set pathways or go away seems to be the new policy...not good!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't think you can roam freely on these Dunes any more. There are now just a few  marked pathways when walking from the Riu Palace end of Playa del Inglés and these take you only to the beachfront. The official excuse is that it is a Natural Park and that this measure is to preserve it. This is not the only such Park in Spain and these vigorous restrictions have only been put in place here with, seemingly, such force with park rangers ordering tourists back onto the designated paths. There is, apparently, the threat of fines for transgressions but didn't experience or witness this although there are plenty of rumours circulating that drones and helicopters are being used to enforce a crackdown!!! Certainly there are signs and information boards about sticking to pathways as well as posts set into the sand marking these new routes.So, that seems to be the end of 'free roaming.'Although there are a lot of naughty tourists everywhere, including here where rubbish has been left on the dunes rather than taken away with them, the controlling measures do seem rather over the top. After all, shouldn't we be able to ENJOY this stupendous place without such draconian controls? This is just the sort of thing that many holidaymakers will surely be upset about as, traditionally, this was a great place for roaming free and naked even! There has been an official map released to show s totally forbidden to enter zone...o.k...fair enough but what about the rest of this huge space? Are we to be excluded from enjoying this landscape for ever?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: tired but still fun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: well, what can be said. please remember that i am writing this as we are still in the grip of covid and will bear this in mind. i am here for a month having a break from travelling for the last 2 years. i wanted somewhere warm over the xmas/new year period and it has delivered. very comfatable. i go for a lot of walks and get to see everything at ground level and i have to say the whole place is a mixture of dilapitated and modern. i have been to 2 "shopping centres" which to say are derilict is bigging them up. all the concrete has starting to crumble and roofs missing and the reinforced bars are rusty and exposed. not closed due to covid as it looks like a few years. the medium sized hotels have sprung up and have been allowed to build without proper checks regarding safe building practacies. the dunes are really magnificent and only a brave person will try and walk it but the walk on the beach from playa del ingles to Maspalmas is a good stretch of the legs. plenty of bars and resturants along the waterfronts run by a mixture of scandinavian and european and some are keeping with rules and asking for covid passports. many well stocked supermarkets. a good bus and taxi network. on the whole an enjoyable break and if keeping out of the bigger more expensive hotels your money will go further.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but Rocky sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the shopping and restaurants here but the actual sea entrance was rocky so not really good for swimming unless you have sea shoes. The gay beach is at kiosk 7 towards the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas - Nice Area with Great Shops and Restaurants
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Maspalomas and found it much better than the edge of Playa De Inglis where we were staying. Great shops and places to eat and nice areas to walk too. Seemed a much classier resort

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful walks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A bracing walk along the beach with sand dunes everywhere.  Lots of little places to stop and take in the view and at the start of the walk lots of little cafes to stop and have a drink and relax.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant circular walk.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Vast space with desert-like features. Pleasant circular walk from the large hotel at the entrance to the dunes. Wasn't expecting a huge nudist beach though. The shoreline can get very busy with people taking a stroll. If you don't mind lots of bare flesh, then the dunes are well worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying at Mogan nearby but visited us for the day.I have to say, we left disappointed as the place we were staying was so much nicer.It’s facilities aren’t nearly as good and it is not nearly as picturesque.It is pretty good for walking as it is so big but other than that we much preferred where we were.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing changes to the amenities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a fantastic beach but notoriously windy! Great for a walk.All of the old kiosks have been replaced but none are open. In all of the former locations from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingles the wind breaks and the sun loungers have been removed. Without the wind breaks, sitting or lying on the beach isn’t a pleasant experience! Best avoided for the time being.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have enjoyed this beach for many many years, and it is still beautiful to walk along by the sea or in the sand dunes, and it is still one of the most stunning places to see the sunrise or sunset, but it is not really a beach you can sunbathe on all day unless you have come prepared with windbreakers, parasols/tent and / or your own lounger. Gran Canaria is known for being windy, in our past holidays the kiosks have been open and have had sunloungers, parasols for daily hire and when the wind gets up they would put netting around for you. This is all gone now, we had two aborted attempts to be on the beach, it was not too bad until it reached midday and then you'd be eating the sand and getting sand in places you didn't no you had, it was not pleasant. We asked locally as we thought maybe it was a covid issue, but apparently it is not, the other beaches across the island have sunloungers and parasols out. Apparently, it is a contract dispute concerning the new kiosks, so until this is resolved we won't be visiting the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is a reason this is one of the most visited spots in Gran Canaria... its gorgeous. There is a clearly marked path to walk through to get to the beach. This helps preserve the biodiversity. The beach is extremely windy so if you plan on staying long prep for it. Many were set up with wind/sand breakers and enjoying the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunset at Paradise.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is not much to add to what people already highlights about this place. But one thing that definitely impressed me was the sunset.... Probably the most beautiful I have ever seen in my life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No longer any sun loungers on the beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I used to love the beaches at Maspalomas and Playa Del Ingles but not any more. The sun loungers and parasols have been removed from both beaches, which means you’re guaranteed a sand-blasting every day from 1pm when the wind picks up and the sand starts to blow around. On my previous visits the sun loungers lifted you off the sand sufficiently to avoid the worst effects of the moving sand and they also had netting around the sun loungers area to protect you further. Not anymore, they’ve all gone. Lots of very annoyed people being forced off the beaches this week. We won’t be coming back here sadly :(

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gran Canaria busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hi looking to travel to Gran Canaria is it busy and good not to much hassle please could tell me if been recentl thankyou

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes and hot sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sand ,sand ,sand ,just a beautiful environment with stunning views. Got to wear good shoes cause the sand can be very hot and burn your feet. Best time is in the morning if you don't like the heat.and don't go to far if you have children  with you

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach. Would recommend to go west of the lighthouse, close to the tiny brown “hut” near the lifeguards as there are rocks on the east part. Other than that, don’t forget your shoes, the sand is burning!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So thrilling, a cool place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must if you are in Puerto Rico! The dunes are not smth you can see everyday. I would recommend to take the buss 39-90-02 if you travel from Mogan and you can walk like 10-15 minutes to the beach. Cristal clear water, dunes, simplicity and beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sand dunes. What more can one say, apart from maybe a good idea to bear in mind that it can be uncomfortable when it is windy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sahara with beers!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fascinating sand dunes desert landscape. Fine beaches often with life guards on duty. A serene contrast to the lively Playa Del Inglés scene where, however, you can have a well-deserved beer after hiking around in the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Clean Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very wavy so if it's snorkelling you're up for, you're best off going to the west of the island. It's so much fun to play in although children will need a lot of supervision. Lots of restaurants and bars near by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sands of the beach are beautiful. Sometimes when the wind is up the waves become quiet big which is great fun for body surfing. Currently the umbrellas and sun loungers have all been removed so go with that in mind that there is no shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A quiet stroll along Maspalomas Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a big shocking to see this very busy beach, usually full of people, umbrellas and bed lounges, to be quite empty.  Only few people were about and everyone walking along the beach are required to have their face masks on.  The beach was peaceful and very clean.  There were some people about either sunbathing, swimming or walking along the beach like us.  We really enjoyed our two-hours stroll along this beach and through the dunes.  A good way to have burn some calories that we have been stacking up throughout the holiday.If you are planning to walk this beach, it is highly recommended that you bring your own water.  The kiosks along the beach were all closed at the moment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Sunny, Friendly, Quiet, Safe, Stunning Location - Visit Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having spent 2 weeks at the Palace Oasis Hotel,  that besides the excellent facilities,  location, quality of the staff I wanted to comment on the impact of Covid-19.  Only 20 passengers on aircraft so a row to oneself. Levels of social distancing, at the airport,  Hoppa bus - good. The locals put us Brits to shame, the majority of all ages wearing masks including out of doors and on the beach as well.  Sadly low numbers of tourists,  and economic impact evident in the number of hotels/bars/restaurants closed. Locals are very friendly and keen to assist.  So if you want a quiet safe holiday,  set in a stunning location with expansive beach, stunning dunes and lighthouse as a backdrop,  and where isolation on return is not an issue,  then I would recommend visiting Gran Canaria.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A surreal and pleasurable trek.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sands dunes conjure up visions of being on another world, a place to leave your earthly worries behind, as well as your clothes and inhibitions if choose.  And walking naked I found exhilarating, but even those that weren’t seemed to have acclimatised to the accepting surreality that accompanies the place.  And passing wearing just a back pack and anklet people happily nodded good afternoon as if both strolling down a country lane.  Whilst fellow naturists cast a smile like you’ve both come home.  And a place for all sexualities, a public kaleidoscope of bodies and lusts, some openly entwined in the freedom and the sun.   No judgement is made of it.  Just people being people, who they really are, normally disguised in a textile world.  With no obligation to join in, nor would you be approached unless so seek by lazing provocatively and retaining the pose under gauging gazes.  But should that be your thing, enjoy love with an indulgent flavouring of hedonism, then a plentiful supply of fellow pleasure seekers with whom to share the liberating joy of the lunarscape.  We stayed a week, and was an oasis experience 😉.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great walk in those dunes and Long Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Top walk in those big large dunes in Gran Canaria, impressive place like in the Sahara. Beautiful Long Beach of 10 kms long 👍❤️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A fantastic beach with golden sand, plenty of space, dunes to explore and climb and best of all - waves!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must visit if you want to take a stroll on the beach, very different to other beaches I have visited before.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A safe and enjoyable few hours
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are impressive and and something to admire. The main 'beach' area was well populated but everyone respected social distancing. The water was warm and the beach very clean. The waves were deceptive , great for everyone but if little ones walk out be wary as some waves were unexpectedly big. The facilities are good and there are toilets available and plenty of places to eat and drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A popular if slight overstated choice geared to younger visitors
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Surrounded by the hotels of and apartments of Play Del Ingles and Maspalomas itself. This beach has as you would expect the most facilities of any beach in the area, this beach is the conventional expectation in the Gran Canarian seafront experience. You have numerous restaurants that’s presuming you aren’t based in one of the nearby hotels as well as number of outlets for water sports and entertainment. Because it’s more structured you don’t have the same feeling of density as you can get on the more natural beaches where space becomes a premium quickly. It is also more built up by its proximity to the hotels so can feel artificial but there is just enough natural beauty on view to still be interesting and worthwhile.Recommended if you want facilities over nature.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive dunes and a lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I stopped here for a short visit as part of a full day cruise ship excursion. It was fun to take in the desert scenes of the sand dunes and admire the beautiful stretch of beach. We saw a large lizard in the sand too. There were public toilets at the entrance to the beach and we thought it was well worth a stop if visiting Gran Canaria.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A long beautiful beach, situated by the dunes. Like in the desert.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A long beautiful beach, situated by the dunes. Like in the desert. Naturists can feel free here and can move freely around the entire beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One week near Faro
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is awesome. There are a couple of surf schools operating from 09.30 to 12 near the rocks almost every day. The best but most dangerous place to swim is neae the rocks. During high seas the resques swimmers stick redflags around the dangerous current area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Flat as a pancake
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like walking or cycling but don't like it being hilly this is the place for you. We go in February and the weather is always lovely. The people are friendly and nobody bothering you its just a great place to chill. Market day is Saturday and Wednesday and at the moment they are doing an upgrade to the indoor market. There is lots to do or just chill by the pool or the fantastic beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful and you feel that you are close to a desert. Touristy sellers and the stuff that is Gran Canaria, but worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best place to make cool films
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We come back to the dunes, no matter how often we’ve been here. Amazing place to be creative with your camera: we’ve taken cool photos of our shadows in yoga poses, filmed us when digging for water.... Do it, go and play!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: the best part of our stay in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From walking down the path under the Hotel Rui you get the most amazing view of the dunes and sea beyond. We loved spending time around here and walking along the coast too. There are nudist areas so don't be suprised to see a few wobbly bits here and there :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I spent a day on Maspalomas Beach. There are lots of different activities you could do there, including a day trip on a boat spotting dolphins.From this beach you could easily get to Las Palmas on the blue buses (number 30 or 50), and you could visit Aqualand or Palmitos Park if you have children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach at Maspalomas is huge and although busy there is plenty of space to find yourself a spot. On our week visit to Maspalomas we only visited the beach once and the sea was rough so the red flags were up and the lifeguards were patrolling and chasing people out of the water which is a good sign, they're obviously thinking of public safety.The water was pretty darn cold anyway, a paddle was sufficient for us.The sand dunes are huge and very difficult to climb but good fun all the same and the views of the dunes is spectacular.It's certainly worth a visit, I'd suggest a calm day though as you get sand blasted. Speaking of sand, we just escaped on the second last flight to leave before the airport was closed because of the Sahara sand storm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not as in pictures
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dunes area is really big. It’s worth visiting as it differs from other natural beauties but I have seen sand dunes before and may be that’s why I wasn’t very impressed with Maspalomas. The colour of the sand and sand itself isn’t that great as you imagine when looking at pictures on the internet or travel guides. Facilities are quite poor too. Anyway, if you haven’t experienced dunes ever - then GO!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches of maspalomas are probably the most beautiful I have ever seen miles of golden sand walk over the dunes and all you see is sand make sure you take water with you

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It has the dunes, for walking on and sliding down, and it’s a big beach. All facilities and car parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and dunes, in the evening we got great pictures of the sunset and the sea water was warm

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We sufferred the sand storm!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we were here when the now famous sand storm of 2020 hit- Boy was that an experience- never seen anything like it!Other than that, the area is nice, and the lighthouse area is good for a stroll watching the surfers or shopping/eating out.Beware the Migrants selling their wear on the beach- most are harmless when you say no- but on the walk to the lighthouse there are a number of females who grab males and try to distract you as they try to rob you of your wallett. Only saw this done to single or groups of males, and I had to be very direct to get them to back off from myself- its a con- beware (these are all over the world too I know).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beech
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beech in Maspalomas is lovely. It is spotlessly clean and really well looked after. It isn’t over looked by naff high rise hotels and feels very authentic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great sand adventure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have stayed in Ingles and enjoyed the beach and kids playing in the Sand Dunes. So long as you don’t mind coming across a few naked bodies on the beach it’s great. I really recommend the Camel Safari.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brill place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas  is just fabulous. Wonderful area, great restaurants and bars. Mainly an adult venue with brill restaurants. For a winter sun destination it’s got it all

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Winter holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to maspalomas beach and decided to walk through the dunes to playa de ingles ! We stuck to the path and had a lovely slow walk . It took us an hour an half and the views were amazing. Really could have been in the Sahara desert. The next time we went we went the other way and sat on the beach near the lighthouse which is also worth a visit . Lots of bars and lovely shops are near and the beach is lovely and clean well worth a visit .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You have to be reasonably fit to walk the dunes but you MUST visit if you can. The kids will love it. Take a picnic and walk to the sea. Some nudist activity but we only saw one man who was clearly a pervert. All the others were most discrete.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Peaceful, beautiful, amazingly high.  I don't think you are meant to walk on them, some people do, but I think they need to be protected. You can walk along the beach, or there is a path marked by posts between and at the back of them. But just walking around and between them should be fine, great experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Starting from the lighthouse there is a great walk all along the beach to Playa del Engles.It is about two miles all on sand and is very popular.It is amazing to see a constant large stream of people doing this walk every day in both directions.There is a considerable amount of nudist activity for amusement.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good place to take walk on your own
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice and calm place. Especially at the evenings. I happened to visit during windy night, you should have a jacket and perhaps a face cover in this situation, since the sand is pretty smooth and goes airborne to your face and inside your clothes easily. Take some time to empty your shoes after your walkabout :)But the scenery is picturesque, take your camera with you. Free-forming sand dunes with a sea shore. Go visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked from the beach from Maspalomas to Playa De Ingles. Walking on the sand quite tough although the views are worth it. Be warned there are parts that where there are naturists sunbathing and walking on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bare buns !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walk along the waters edge to the naturist beach to get away from the crowds, and laugh at the 'textiles' as the non nudists are called as they walk up and down for a sneak preview  (ha ha) DO NOT walk inland to the road unless you have had SAS desert survival training ! There are beach bars on the nuddy beach, but take a hand towel to put on the bar stools before you sit down (you don't know who was sitting there before you)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the Playa de Maspalomas in January this is a truly amazing experience we walked all over the dunes which was fantastic, because there were loads of private sections to stop and chill out and just take in this wonderful place.If you visit Playa Dei Ingles taking in the dunes they are awesome

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walking from Play del Ingles in the sea to a great beach warm ish water very popular but beach so long you can pick your spot, at dusk look like Sahara, itst a nudist beach so be aware if you not happy about this, otherwise great beach, but not many facilities

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very windy but nice...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well it’s famous for good waves and so its a bit windy there is a load of highend shops  but we just went to the beach and had a beer at paddy’s as i had been there berfor👍🏻

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super clean!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing, clean, beautiful beach with bars around and lovely views.Going around it's magical, be ready to take your water bottle!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice  each
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach and some great hotels in the area  but you have to look really hard to find good food or bars unless you like McDonald’s or all day English breakfasts / Bratwursts

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A desert closed to the ocean 👌🏜. Nice to visit and walk through the dunes down to the beach. Good work out also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another great visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is our third time here and yet it's still unspoilt. We love it here as its relaxing as it's so big you can get away from the crowds. Restaurants along the front, lovely clear sea water. Lifeguards along this beautiful beach.There is nudity, but most take no notice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely long beach that would never get crowded. There are lots of sun beds, only 3.5 euros for the day. Great setting, very relaxing. There are lots of good bars and restaurants close by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful nude beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We usually take a taxi to the Playa del Ingles beach and walk to Maspalomas.... as soon as the FKK beach begins, we strip nude and walk some 5 km totally naked along the water line ... taking little breaks to dive into the waves !Around kiosk number 7 is where all the gay boy are...That’s the time for a nice cold pint of lager....After that, we stop at the Strand Apotheke... for another beer and some fun with the boys.The beach and dunes are very beautiful and the sense of freedom is amazing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beaches that weren’t over busy. Had a cool spot by some music to chill to. Good range of restaurants. Enjoyed watching the surfers and paddle boarders. Had a cold swim but sea was a bit rough.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place to visit, and to take long walks around sandy beaches. Beautifully views and soft sand makes it very enjoyable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a cloudy day so prompted to leave our hotel and sunbeds and walk further than the lighthouse from our Riu Gran Canaria hotel. Didn’t realise that the beach is just up from the lighthouse. Lovely huge area to walk around and good exercise climbing sand dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but windy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice beach but quite windy. Not the best beach on Grand Canaria but interesting one which lures many tourists. From Playa del Ingles it is about 30 minutes walk. The beach is clean, water clear but still cold otherwise perfect for children, shallow water for them to play in. The chairs and umbrella can be rented. Dunes can give you some wind protection, do not be surprised when you see some nudes in the dunes. The dunes really impressive and worth to explore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Maspalomas with our toddler and it was really nice. The watter was okay, but I think there are better beaches on Gran Canaria, Amadores for example. There are many restaurants near the beach, that’s really convenient. It bothered us that the umbrellas and sunbeds can be rented only until 5 o clock and then they take them away, so you’re on your own after that. The beach is not so clean, it could be cleaner, especially if you’re paying for the sun beds. All in all, nice beach, but nothing special.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fine beach for all
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wery nice beach for swiming and having good day on the beach with family and friends. There are many shops and restaurants near the beach. You can laying on the sand or pay for chairs and umbrelas, 5 Euro for 2 chairs for a day. But i dont know how much is it on the season. Our family recomanded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go elsewhere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is ok, the sea is ok. The problem I have with the beach is that it is so windy. It's ridiculous. The sand whips up and blows in your face. Its clean, part of it is a nudist beach. I realised this when I walked up and down it.I only managed one day on the beach near the rocks for shelter. I didnt attempt to even go in the sea. It's really choppy. There is no protection from the elements here.Every day since then I have stayed by the pool as its between buildings and gets no wind.To be honest the place itself is actually pretty boring. Nothing but restaurants and shops and quite expensive really.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: December 2018
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stayed at the Afa right on the beach nice hotel allocated you with a choice of sunbeds which you had for the week so no getting up early to run out with your towel went half board food good rooms very clean staff friendly only down side we were on the main square and there was some sort of festival on the person on the Mike was very loud and it went on all day and lots of people about so if you want peaceful l would check before you go it didn't spoil my holiday there are some very good restaurants close by a little expensive but the food is of a good standard

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fab beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely sandy beach it starts at the light house in melonares with lots of high end shops and restaurants and then you walk past sand sculptures artists , bag sellers and  there are big boulders and rocks this end and then a sandy beach as far as your eyes can see you can have a massage on the beach there are a few places to eat and walk in further and there are Su beds to hire and then further still are the sand dunes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect day around!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even if we didn't swim the dunes of Maspalomas impressed us and the bars and restaurants were all very good with quality food and drinks and not so expensive!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Playa de Maspalomas on a beautiful sunny day with no wind. Walked alongside the ocean and across the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean and beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was surprisingly clean and the dunes were beautiful I only regret that the wind made it impossible for me to visit more time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 8km gold sand with sand dunes, nudist beach, gay beach with a kioszk that serves food and drinks(alcohol too).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An Unforgettable visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Skipping this beach would be a total shame, and will always be one of the top beaches I have visited in my life.The hot hot hot sun and sand, tempered with the cool waters will stick in my mind forever.  So many people, all doing their own thing, but still feeling part of the community of beach-goers.Loved grabbing a beer from the stands along the beach, sitting back and enjoying the peoples stroll by.  An absolutely memorable day.  Can't wait to go back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I never see any place like this before in my life.You visited dunes and beach at the same time!Beautiful sunset from the dunes.Not so fan from nude beach, but for a place with so many tourist maspalomas area is very clean!Just impressive!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach although its a bit of a trudge to get there over the sand dunes but once there the perfect place to chill out or meet new people

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have been travelling to Maspalomas for many years, and.have always found it excellent.Classy and expensive, with a fantastic seafront esplanade

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean clear beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Open beach, very large. Sun beds for hire. Shallow kids end for them to play. Backed by the dunes and nature reserve. Sand sculptures tend not to change, year to year. Lots of bars and shops of variable quality. Viewing platform at the faro. Apart from the African women, fewer touts this year. Sand tends to blow a bit when windy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very windy beach but plenty of space
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large, long beach very sandy. Was quite windy but Sun beds have screens to cut this down. Shopping centre near beach with many places to eat and good variety of shops.Viewing platform near light house has information on local history.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach .You must visit it. Beach is with nice sand and very clean water. Have sand sculptures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great long beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good long beach with sand dunes and lighthouse.  Lots to see.  Sand sculptures are good.  A great museum inside the lighthouse and good views.  We walked part of the sand dunes, and lots of wildlife. Also nearby are camel rides.  Had a maasage in a small salon. Was ok, nothing special .  Sand dunes are hot.  Wear trainers, not flip flops.  Good cafes, restaurants and shopping nearby, in maspalomas too.  Lots of watersports.  Nice places to swim in the sea, and shallow enough for babes and toddlers to mess about.  Soft  orange sand.  Beautiful natural lake for birds just before the beach, below the dunes.  Protected areas all over.  Love the nature.   Would go back and stay nearer to the beach .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very long beach with fine sand. Very much people. In water a few. People mostly walking around ocean to next beach. At beach is good WC for 0,60 €, also is shower and lockers for service fee. Some migrants offering fake products. Cruz Roja Espaňa have here a station. Its good also walk to EL FARO Lighthouse. Beach is also watching by local police.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Upmarket Town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very surprised with the modern, clean town, very classy with lovely buildings.  Great places to eat and a fantastic range of shops.  Lovely beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach, really clean. Sun loungers and parasols are available to rent at €2,50 per item which is good value. The only downside is there are a lot of traders trying to sell you things which can be annoying.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday Heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was on holiday with my wonderful wife and we visited Maspalomas everything was emaculate well kept and the people were extremely friendly would recommend it to everyone for a wonderful holiday but I do feel it is not for kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chilly day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked back towards playa des ingles from our walk in the dunes along the shore past the playa de maspalomas. Still managed to almost bump into a man with nothing on his bottom half even when it was quite chilly. Probably not a beach to bring your teenage children to unless you are comfortable with naturism as a family. To be fair it wasn’t much of a surprise as we had come across a few naturists on the other beaches already in areas where they might not have been expected.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rented 2 beach loungers and an umbrella for €7.50. Spent the day enjoying the sun and the water. We felt very safe and secure here. We had ample space and did not feel crowded even though there were hundreds of people enjoying the beach on a beautiful day in the fall.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's about a 4 mile walk but worth the effort. You pass through family areas into nude areas and then hay areas on this walk. Some right sights to be fair ! Some people just don't care. When you get to the other end it's cocktail time and you will have earned one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good walk to the lighthouse
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The walk along this beach to and from the lighthouse sets you up for the day. The beach is great for sun tans and water fun. If you go to Gran Canaria you should try to fit at least one day in to visit the sand dunes at the back of this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: loveley break
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Met some lovely people and had a very relaxing, care free time. Apart from the bigoted Celtic supporter.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bit of an eye opener
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with fantastic views of the mountains. Follow the kiosks along this lovely sandy beach but don't be surprised by the goings on at kiosk 4 and further down. This area is for nudists, swingers and the gay community. If u don't mind stripping diwn this is the place for u,anything goes here, however if ur a little more reserved then stay between kiosks 1 and 3,its a little more family friendly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches we’ve found with something for everyone On the left the Playa Des Ingles beach is as commercialised as we’ve seen with hundreds of sunbeds arranged with precision backed by a solid line of bars restaurants and shops and varied watersports available. Not to our taste but plenty seem to like it.Walking along the flat wide beach that soon shifts to introduce the world famous dunes and clothes start to become rarer until at kiosk 8 there is a naturist zone.Keep walking along and you’ll find the “gay beach” too then another naturist section at kiosk 4 then it changes again to return to a more conventional scene.Locals, tourists, families, couples, naturists, gays and straights all mix on the beach with seemingly great respect for each other. The vibe is never less than chilled. The surf is fun to play in and in October it was still warm enough to swim comfortably The dunes are well worth a visit rising behind the beach and a great photo opportunity. We visited them for both sunrise and sunset and were spellbound. Walking trails are marked so you won’t get too lost The beach after 4 miles or so ends at the Faro lighthouse and the new upmarket resort of Melonares which is good for another sunset opportunity and people watching

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went for day trip by car, but we had lot of trouble finding the sand dunes, as it was not very well sign posted, but the dunes were amazing..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach and dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was lovely with plenty of sun loungers which were quite cheap. The dunes are close by and absolutely gorgeous!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long sandy beach (5.5 km), excellent for long walks along the waterline. Fine weather, excellent hotel (Riu Palace Oasis) with superb food, relaxed atmosphere, top service, several pools (at least one of 25m length), big rooms, absolutely clean, small but fine fitness room etc

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches are very clean and there were plenty of sun loungers.  It is a lovely walk with plenty of amenities ie shops, bars etc.  The only downside is  people trying to sell time shares and products.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can't knock it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Thoroughly enjoying 2 weeks of lying on the gorgeous golden sands of the beaches.A couple of times the heat and lack of wind has driven me further back into the dunes for a few hours; but no great loss. ( See other dune post ).I love the gentle slope into the water - ideal for people with kids - but sometimes the waves can be big enough to reduce your attempts at "slow immersion" into one all-over drenching.  But dont worry - unless you're very small, this is not an issue.Love the touch of the beach concessionary kiosks selling anything you would expect to find in a licensed beach-front cafe.Also, the fact that you can leave your posessions on the beack, or next to a sun bed, and they will still be there when you come back.Love it; heaven.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning dunes But busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked along beach to the sand dunes, along with many other people! We managed to climb a small dune on our own and enjoyed the quietness and views of the sea and dunes beyond. We had to pass the naturist beach to the dunes, which might be a surprise for some, if not aware.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely town maspalomas  sandy beach nice 9 for Under 17  lively bars:drag shows: and nightclubs .You can book your boat trips from their .we went to see the dolphins anod markets just remember to haggle lol lovely place but quiet compared to playa de ingle. The sand dunes are must you can ride camel like in desert lol I couldn't as have bad back. Their is also palimospark,and Aqualand suitable for young and old

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit to Sand Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myself and my boyfriend visited to walk the sand dunes. Very beautiful and it is further than you think to walk it. It was very hot when we got there and it is better to go in the morning before the hottest part of the day and take water with you. There are toilets on the walk side up to the sand dunes and cost 60 cents to use pp. Be careful though walking up the promenade, we were approached by some African ladies and one grabbed my wrist and another had my boyfriend's wrist and the third was trying to get behind us to get into our bags. They slapped friendship bands on us and demanded money and asked what for as they had done anything. We have them a few euro s for the bracelets but it all happened so fast so be careful of these ladies.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely place to visit either for a long or short walk lovely beach and at one end beach bars and restaurants and cafes etc

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Third time to the island and first time to maspalomas. Beautiful scenery and people. Would recommend the camel dune ride to do on a morning when you don’t have any plans. Otherwise watching the sunset around Faro.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you're looking for a relaxing beach, this isn't the place for you. Being on the  Atlantic the sea was very cold. There were many lifeguards patrolling the beach due to the massive waves from the sea, they were stopping people going beyond waist height.The sand is very soft, few pebbles but incredibly hot, could not walk barefoot.€7.50 to rent 2 loungers and a parasol which isn't bad. However, public toilets were a long walk away and charged 50 cents.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach and promenade to wander along at a leisurely pace Lots of up market shops if you fancy some new jewellery or clothes and if hungry a great selection of goods restaurants to pick from

reviewsWithKeywords.title: a very pretty island with beautiful mountain roads
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the touristy areas cater to the elderly and gay people mainly and are nothing much to write home about. I was tired of this very soon. I then rented a car and drove into the mountains where I discovered a very different region with challenging roads, unspoiled nature (although a bit of damage from intentionally set fires was to be seen), friendly people and cosy little restaurants and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was amazing hanging out at this beach .I was here for 2 weeks .the weather and the water temperature was amazing. Sometimes me and my husband even took long walk along the coast and it’s was so nice! Also at night ...this beach is Amzing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful sandy beach & dunes.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The long sandy beach and inland extensive sand dunes just east of Maspalomas lighthouse “Faro” and running ca 3 miles to the east at Playa del Ingles are a real treat. This is the southernmost tip of the island of Gran Canaria. The sand is clean and the water very good for swimming as it shelves gradually.There is a reasonable tidal drop that means that the beach area does shrink at high tide but at low tides there is a very great deal of space for everyone. It is busy with strollers but the vast area copes easily.The beach and dune area has been well protected from over commercialisation in direct contrast to the 2 neighbouring towns at either end that are rather a large sprawl.There are occasional small huts selling drinks and there are some lifeguard spots as well as a couple of sections of beach with nude bathers.  Public buses , service 39, run close to either end and so you can easily make it a one direction walk or a there & back trek.Similarly it is easy to reach Maspalomas by bus from the Ressorts along the south of Gran Canaria and hourly from SAN Telmo bus terminus in Las Palmas, with bus Service 50.Walking over the dunes area is tiring and very hot but along the waterline is great.Highly recommended beach but just be aware this is a busy, not a secluded, place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place and absolutely stunning views.You could be on another planet, it is windy but that doesnt matter, it's a lovely but long walk between maspalomas and melonares.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OK for a quick wander
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An ok place for a quick wander along the sea front. The sand dunes look interesting. The lighthouse is a landmark which you’re not allowed up which was a shame. Glad to have been there but wouldn’t rush back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you love beach holidays then this is the place to be. Fantastic sandy beach, the sand dunes are so picturesque. Lovely shopping and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Be aware
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach but be aware towards the dunes end it becomes clothing optional shall we say was walking with my partner and 2 daughter's aged 18 and 10 and suddenly an old man walking out of sea naked 5 mins later a lady then another 5 and passed 2 men obviously had to cover wee ones eyes a bit embarrassing other than that gorgeous beach beautiful scultures and nice bars and shops

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach 10 minutes away from where we were staying, plenty of restaurants and bars in the front with lots of choice...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful clean beach and sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent many days on the beach here. Lovely and clean though the dark sand stuck to your feet and legs! Sun beds and umbrella reasonable to hire and sea cooling for a paddle though a bit rough to swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Almost a Dessert
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A desert in the middle of the island. A beautiful and gigantic beach where you can get lost among its dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: real gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: stunning place to see, great views, great for a long walk, just make sure you have a decent shoes (sand is very hot!) and lots to drink!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing to see - Well worth the visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked to the visitor centre by the Riu Hotel, there are information boards and toilets. You can then access the paths to the beach and take those amazing photos.  It was very hot and windy, the sand is burning hot and it is extremely hard work walking up and down the dunes! But you've got to do it because it is simply amazing to see.We also walked along the edge of the dunes by the sea from Playa del Ingles to Meloneras. This is a pleasant walk and gives a different perspective of the dunes, it took us about an hour but you might want to keep your eyes on the sea or sky when passing nudists :-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely must see when on gran canaria, just be careful, sand is really hot!! Stunning place,!!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible small desert - worth to see.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take your slippers, because the sand is really hot before 6 pm. You will have to pay 7 EUR for the beds and parasols - what the supervisor guy will take away at 5 pm. Ridiculous :) So does not worth to pay for them at 4:40 :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went later in the evening, the “golden hour “ to take fab photos with the lighting just right and the temperature cooler. Magnificent .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good facilities but rocky
reviewsWithKeywords.text: NIce waves, good facilities safe but rocky beach so be careful otherwise easy to get injured. They have first aid and toilets which only operate till 17.00

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good place but be careful near the dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The walk along the front next to the nature reserve and the dunes is beautiful but be warned there are several African ladies that will ask you where you are from then offer to shake your hand. DO NOT EXTEND YOUR HAND . Ignore them. They will tie a piece of string around your wrist , chant a prayer and then demand money (the string is worth about fifty cents but these women wanted 20 euros !) Then become aggressive when you refuse. Just walk on by don't even give these "soft muggers" the courteousy of a no thanks. Why the local authorities do not intervene is beyond me.The main shopping area across the street from the bus station is really nice with PROPER shops and not those tacky market stalls you see all over the Canaries. There are some nice places go eat and drink at reasonable prices and there is also a casino is that's your thing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a nice sandy beach that’s quite big/long. There’s plenty of sun beds throughout the beach but it’s best to be there early to get one. There are some stones in the water so you have to be careful. With big waves you do have to go a bit further to have cleaner water as just on the beach loose black sand mixes with water and it doesn’t look nice especially when it lands in your mouth. Nice for long walks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowdy tourist spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Typical tourist spot, head over head all day. Restaurants on the beach are aware of this and setting price high for mediocre quality at best. In the evening the main square in front of parking lot gets crowded with sunglasses dealers but they will offer you drugs instead. By their behavior I guess the man with leather belts holds the stash for other dealers. If you want calm and cozy time, head for San Agustín, Meloneras or Puerto de Mogan.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beach in Maspalomas, near the wonderful dunes. Very good and quiet for families with children or teens.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely place to visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely promenade to stroll along and good range of shops including designer shops. Beach clean and not too crammed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We loved the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I think we took the longest walk to the beach, the sand burned our feet, but the experience was amazing! And the waves were nice, the kid had so much fun, and so did we! Is a mixed beach, which was a bit weird as we had to explain the kid why some grownups were naked, but he moved on quick,  understanding is a personal choice.We will deffo return there without the kid ;)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunningSand on beach does get very hot so I would recommend wearing flip flops Sun loungers to hire for the day is €7 euros each

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked down here many times with my family. Lot’s of restaurants, good beach, friendly people. Good taxi links. Clean and well staffed everywhere. I would recommend this resort to anyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is very beautiful, if you walk alongside the shore in direction of playa de Ingles, you will find way less people there. There is long nudist area as well as gay area. You have beautiful view on dunes from the middle of the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Getting to the beach is more fun than the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While the Maspolamas beach is just ordinary imo, long one with much shallow water when entering, reaching it was great.You can reach it on foot from the most visited Playa del Ingles, which is quite ordinary, or you can park somewhere around the RIU palace hotel and walk over the dunes.The latter is much more adventurous and you'll make perfect pics along the way.The scenery when walking from the RIU hotel is like you're in Sahara or any real desert (many desert themed movies were shot here). So many dunes with the blue sea in the background make a perfect contrast.Beware, from the hotel to the beach there's at least 30 min to 60 min walk depending on your physical condition and how often you stop for pics. Dress accordingly, is burning there, put a hat, sunscreen and bring water with you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well it’s changed!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not been in years, It’s so much better than it was, high end shops high end restaurants. The front has really been done up, don’t miss a drink in maximillions on the front.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is nice and clean however when me and my wife took a walk there was lots of naked men sunbathing on the beach. I was aware that they had a section on the beach but guys standing at the waters edge hands on hips with all on show is not a very nice sight.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful dunes on the southern tip of GC
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Accessible from Playa Ingles, Meloneras and Hotel Riu Palace, it's a spectacular area of natural beauty.  You can set off from either end or in the middle.  The beach is walkable from one end to the other but it is a fair distance and is approximately 5KM from one end to the other (10KM return).  There is an area about half way that has a lot of stones and soft sand that makes walking difficult but generally, it's an easy walk.  There's something for everyone on the walk including beaches with bars/cafes and toilets

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Another grand tourist centre with loads of shops, restaurants and bars along its promenade. The beach starts from the lighthouse with its name changing to Playa del Ingles at a turn, where the FKK zone is. Combined with the marvellous dunes of golden sand in the backdrop, the beach is just spectacular with sections where you can rent sun loungers and parasols.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a very beautifull beach with fine sand. The ocean in front and the sand dunes in the back make a perfect combination. It was a nice experience

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very hot day....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Trip to see the sand dunes in 29 degrees heat. Remember to take lots of water and a big floppy hat. Maspalomas is one way a o the taxi drops you off near the Lighthouse area then you take the promenade past the Nature Reserve and the lagoon area to get to the taxi rank for your return trip. The best place to see the dunes is to the left by walking actually on the beach but it was too hot for us. The shady area near the Nature Reserve was very welcome. You will see the sand art and pebble art along the way but beware of taking photographs without any small change. One woman was very nasty and I only had notes left. The art work will have taken them hours so understandable. A good day out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Watch out the sand gets really hot! And you have to pay to use the loos ( but at least they are clean and have loo paper) the hire of sunbeds are at a reasonable price. Annoying that you have to keep telling sales/massage ladies no thank you all the time, but you get that everywhere. Overall nice beach, great views. 👍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clean beachLoads of shopsGreat foodDefo worth a visit loads to do for all.  Some beautiful buildings .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Big beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa the Maspalomas is a great beach, a lot of space and big waves, we really enjoined our days there

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have visited several beaches in the two weeks we have been here but have made three trips to this particular beach.  From the beaches we have visited this one has more waves and much more room to enjoy the sun without someone being in your space. Chair rentals are cheaper here as well but parking can be a little expensive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Scam/con
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Caribbean women along the walk to the beach conned me and my boyfriend of 10€ they was horrible and persistent and demanded money they started saying loads of spiritual rubbish and wasn’t happy with a bit of change they wanted 5 euro each. BE AWARE. I hope they get caught and fined!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dunes are not so impressive like those on Fuerteventura but stil lhave a decent desert vibe. Good for walking and wondering. Good tip to have a cash with you- bars on the beach do not accept card payments- you might dry out until you get to closest shop. Also found all beach loungers reallllllyyyy far from road so it might be a bit of challenge to get there in a full sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This area of Gran Canaria is beautiful. The lovely beach with the port and plenty of things to do in the vicinity. It's worth a day trip if you arrive by cruise ship.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to this place on a recommendation. It was well worth it. Fun to walk through and take pics. The kids did a roll down the dunes and we took a slow motion vid.We managed to get to the beach and there was a hit there selling drinks and snacks at a reasonable price. Not a place to swim though and a few nudes just wondering around.I would recommend wearing shoes as the sand is hot and bring water to drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to the beach with my children. You could hire longer and parasols - 2 loungers and 1 parasol for 7.50 euros.The beach was clean and safe to paddle on and many even ventured a lot further from the shore.We spent a few fun hours here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best Beach I have seen goes on forever ,very clean, very organized,noticed Red Cross/Police patrols,nice bars restaurants close by and not too expensive, well worth a visit..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From when I was hear a few years ago some of the beach has gone and is now full of rocks there isn't much on the sea front anymore playa de ingles has best beach front now

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic shopping
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful place!  Shops are so tempting, with latest fashions, there are so many choices...not only clothes! Cafes and bars and restaurants ! All very well kept! The beach is very long and it can be very crowded ! Dunes are something out of this place...just Wauuu!The promenade is also nice if it is not too hot! Here you spend the whole day....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Have been coming to playa de ingles for several years but have started to notice how dirty it is becoming compared to other resorts on the island,pavements are stinking all around resort and the promenade is just as bad the whole lot could do with a good power wash,there is a lot of building work going on all over resort so expect a lot of noise,yumbo center is very clean but the kasbah centre is very run down,overall with the amount of money from tourism you would expect the place to be clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great beach people seem to mix up the dune area with this smaller beach just a Melonaris a beautiful cove where relaxation is the key to the enjoyment . unfortunately over the years we have been sunbathing there it has become very popular but this wont stop us coming back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely stunning area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like shopping in quality shops and just lounging about in nice restaurants and cafes, then this is the place to come. Most of the hotels run free buses regularly to this beautiful part of Gran Canaria, and rightly so. The shopping plaza is a leisurely 10 minute walk away from the bus stop, with plenty of cafes and bars scattered along the way. This is probably a good time also to check out some of the other 4 and 5 star hotels in this area as we did, because, I’m sure you will want to return to this area, as we will, in the future.The beach is massively long, and can be very tiring in a hot day, and was absolutely jam-packed when we arrived. The dunes are well worth a look, and you will see plenty of birds in the lagoon area if you are a birdwatcher. It is extremely tiring walking along the fine sand in the dune area, but you must go there to appreciate the beauty of this place.There is also a long promenade, taking you past the shops and the lighthouse. I don’t know if you can go to the top of it though. But it’s a beautiful walk if it’s not too hot when you arrive.Must be in the top 3 areas in Gran Canaria to visit, if not number 1!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a excellent beach it goes on for milesThere are nice little coves at one end and the dunes at the other in between there is sandy beach.The sunbeds are packed close together but you can always find one and are the cheapest we have come across in are travels 7.50 Euro for two beds and an umbrella

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic and impressive dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Located between Meloneras and Playa del Ingles, against a backdrop of 10m high dunes, this 8km long 3.5km wide stretch of clean fine golden sand shelves gently into the sea for the most part. It has sunbeds and parasols for hire, showers, pay toilets and several beach bars, plus there are plenty of restaurants and shops in the two resorts at either end. There is a lifeguard and plenty of patrols. Understandably it can get very busy - popular with sun-worshippers, walkers and wind-surfers. There are two designated naturist areas (between beach bars 3 and 6). There are more hawkers here than in the main Melonares resort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tired  horrible , tacky Orange loungers ..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here for a day .Cheap beds and umbrella  but dear me .they are tatty work out and embarassing. Then a trek to find a toilet .. I asked several bars & restaurants to use theirs " no " as beaches go it's sand but facilities are shocking. Then the constant harassment of foot massage African sunglass sellers. A tired beach for a tired resort. Compare this to say Salou or even ones in Rhodes  , this is a tatty .." let's squeeze every last euro out of the gulible" beach and resort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Immaculate beach area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Huge sandy beach. Very clean. Early each morning the local council descends on it to clean and rake the beach. The only thing they seem to miss is cigarette butts. Blue flag for 20 years. Yellow sand with some black volcanic specks so it can get hot. Some areas have smooth sand going out to sea. Some have hidden volcanic outcrops hard under foot.  Plenty of beach bars. Serviced by lifeguards and the obligatory coloured flag system. Pair of loungers and umbrella €7.50 for a day.  Quite windy.  One of the best beaches I’ve been on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunbathing spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take a walk along the beach.fantastic have a swim then soak up the sun.beware a bit further along the beach towards the dunes the beach is a nudists beach.seemed to be mainly men more like Adam and Steve than Adam and eve.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: lovely beach !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice, large beach ! Smooth entry into the oceana lot of restaurants  with good food and good prices, bar on the beach, sunbeds. You'll find everything you need !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice sunbeds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I can’t give this beach more than three stars because the shore is extremely rocky, and a little roughThe beach itself was wonderful - very wide with great sandRental of an umbrella and two lounge chairs were around eight euros for the dayTons of great places to eat nearby and great people watching a very nice day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Booked this trip locally from tourito through tui the sand dunes here go on for miles we also had a camel ride quite good I felt like Lawrence of Arabia quite good fun and not that expensive

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enormous beach.What more does any child want - sun, sand, sea, waves.Great place to spend an afternoon.  Plenty of seafront restaurants.   Showers and sun loungers available.Areas further away from the lighthouse are naturist and LGBT friendly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What can I say, everything you would want from a beach! Plenty of space, shallow water for a long walk out. No pesky pebbles!The sand is extremely fine and so gets into everywhere!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: During our recent holiday we walked from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingels along the beach- we visited the refreshment huts no 1-7 along the way and also “climbed!” Several dunes then dipping our feet enroute- the beach is beautiful & clean & & was very busy with likeminded people walking along the beach- it is a worthwhile visit if your staying in the area with plenty to do with many beachside bars

reviewsWithKeywords.title: lots of space i the sun for all, nudist and textile
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we walked the beach from the lighthouse to playa des ingles the day we arrived, enjoying toes in the water as we walked. lots of people around as it was the start of the Easter weekend, Went back the next day to sample the nudist areas, lots of room here and free from the noise of someone else's children! we pitched camp between the gay area and the nudist section, lots of room, clean fine sand, and a nice breeze to keep the heat down a little.  the drinks cabins are very welcome as are the proper toilets at the gay beach.  we have been to a few places on our travels round the island that as soon as you step round the corner there are little piles of toilet paper, very sad really.back there again today so we shall see how it is again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely sand dunes and a lovely walk along to the lighthouse, some great pics taken from up in the lighthouse and some nice restaurants along the promenade. Lots of people trying to sell you things and keep going on at you and then the same ones will be back! If you like knock off sunnies and watches then that’s fine! Nice place and it’s also a protected nature reserve.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Third year I have been back to Masapolomas beach and love it even more. Bonus going later than before as sea warm enough to swim in. The dunes are as spectacular as ever and for the first time we walked all the way to Playa De Ingles which was awesome. There are a lot of people walking but there is so much room! There is a nude beach, gay beach and a large beach where families and others sunbathe. All very liberal, all very chilled and a really nice vibe. Plenty shops nearby if you want a break.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach and facilities.  Do not tackle the sand dunes in flip flops!! A must beach if visiting Gran Canaria.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WARMEST PLACE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the best place to be (weather-wise) in the island. With plenty of large hotels and private apartments to stay. Here you will find sandy beach and all facilities that is needed for a nice and relaxed holidays.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An excellent beach backing onto the dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you leave the Faro you pass a plush hotel and many restaurants and bars before you reach the open area of the beach.  There are a number of sand sculptures to extract money from the tourists. I thought the most impressive was the one of Shrek and Fiona and other characters from the films. There are also bag sellers (Tunisian?) pestering the visitors. The beach itself is very extensive and great for a swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golden sands!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Arrived by hire car at Playa de Maspalomas and parked in the under cover municipal car park (half a mile) near the bus terminal, after driving around for a while closer to the beach but not a parking space to be had. I think the car park worked out at about 1€ an hour. Approached the beach by the lighthouse (Faro - worth a visit) and then along the boardwalk past a succession of breach shops, cafes and restaurants. Looking towards Playa del Ingles across the beach you can see the beginning of the famous sand dunes. There are sun beds and shades for hire along the beach and its patrolled by lifeguards. You may need to beware of the nudist beach somewhere between the two resorts as we did come across an elderly gentleman walking along 'au naturel '.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beachtime
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Close to Playa Meloneras and has a lot of stores and restaurants close to the beach. Easy to get here with bus or taxi. It was quite windy on the beach though. The dunes start close to the beach which were funny to fool around on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved the beach, clean and vast!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great for walking and the small Wales were fun for kids and adults. Sorry we forgot the boogie board! Really peaceful, suggest you bring your own shade! Fantastic shower and feet Washing facilities and lots of nice cafes and shops and restaurants nearby. Felt very safe, kids enjoyed playing on the beach and in the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very pleasant beach and very long from Playa de maspalomas all the way to Faro de maspalomas,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you get to the beach front there's a good size shopping bizzar area and a lot of eateries opposite, you will see a lot being hundreds and hundreds of people walking South along the sand's to a very nice little new resort called Faro de, follow them, But be warned you will pass a couple of nudist beach area's, it's a good hour and 3/5 steady walk and Faro has a lot to offer, shops eateries rest areas, sand castle works of art, the beach is not as the Mediterranean, being Chrystal clear water and white sands but good to walk on, apparently it's a daily ritual from one town to another, keep fit for all, will post some pictures, well worth going to if you get the chance,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Superb sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Famous for its sand dunes and it is easy to see why. The dunes are part of an extensive beach which is very popular for beach walkers. There are some sun loungers and parasols available for hire at various spots along the beach.As well as sand dunes this area is also well known for its nudist area which is close to the area of the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lucky to be staying at the RIU Oasis so we could walk every day to the Dunes that are simply stunning. However there is a nudist bathing area you have to pass through were gentlemen of a senior age enjoy wandering around in the buff..!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: M Taylor
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth a visit but not a great experience to be honest, unless you like sand dunes.  A nature reserve is just around the corner.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view of the dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place to sit and relax at the beach as well as great views of the dunes. Also plenty of bars and restaurants. We just spent the day on the sun lounger - about €7.50 for 2 sun loungers and an umbrella if I remember correctly! Only downside not much parking nearby, we found a pay and display car park that is about 10/15 minutes walk from the beach in the end.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nomads on something like Sahara
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Here you have a smooth feeling of Africa, warm wind and a lot of space to hide. Be careful of hot sands.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long wide beach, hot sunshine even in March. Singers and umbrellas for hire. Toilets down long flight of stairs -60 cents. Nearby dunes,camels and nature reserve all worth seeing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everything you need for a relaxing holiday
