reviewsWithKeywords.text: This area is absolutely beautiful, the beaches are well maintained, plenty of security patrols to keep you and your belongings safe. The golden sand stretches for miles.The sea is a little choppy but very clean.  There's plenty of restaurants for all tastes, serving qood quality food.Plenty of activities for all ages. There's plenty of good quality hotels and apartments to stay in, to suit your holiday needs.The weather's brilliant all year round.Everyone's really friendly.100% in my opinion.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vast beach and dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Like a little bit of the Sahara, this beach sits in front of a huge area of sand dunes in front of Meloneras, Maspalomas and Playa del Ingles. You can walk all the way between Meloneras and Playa del Ingles and it's a very pleasant walk, although you will see many naturists. It's a very relaxed, anything goes kind of place.It can get windy though and with all that fine sand it can get a little unpleasant at times but this only affected a single morning of my entire holiday. The rest of the time we had clear blue skies and temperatures in the high 20s even though it was mid-March,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just back from Gran Canaria, we were staying close to the Maspalomas dunes which are definitely worth a closer look. We had absolutely fantastic weather for March with the temperatures everyday between 26°/27° and even hitting 30°. Walking across the dunes is spectacular the nearest thing to being in the desert. We even saw a couple getting married there. Well worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking in Maspalomas Beach area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking views out across the Atlantic ocean, some days the sea had plenty of waves for the surf boarders, on other days, it was fairly calm. The paved walking areas are in good repair. Lots of natural plants & grassed areas. Cafes & restaurants aplenty, along with shops, some souvenir, some more upmarket. Some hotels also along this stretch. A pleasant walk. Taxi's are reasonably priced

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is fine but walking from the lighthouse it quickly changes from families to naturists and that may not be to everyone’s taste. If the naturist element doesn’t bother you, it’s a lovely walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Over rated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Supposedly lovely vast sandy beach suitable for everyone. Actually a crowded windy sand blasted hell on earth with dangerous bathing conditions. Sit by your pool with your G & T and save the €15 rip off for faded broken uncomfortable sun beds and ripped umbrella.......miles to the nearest toilet - you can imagine the smell of urine actually makes your eyes water .....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, especially walking downFrom playa del ingles. Worth a visit. It is a long walk from the dunes to the waters edge though so bring water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge busy beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large beach with lots of people but still room for more. If you want a quiet drink worth walking past the lighthouse onto the promenade. Some good sand sculptures on the way!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wedding Anniversary Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely place,very clean lovely views over the dunes .  Great restaurants on the esplanade . Nice friendly beach bars . Great views .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went late February early March, great weather, not too crowded,but enough people to create a good atmosphere. Good food, very impressed that the restaurant staff didn’t drag you into place like some resorts.Hopped on and off the local buses found them very reasonable and efficient. Visited Morgan and Last Palmas old town, great days out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Anniversary Break
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to Gran Canaria for wedding anniversary this year. Stayed in Maspolomas. New and vibrant town. Very clean. Good soft sandy beach at Playa de Maspolomas with smaller sandy beach further up at Playa de Melonares. Good beaches with plenty of room in March. Could get packed in Summer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Massive beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has lovely clean sand and sea. The sunbeds can only be hired in twos for 7 euros so beware if you are on your own or if there are 3 of you. They will still charge you for 2 or 4. We just took towels down to lay on a nd saved our money. If you walk down towards the dunes end of the beach it can be very windy but the dunes are worth exploring. Around the headland there are naked sunbathers and also a gay beach around a small beach cafe, Because there is so much beach there is room for everyone but if you prefer not to be near the nudists, then just don't venture near the headland.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Out of this world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach, clean and peaceful.  Walking the dunes was an eye opener if you went too far in! :-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short break away
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas has a nice beach with lots of bars, restaurants and shops. However, you are hastled constantly while walking around by African men trying to sell tat or African women who corner you and attempt to tie bracelets on your wrist and then force you to give them money. It doesn't stop while you're sat in a bar or cafe either. They will walk up to your table and try and sell things to you. Even if you say no over and over again they keep coming back. I feel like this let the holiday down. It was supposed to be a nice relaxing break away but any time we went for a walk we were constantly hastled and regretted leaving our hotel. I wouldn't revisit Gran Canaria again because of this.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is beautiful and the nice restaurants overlooking the sea and a few nice designer shops near the lighthouse and taxis are so cheap

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic -  Sahara by the sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful walk through the dunes from Playa Ingles to Maspalomas. Great fun scooting down the high sand dunes then dipping your toes in the sea as you walk back. Takes about an hour each way at a steady stroll

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach and and nice day out walking down the shops and the beach , when u get past the shops the scenery completely changes and looks like a scene out of a movie

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great beach to walk and walk and walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large beach where one can sit and enjoy the ocean, the sand, the people watching without feeling crammed in

reviewsWithKeywords.title: then you're in the dessert, then you're not
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go through there, it's absolutely special. Sometimes you are surrounded by only barren dunes, in a blazing sun and it's like you're in the Sahara And next you are walking among trees & bushes and it's completely different. Only thing were the solitairy men, looking for other men... that was a bit creepy, at times...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Naturalists & The Perverts
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to looks at the famous sand dunes at Maspalomas. After reading the guide books we thought it was a must see. We went with our two boys - 7 & 9yrs old. We parked near the Santa Monica suite hotel. It’s beautiful to look out across the dunes - our kids were super excited, they ran towards the water, up and down the dunes. However, when we got close to the shore they said “Mommy some people aren’t wearing any clothes?”  I said “Ya, I think you don’t have to wear clothes on this beach.” THEY WERE TOTALLY NONPLUSSED. We are open with our kids and they don’t care about nudity NOR DO WE. I knew from the guide books there was a nudist area- I didn’t think anything of it.HOWEVER THERE IS DEFINITELY A SEEDY ELEMENT TO THIS PART OF THE BEACH. Single men walking around in various states of arousal is NOT appropriate for children. There was one man in particular that was being quite the exhibitionist. Also there were 1000s of people walking up and down the shoreline. It was like being in Oxford Circus on a Saturday. It was just not a pleasant place to go even if you went without kids. Perhaps we landed at the wrong end of the beach. More research is needed before I’d be tempted back. I am guessing the only reason you might go here is to meet other like-minded people- hey have fun- no judgement but IT’S DEFINITELY NOT SUITABLE  FOR KIDS!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sahara Dunes and Kitesurf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazing walk through sand dunes until you get to Maspalomas or Playa del Inglés (both beaches connected at walk distance).    You can take a sunbath, play paddle, enjoy drinks and cocktails or if you like watersports,  it´s the ideal place to stir up your kite and go Kitesurfing.  The kite community is very open and friendly (specialy open to tourists). You will not find a close beach with such a great space, view, sun and wind to do any activity.   After your beach day, simply walk towards the parking lot and you can find a Mc Donalds with Fast Free Internet. :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I enjoyed a lovely walk from Maspalomas along to Play Del Ingles. The beach is very clean for the amount of people using it. There is A LOT of nudists on the beach but you can still enjoy the lovely walk. If you like sunbathing nude this is the place to be! :-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice day out. The dunes are impressive and should be seen. It does get extremely busy. If you wander too far keep an open mind as the last third is nudist ( go when it’s cold for a laugh). Various places you can park apart from the pay and display car park if you don’t mind a walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Natural phenomenon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are easily accessible from maspolonas beach. The dunes are impressive and there is a beautiful lagoon to watch birds. The dunes also form part of a nudist beach. If you do not want to walk camel rides are available near by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visiting desert
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty cool place. Just magnificent how in such a small island there can be so much different environments. This place as well is just perfect for everyone who would love to make great n outstanding photos. Colours, background and view is just screaming good.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach area, long sandy beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very sandy beach, great for walking. Also with lots of places to sit and sip and watch the world go by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Depends on what you want
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked over the dunes from the Rui hotel.It can feel like a lot of effort to get to the shoreline! In the dunes you will see guys ‘lurking’ but they do seem to keep themselves to themselves I only stayed at the beach for around an hour as the wind was so strong it was blowing the sand around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand dunnes are amazing,  you can take the walk way by the rui hotel in maspalomas and walk to playa del ingles and marvel at a wonderful creation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Extreme dunes just by the sea in Maspalomas. Like a small dessert.very Nice to walk in or just to look at.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This place is a Must Do - once in your life experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have been to Playa del Ingles several times and each time we have a visit to the dunes.Chill by the beach then wander round to the Dunes area - we tend to do it "Mad Dogs & Englishmen times" - as in early afternoon !January 2019 - this visits attire involved a pair of shorts and a smile - bad idea :)The sand gets warmer the further you go into the dunes !!I was on my own so simply followed a previous explorers footprints - turns out that the tops of the dunes all meet at some point so its hard to retrace your own steps :)After about 1/2 hour of a track I found my way back to civilisation (Kiosk 4 I think it was) - a cold beer and a treck back to the main beach at Playa del Ingles and I was reunited with my wife who welcomed me with a smile and a beer from one of the numerous kiosks along the beach !The dunes are amazing - do it - but wear Flip Flops at least :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach ,well worth a visit if in the areaBeautifully clean and a safe vibe , great presence from Red Cross and life guardsThe food and drink in the huts is quite expensive however, so take your own

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular - but hard work!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach at Maspalomas seems to be a super highway for walkers along the waters edge. I have never seen so many people walking along a beach. The beach runs from the square at Playa del Ingles to Faro and Melonares. Its about two miles or so and takes about an hour - depending if you stop to take photos. There are a number of areas along the beach for loungers to sit and sunbathe but it is often quite windy. Some of the areas are designated (or at least have a preference for) Nudist areas and there is one area where there is a Gay area (no7 area) so be prepared to see naked bodies on the waters edge. If you like the idea of walking over the dunes you should be prepared for hard walking as the soft sand is difficult to walk on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Winter Sun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having been to Gran Canaria several times over the last decade, the beach at Maspalomas is one of my favourites. The wide expanse of clean sand with the dunes behind make this a go to destination. There are good facilities at the Faro end with shops and restaurants and the long walk towards Playa del ingles has beach bars located every half a kilometre. This beach is inclusive and has a large stretch where clothes are optional but you can keep your trunks on and admire the views !There are plenty of sun loungers for hire or you can rest up on the sand and watch the Atlantic waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fine beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Family place. Lots of clear sand. Clean. Loos near bye. Some shops and cafes. Life guard from Red Cross. Good.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love it here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovley views,lots of waking the kids loved it ,they is toilets just of the beach (kids where busting looked all over finally found them

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique Experience!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach is simply wonderful! It's huge and you feel like in the desert, but there's also the ocean there to swim if you wish. The sand is simply fantastic!!! A piece of Sahara in the ocean! No crowds, just piece, sun and the charming sound of the ocean waves. Might be quite windy though. :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is a world heritage site famous for its sand dunes all the way from the sahara a natural sun trap

reviewsWithKeywords.title: relaxing winter holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas is a great place to stay beautiful promenade to walk along, with plenty of cafes and restaurants to cater for most tastes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun sand sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place to walk and catch the sun as you walk , beautiful scenery, but be aware there’s loads of nakedness but that doesn’t bother me , you to let you no if you don’t like that

reviewsWithKeywords.title: wonderfull beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach and dunes of Masplaomas are both spectacular, the beach is soft golden sand. There are also beach bars along the beach for snacks and drinks, also plenty of sun beds and parasols to rent if needed or just chill out on your own towel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This popular beach behind the sand dunes is a real sand beach with plenty of fine white sand.The beach is divided into areas: for families and kids, and nudist zones.There are all sorts of sports and leisure facilities available including showers, beach bars, and restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a lovely resort.  Built purely for tourists however without the usual touristy nonsense.  Fantastic shops and restaurants.   All ages will enjoy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great shopping with some fun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most popular places for eat drink and shopping. In here must be like 50 plus bars and restaurants and many shops.there are many LGBTQ bars with great shows.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A desert visit by the sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a glorious place to visit if you are in Gran Canaria. The dunes are what you see on TV of how a desert looks. There are fantastic cafés and restaurants on the way there. And a fantastic beach which is perfectly patrolled by lifeguards.Being a high tourist location, the restaurants are a bit more expensive. The dunes are free to enter.There is a tiolet on the beach. But you have to pay to use it.There is a local medical facility for visitors to use if needed.Please remember though that part of the beach is a nudist designated beach which is on the far left facing the sea. Families and those of you like my wife and I remain to the right, nearest to the facilities and amenities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for sunbathing and walking/running. Spent many happy sunny hours there over my holiday. Always clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quiet area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely small town easy to get around by bus or taxi. Lovely walks along the promenade.  Quieter than most of the towns on the coastline but just as pretty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You must go see this!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is something that cannot be shown on pictures, you must go see it. It's amazing to see how that sand can make theese very big formations. And the sand is so smooth to walk in. We went there on a windy day, that's not the best if you want to sit in the sand and enjoy the view. Cause you'll get sand in the eyes and the mouth no matter how hard you try to avoid it, but even tho, don't skip it, go see it you will be amazed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place ! Stunning views and great beach. The dunes are cool and it will fell like a complete workout walking around there. well at the beach there are sunbeams etc you could rent... this is defo one of the places to visit in GC.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: sand dunes not for the old and in-firmed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: not for the very old, with walking problems, can be a bit scary, but very enjoyable, been many times and loved it, you can get to the dunes by walking from the light house, say about 20mins walk sand is to die for, only problem when you get wind you get sand blasted, like nude bathing this is the place for you, like any other bathing again try this place, for walking its great miles of it,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented a car and drove to Maspalomas sand dunes. Well worth both money and time! We had a fun time walking and running in the sand. Will definitely do it again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: UNAVAILABLE TO VIEW
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was lokking forward to visit this beautiful natural site, only to be frustrated with the ability to park anywhere.  The near by shopping venues were the only places we could park, and that meant a long way to walk.  After several attempts on different times of our holiday we gave up and walked it, but only saw the outskirts of it then.  We took a few photographs of the edge.   Everywhere was very packed, and was surprised the many peoples who travel over Christmas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rolling Waves of Sand and Sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Dunes and Beach of Maspalomas are a surprising sight and something not seen every day. Get lost in the dramatic sweeping dunes, walking along their crest of in the valleys between only to find before you a beautiful beach with inviting waters, even in December I was able to spend 45 minutes in the water! Key Points:1) Bring Sunblock and Water. Not a lot of shade in the area and you don't want to wait for hours in lines a the drink shacks.2) Dunes are gorgeous and fun. Have fun, try running down the dunes and jumping by the edge!3) Be careful of the rip-tide. Maspalomas beach is a place where currents intersect. On some days the riptide is enough to carry you away even if you're in knee-high water.4) Not a nude beach, specifically. But plenty of nude people. However, people are comfortable is how they do the beach there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long walks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Is nice to walk along the beach, it’s windy though so not so nice to sunbathing. Take water and snacks with you if you like to have a long walk

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful park and Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach really is for everyone! If you’ve young babies in pram or disabled/elderly in wheel chairs then follow the wooden path towards shops and cafes. If you want tomgo the nudiest parts dunes or catorgory parts of the beach go along the sand towards the dunes. The sand, sea and nature park are all beautiful, sand can obviously get hot especially dunes so take a good pair of walking foot ware that cover most or all of foot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cool place to see a natural wonder of the world. Amazing sight to see - must visit if you're in the area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not so crowded and large
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kinds really enjoyed the beach and playing in the sanddune. Among different beaches we visited (Puerto rico, Playa de mogan, Ingles) we really loved this one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice enough - busy most times and nice walks along promenade. Places to eat nice, can get varied costs. Shopping centre further along with free toilets. Toilets near main beach area 6euros and sunbed 12

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful dunes in front of the ocean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is 8 km long and you can walk to the lighthouse in 1.5 hour, the ocean on one side and gorgeous sand dunes on the other. Recharging experience!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good Sand but a lot of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Grabbing a bit of sun between Christmas and new year we were not let down. The beach with its dunes is large taking a good hour to an hour an half to walk along the coast. The sand is soft and feels good on the feet. The beach is very clean and the dunes are the most extensive on the island. There were a large number of people with pockets of nudist which are an integral part of the landscape.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very big but very crouded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach at Maspalomas is huge but it is fully carpeted with sun-loungers and parasols. I was pretty put off by that. The dunes are worth a visit if you are staying there.The good news about this beach is that it is in the Canaries and as such the days are fairly hot and you can comfortably spend time on the beach and in the water. There is nowhere else in Europe that I'm away you can do this in December. That is hard to beat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful dunes - a must visit if you are in Maspalomas!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sand dunes are beautiful in Maspalomas, makes sure you climb them if you are visiting here even if only for the day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place for photoThe Desert 🌵🐫 long sand desert beach should visit there if you like to walk in the sand and want to see a little desert in EUROPE

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun in winter
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Two weeks in Playa del Ingles/ Maspalomas in December . first impressions were mixed - lovely warm sunshine, but frequent quite strong breezes. The beach - huge and open meant that sand could get whipped up and be irritating. Made for the shelter of the dunes and the gay beach most days. Masses of people - but masses of space. The sea was always turbulent so not good for steady swimming but great fun for jumping and plunging into the waves. Think Hunstanton on a good day in English summer! A very lively resort with wide busy promenade lined with restaurants, bars and shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busier than London
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dunes are exceptional, but the whole place is mad, a constant stream of people walking. I think I expect something else from a beach. Next time we’ll go somewhere else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beaches to warm your heart and body.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sand dunes and beaches are to be visited to be believed. We also took a boat ride on a wonderful motor-cum-sail boat, called The Secret. It is run by a an enterprising woman who bought it from a German designer. It is perfect for small groups to visit various parts of the island or beyond. I love wild beaches which are accessible by boats only.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely walkable stretch of coastline
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed ourselves walking this stretch of coastline. On some parts there are a lot of pebble/rocks laying around, so that in account. Furthermore there are a lot of nudists. So that's another thing to consider.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lot of walking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a good place to visit as long as your prepared to walk .... ALOT! There are sporadic beach bars every 100 meters or so which charge silly prices so beware.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing dunes but beware
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No-one can deny the beauty of Maspalomas dunes, however it is easy to get lost or find yourself having to ascend a large dune. With all the income the local council gets from sunbed and parasol hire (7 euro 50 cent per couple per session) much could be done to mark out pathways and fence the precious environment. Also beware nudists using some dunes for strictly adult purposes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A truly unique experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is several miles long & very wide & the sand dunes provide for a truly unique experience...be careful as the waves & current can be strong! there are certain parts of the beach appropriate for families while some areas are geared for the naturists & the dunes for the sexually promiscuous...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very crowded and crashing waves.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not too crazy about this place, the beach is long. The waves crashing, tourists everywhere you look. Not my scene personally but I like more pristine places.There is an absence of public washrooms, those you do find charge .50€Many people obviously like it.We were warned not to swim by the lifeguards. Apparently a rip tide.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Buyer Beware!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Superb beach and high quality restaurants and shopping alongside a world  class beach. Excellent  tourist facilities for all budgets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are in Gran canaria it is a 100% must do to go and take in the majestic sites of the sand dunes. What a great photo opportunity for you and your family and friends....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with facilities close by
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice sandy beach with safe entry/exit to/from the sea. Plenty of nearby shops and eateries to help meet the needs of the day. Worth a visit....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clean beach views amazing walking along this beach you do get a sense of a tropical feel not to be missed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most gorgeous beach, nice eateries and supermarkets close by. Sunbeds and umbrella’s for hire and a great view. So nice 😍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of restaurants and bars but not many bars with entertainment, very little really. Lots of things to see, camel ride was brill, lighthouse, sand dunes.I will be back to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must vist place. Fantastic with the dunes and mountains as a back drop. Take a dip in the sea for a refreshing swim. Sunbeds and kiosks in intervals along the length. So vast room for everybody

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but can be very windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I always walk from the Faro lighthouse through Playa Del Ingles and onto San Augustin.  We always used to walk right next to the sea,  but in recent years we use the paved walkway at the top end of the dunes to avoid being totally sandblasted. It is still a nice walk and an unusual experience for a couple of Bits.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although it was cloudy most days when the sun did come out this place is fantastic. And if you fancy going ‘eau natural’ then there is nothing stopping you. Enjoy and let it all hang out!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking on the moon; and it’s free!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth a visit, especially near sunset when it’s cooler to walk on the sand. Can be hard work climbing the dunes but it’s great fun and children (and adults) will love the challenge. Great attraction, and the fact it’s free makes it all the better.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Touristy and overcrowded ....not to bother
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I had this town included as part of a tour and are ever so grateful we didn’t have to spend more than hour there. From windy conditions that resulted in a continuous sandstorm preventing most people from sitting on the beach to enjoy  the seaside views to aggressive vendors who offered us cheap meals in packed restaurants filled only with English speaking patrons . The menus certainly did not include any semblance of traditional Spanish food .There was an over abundance of shops that carried only beach related gear and tacky souvenirs for sale at ridiculous prices and no displays of local Spanish culture. Moving along the streets was virtually impossible without being jostled or pushed ahead so we decided to leave the area as quickly as we could. We had thought we’d like to spend a couple of extra days on our month long holiday here but so happy we are staying put in the beautiful city of Las Palmas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Poor beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gravelly sand, lots of rocks at the shore break and very busy. Be aware that there is a nature preserve behind that is used nudists, particularly men, so not idea to take the kids for a walk there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not really for families more for german nudists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here a couple of times.Windy and bit of a rip tide so not great for swimming.It makes for a great beach walk.Great if you like to be nude and bend down all the time to adust your sun bed.We even saw mums and dads nude in front of their small children, call social services!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sandy beach with a few bars and restaurants not too many lucky lucky men! We visited in the day but there's plenty to do at night . Showers provided and sun loungers available

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dunes were amazing view..there was a long path to reach the beach that is windy and mostly popular for nudists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean Sandy Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice clean sandy beach. The waves are definitely present! but not dangerously so when I was there. Nice area all round with some sand sculptures in certain areas on the beach, plenty of places to eat and shop to, and a nice promenade to walk down to ward the lighthouse

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean tidy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean and tidy beach with beach bars and portable toilets but I cant comment on whether they are clean or not as we didnt use them. Good for walking and swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is great. During our stay the ocean was a bit wild and the waves were high. We had a great time with our kids and they loved the high waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Sand Dunes outside the Sahara
reviewsWithKeywords.text: These are but a few of the many photographs taken at the time. I promise you its absolute magic to stand looking over the dunes.  My photo's do not do the place justice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach is beautiful and has lovely clear sand. You can walk for miles along the beach although be warned the only shelter from the sun is the rentable sun beds with umbrellas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing sunsets as well as sunrises
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We experienced during our holidays the most amazing sunsets as well as sunrises at Mespalomas beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked from play de ingles to maspalolmas and it was lovelyWarning though for families nudist beach just at play de inlgles and a gay nudist beach just further round also many walking along the beach so OK for adults but I found it uncomforting to see kids around that were naked whilst their parents were clothed or visit versa..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: If you like the waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow! I like the waves! Big fan here! Summer all the year! Hope i will come back again! I love this beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just spent a week in Maspalomas and spent nearly everyday on this stunning beach,very sandy with stunning dunes and very safe bathing.Also what makes this beach is the variety of people using it - families , naturists ,gays, singles just about everyone you could think of all mixing together in a very stunning surrounding - one of the best beaches i have ever been on - if not the best

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sandy beach stretching for my miles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sandy beach stretching for miles. Loads of sun beds and restaurants and bars all along the coast. Great for families but no if you prefer peace and quiet. Heads for the more secluded beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Exchange the cold days for the sun,a good time and fun !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went for a walk from our hotel and decided to cross the dunes, finally we found ourselves exactly in the middle of the nudist area !  The atmosphere around the place was so relaxing that we couldn't resist and joined the community in no time ! It's not true that there are only German oldsters hanging around there,we heard people of different ages talking different languages and we aren't Germans too,we come from Ukraine ! Getting naked gave us an incredible feeling of being part of nature ! Too bad some people don't understand that ! So,if you like strolling along Playa de Maspalomas, which is really great, but you get embarrassed seeing naked bodies, just keep your eyes down or turn them towards the ocean when you pass the nudists and keep on walking !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas deserttrip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Read a lot of reviews about it being too hot to walk on desert during the day. So i waited until 18-18.30 before i went to visit the desert..I went through the RIU palace hotel entrance and it was truly stunning to see the view from there.The sand dunes were awesome to walk on. The walk from the hotell to the beach takes about 20-25 minutes... I saw the beautiful sunset and I managed to dodge all the nudity I had read about. I only regret that i didn’t visit the earlier so I had more time to enjoy the desert in the daylight. The sun surely went down fast and it was truly awesome.... To think about. Bring scarfs to cover face and hair. It sure blows sand everywhere 😃

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On a clear day the dunes are worth a visit and walking along the dunes across to playa . This is a nature reserve and nudist sun bathing so don’t be embarrassed

reviewsWithKeywords.title: HUGE BEACH NEXT TO A LAGOON
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I travelled here with a Royal Caribbean cruise excursion, Unfortunately, the day was cloudy and the beach was a few hours from the port.  While the ride over was pleasant and we were able to see a lot of the communities on the way we felt that it was too far a distance to travel in such a short period of time and we felt rushed and not able to enjoy our time here.  The water was a bit on the cool side and the facilities were far from the drop off point.  Toilets had a fee.  If you enjoy beaches it was a truly wide and beautiful one and the wildlife in the lagoon was quite amazing.  We would not travel there in the short window provided by a cruise, though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: this is what it's all about
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our fav place to walk later in afternoon then get a coffee. Beautiful scenery and perfect beaches to walk along on the edge of the sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good place to stay if you love waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Okay, the beach is pretty good, however, I would stress mostly cons here. 1st - no toilets. 2nd - impossible to park your car ( I found free 25 minutes from). 3rd - hide waves. Well, it is definitely pros if you like waves, but if you are with a kid - I am not sure this beach is for you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes are great.. Full frontals not so great!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this beach as was staying close by in San Agustin.  The beach itself is beautiful and the dunes dramatic and great fun to scale.  Now there is the issue of nudism..  I recognised the fact that people, (mostly the Germans) may want to bare all, which is their freedom, but there seems to be NO section of Maspalomas beach where MY freedom of not wanting to be subjected to breasts, bums and willies is respected, which is unreasonable.  Personally it doesn't impress me as a health care professional, as I see those assets all the time and to be honest, some of what I saw may need urgent medical attention!!  You could  tell those who were just trying to show off what they had 🤔The beach is near several five star hotels that usually would have been on my list of places to stay, but I'm actually very glad that I didn't choose then for that reason alone.It seems to be the place to come if you want to flaunt your bits, so please beware if you are not that way inclined - I suggest you find a quiet, more family friendly  beach, of which there are a few, if you want to enjoy the sights of the sea, sand and landscape, without being subjected to body parts swaying in the wind.. I wish someone had told me before I got there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Great Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Starting from the busy Playa del Ingles it's a good 3 - 4 mile walk to Playa de Meloneras. There are quiet bits near the spectacular dunes and away from the hotels. If you walk barefoot (recommended) you will have to walk along the waterline as the dry sand is too hot to stand on for any length of time and too soft to walk on.This beach has a lot of naturism on display (and some of it not at all attractive) so you may want to think twice about coming here with children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked across the dunes an amazing experience well worth the effort and not as hard as we thought it would be

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Shoreline stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa de Maspalomas is a stunningly beautiful outlook with the white frothing and rolling waves on top of the most azure sea, to the endless sandy beach that stretches out far ahead. Of course the Maspalomas Dunas are there too. Plenty of water based activities to try. Plenty of space to lay in the sun, sunloungers & parasols for €5 a day all along the beach with some having local restaurant nearby on the promenade and along further and away from the shops and restaurants are kiosks that serve the beach goers. Naturism is normal and this has to be expected whilst on the beach, from topless to complete nudity. All very cosmopolitan

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but busy and crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Thursday 20th September and we walked from our hotel, RIU Club Hotel Gran Canaria, along the promenade we were on our way to visit the famous Dunas Maspalomas which are situated along side the beach.Maspalomas beach, with its golden & black sands, stretches for around 2 kilometres and has the famous Maspalomas Dunas at its back.There are large areas of the beach where there are rows and rows of sunbeds and umbrellas available for hire. It looked all a bit cluttered and busy.There was space along the beach where visitors can spread out the beach mats and towels, on the sand, and relax and enjoy the glorious sunshine and views of the Dunas.There are lots of restaurants and bars by the beach. We saw a bar offering sunbeds, umbrella, towels and shower for €12 a day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent a few days walking on edge of the sea plenty of space and shops close by also if like us you like walking we were informed of the nude beach area well let’s just say many were mostly men

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not the most beautiful beach I’ve been , very very crowded . Although there are plenty of eating places and bars and shops once your there . It’s not golden sand but not black either . Although the sea is beautiful and actually warm . The beach is clean , but it can be very hard to get a sunbed , which is €7.50 for two and parasol , they get taken very quickly . In saying all this , we did spend a few days there and we did have a lovely time . I think I’m used to golden sands and not so busy beaches where I usually go which is southern Spain.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with lots of bars shops and restaurants. You can walk many hundreds of metres either along the beach or on the promenade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best Asian food in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was a recommendation ,today we been here MissAsia.the food is lovely and the sushi was amazing,freshly and tasting great. Lovely recommend ,we will come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As far as beaches go this was one of my favourites. Mikes upon miles of sand and beautiful sea. Loved the sand dunes, and places to get ice creams and coffees. Great day out for all the family.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful long sandy beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: lovely smooth sandy beach with a long slope into the sea so no quick drop into the water. The beach is very long but does have kiosks along the way for a rest and a cold beer or ice cream.The people we met at kiosk 7 were very friendly and we had a lovely time on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I spent 4 days out of 14 days at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The wind was a bit extreme on one of the days. but otherwise this was a lovely sandy beach to spend some quality sun bathing time on. I went a bit further onto the beach, away from the masses, towards the nudist sections, where the crowds thin out and you can  get a fair sized bit of beach all to yourself. The water was also wonderful. Back on dry land, the area of Faro Maspalomas, around the beach has some wonderful restaurants and up-market shopping. All in all a lovely part of the resort to visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice dunes and good for families
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here and really enjoyed the beach. One of the best in Gran Canaria. The dunes are beautiful and worth a hike up and down. Deck chairs are EUR 2.50 each and umbrella EUR 2.50

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like a white sandy beach with huge dunes this is the place to go. Dotted with refreshment huts it is perfect day to do nothing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We couldn't wait to walk from our hotel to this famous beach in Gran Canaria.Our journey began on the far East where a delicious ice cream seemed mandatory.There were many bars , restaurants and shops en route towards the western part of this ca. 2 1/2 kilometre stretch of endless dunes and sand !Within minutes, we left the shops and hustle and bustle of the commercial area .The sand invited us to sit down for awhile and take in the view of the vast Atlantic ocean and the many people promenading past us. We became part of the crowd thatcelebrates this wonderful coastline.It wasn't too long before we were enticed towards a westward excursion. It began to seem endless. The occasional nudists couldn't really bother us but dehydrationwas the menace. There are a few beach huts along the way .Didn't that mineral water quench our thirst !!It had taken about 45 minutes in 33 degree temperatures , the lighthouse was now clearly visible and we knew a taxi would have to take us back to the hotel! In November , we plan on returning to this friendly island to do it all over again. When in Gran Canaria head down to Maspolomas beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, sand & Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very large beach with fine sand and an ocean that attracts you and at the same time calms you.  In the back the dunes look at you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful but beware nudists!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely plaza and boulevard with restaurants and shops. Beach is spotless and very popular however go too far and expect nudists. Didn't bother me but not to all tastes. Do the whole walk and it's about 90 mins and only 3€ taxi back. Beautiful spot!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach very clean and looked after, plenty of bars and places to eat, always feel safe here with several life guard and first aid stations

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We 2 adults and 2 kids (12 and 10) came here for the kids to play on some soft sand! There are plenty of loungers and parasols to rent which are reasonably priced.  The kids had fun jumping over the waves in the sea.  There are toilets/ showers nearby for a small charge in addition to the free shower stand on the beach.  Just behind the beach are a few shops/ bars/ restaurants.  There are a few “looky looky” women about trying to sell massages but politely walked on when we said no thank you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: lovely beach refreshing atlantic ocean waves great bars and restaurants along the beach and the beautiful lighthouse lighting your way in the evenings

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worst beach ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are hardly any facilities such as changing rooms, wcs, showers or water fountains. Only by the entrance to the beach you will find something, which is the only ones to use even if you have chairs 10minute walk away. Overcrowded. Too many waves to be able to swim and too much sand whirled in the water to bathe. For the first time in my life we left the beach after one hour. Very disappointed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach walk.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked across the dues passing the nudists some distance away.Really enjoyed sitting near the sea people watching other walkers and then walking in the waters to Playa del Ingles to get a well deserved drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overcrowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I came from the playa del ingles side so did not witness the nudist beach area but there's plenty of topless bathing.  The place is ridiculously overcrowded even mid week off season.  Bits of the beach is covered with rocks.  In the mid section plenty of shops and restaurants.  It's ok perhaps less people would've made it more pleasant

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice and near the city center
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went there with a friend a couple of times during my holiday in Gran Canaria, on the days in which we decided not to explore the island.It's a nice beach, but it's quite crowded, and when we had enough time we preferred other places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great walk it takes about 20 to walk and then we walked along the beach but!!!! It’s a nudist beach 🤣 the sand is so hot make sure you wear a full shoe not flip flops

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nature at its best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful area to walk across the sand is beautiful and shines in the sun. There are areas of natural plants with lizards darting about.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Strange Atmosphere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I walked the beach twice and found the atmosphere strange especially around nudist area. I witnessed many sights for sore eyes and felt uncomfortable walking on my own on the beach and that is from someone who has seen a lot in his 55 years of living.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas Beach 🏖 Mid section nudist
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful place. 6km of sparkly sand and lovely see (very hot sand you’ll need yo wear flip flops. Each end of the beach is family very relaxed very common for topless women with partners families etc.Mid section is nudist with a short walk and then 🏳️‍🌈 . It’s all very relaxed and comfortable and the nudist section is mainly I big further back but expect some nudism on beach and in the sea.Don’t forget your sun cream - drinks and snack at pop up bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warning - naked old men
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are a must sea. Waking across them is hard work and I’d strongly recommend trainers over flip flops or sandals. Also don’t go past 11 as the heat can get scorching! Be warned. The dunes are also a nudest beach and you will see some sights!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love maspalomas, bit of shopping, cinema, eats, amazing beach, and the sand dunes are something else

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip to beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Day trip to beach, lovely sand, take towels and don’t pay for sun beds, can buy a beach umbrella for 12 Euro’s, good cafe and shops near light house, lovely walk along promenade

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is a nice beach with sand dunes bars restaurants a really nice pleasant walk. There is a lovely shopping centre within the area of Maspalomas has lots of shops bars and restaurants also souvenir shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Upper flass
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Masapalomas whilst staying in a different resort in Gran Canaria, we took a walk in and had a bit of lunch. We walked as far as the bend between Masapalomas and Melonaras. Hotels were absolutely stunning and the beach was great too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family holiday!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myself and partner took our 4 girls here while on our family holiday only a week or so ago!! I've got to say we all had a bloody brilliant time here! The sand dunes are bloody ace and you feel like your on a mini Sahara desert we had such fun and a lot of laughs here trying to run over the sand, I will say if you are planning on going make sure you take plenty to drink, sun hats and cream as it did get very hot and also be careful walking on the sand as it does burn we all had trainers on as had been informed before going... also the shops and markets all down the front are brill, we all loved it as had a McDonald's there it was yummy :)I would recommend this place to family's, couples, friends everyone it's beautiful and so nice to be on real sand xx

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful part of gran Canaria with a large sandy beach and plenty of beach side shops,bars and eating places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a long sandy beach which goes for miles via the Dunes of Maspalomas.You have plenty of sun loungers for hire and lovely little mobile drinks/bar at the back of the beach.At the lighthouse you have some bars and cafes to choose from.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beware the lurkers!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are lovely, if a bit windy when we visited so had to combat sand storms.  Lovely to walk along the coastline, but leave your hat at home and expect to get wind swept!But I just want to issue a friendly warning, especially to people who may be with their children........I'm sure most people are aware that the dunes have nudist beaches which I don't have a problem with, each to their own.  However, we walked back from Playa del Ingles and lost our bearings a bit, and ended up between high dunes which are scattered with bushes.  I just want to warn people that there are nude men walking about in these "off piste" areas that are looking for a lot more than an all over tan!  One man was even "standing to attention" if you get my drift.  Although these people were not threatening in any way, it did make me feel vulnerable and was quite scary, even though I was with hubby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean and tidy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful golden sands, very well looked after. The amenities are clean and have a janitor on site. Plenty of restaurants and bars close by. Where the beach meets the sea it can be a little rocky but you’ll see the area were the people in the know enter. If you’re in Maspalomas it would be rude not to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was just luck we came here and so far the best beach in GC. Very wide and long with possibility to rent a umbrella(5€) and deck chair(1,5€). Also you can get draft bear at the beach for about 3€. The restaurants are near with normal prices. I was also surprised how many topless girls were around:)so very recommended for guys to visit!!;)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family visit to Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic warm sand..Beach was mostly sandy too. We all enjoyed. Facilities to shower. Difficult to find a free parking space but possible to pay for parking nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach but AVOID THE TOILETS & SHOWER BY THE SHOPS/ MEDIC BUILDING!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach here is lovely to paddle in and is quite shallow although it is rocky under foot about 20 metres out when the tide is on its way in afternoon time. There are plenty of sunbeds to rent if you wish. I don't think it was too expensive. Red Cross are in attendance close by. However, WARNING OVER THE PRIVATE TOILETS as they are supposed to be 60 cents an item but are manned by a manic aggressive who man handled my young kids and would not allow them into a toilet cubicle with my wife, demanding 3 euros which she refused. I went back to tell him not to touch my family under any circumstances or we would call police and he went for me, spat in my face and threw punches/kicked me in front of my family as someone in there tried to stop him. My kids were upset but I escaped with a bruise on my leg. Police were called and they had a word and have my name and address but not wanting any fuss, I chose not to put a report in. Red Cross guys rang them and made sure I was ok, saying that this was not the first time someone had problems so DO NOT USE THIS FACILITY PLEASE for your own wellbeing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: miles and miles of sand, beautiful beaches, the sand dunes are very impressive, walking in them you could think you were alone anywhere, the beaches are cleaned daily, the beach beds and parasols are cheap at €2:50 each per day, the beach bar/huts are all numbered but not in order, from faro end it goes no. 3 (for anyone), no. 4 (nude), no. 7 (LGBT nude)  etc, the huts serve drinks including beer, sandwiches etc

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful scenery and good waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went here with very young kids, they loved walking in the dunes as well as the long hitting waves. Would really recommend this!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice, wide and warm with fine sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best water temperature, 22 degrees, feels just fine to swim and relax.There it is always sunny, so don’t forget a high screen factor cream.Even if you stay in Las Palmas, like me, there is a bus (nr30) going every 30 minutes and it costs less than €7.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What an amazing beach in front of the famous dunes of Maspalomas. Fantastic for walk, take a bath or something enjoying a sun bath. Difficult if you go by car, so better walking or taxi - absolutely worth it !!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited masapalonas sand dunes , fantastic beach sand very very hot, some great shops and restaurants nearby if you have kids just be mindful that towards the far end it's a total nudist beach, we unfortunately we didn't see the sign and walked right into the area not good when you have children.The camels rides are not far from the dunes within walking distance definitely worth a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: FAB!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited for the day from Puerto Rico for retail therapy.Had a fantastic time absolutely beautiful.Lots of nice shops to look around went to the light house and beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach here is terrific and the sea is lovely with great big rollers that carry you in it is such fun. There are loads of restaurants along the beach and super markets so buying lunch isn't an issue  however if you can't be bothered they're are regular locals selling 'Aqua ,Fanta limon , San Miguel 'and 'water meloni cocos and Ananias.' The fruit is delicious . Also I would highly recommend having a beach massage it is by far the best massage I've ever had both back and foot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came, we saw, we got hot feet lol. We visited here because we wanted to visit the Naturist or nudist section of the beach. The beach is very clean and well serviced with bar/huts. The clothes free part starts between huts 3 and 4 when walking from the main entry point at Maspalomas and facing the sea turn left. The FKK nude beach sign is quite small and set back level with the huts, blue coloured, alternatively look for unclad bodies......Would come again, wear shoes or good flip flops, the sand temperature is quite hot!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice place. Lovely clean and tidy. Good shops. All close to the beach. Beach is beautiful. Nice places to eat

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a couple of days at maspalomas famous sand dunes and the beach, accidently walked on to the nudist part of the dunes oops. Even challenged my two teenage girls for a race up the dunes, good work out for your legs. Plenty of water sports to do there as well so your never bored. Nice restaurants we found our favourite one to go to most nights.loved it so much that will be our favourite holiday destination Yr after Yr.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach But a Soulless Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So we visited Maspalomas Beach yesterday.  Beach is great but the area is plastic.  Huge hotels, expensive over the top priced shops. No Spanish ambience or even history! One shop owner was actually very rude!The beach is like a sunbed cemetery.  So quiet no atmosphere.  No music! Nothing!We are staying in the north and close to Playa Canteras.  So different full of Spanish and life.  Reasonably priced restaurants and shops.  A couple of streets back and the flavour is here.  We travel to see the local people taste their food and learn about their culture!  Tourists are spoiling the experience of travel by demanding their own food ,  language etc.  I realise the weather is a strong reason for Northern Europeans to visit warmer climes but come and enjoy and savour the difference.😎😎

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Got the bus from Feliz 15/20 mins @€2pp!! Beautiful Beach. Has shops, cafes & bars on the beach. Kids loved it! 🌞⛱ good for building sand castles & cooling off with a swim! Lovely day out!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place want to go back nexto year .people there accommodation food sea sand views are amazing places to go are great enjoyable holiday x

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect in every way!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Superb beach! All perfect the dunes are beautiful and make a fantastic photo opportunity! Don’t hang about go!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Unusual Place of Interest
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lovely desert 🌵 like dunes next to the sea. Excellent place to sunbathe, swim, picnic or go for cool evening stroll. Great place to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Noel Cahill
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely a must see very picturesque a little Sahara desert by the sea beautiful walk in the evening if walking by day make sure to stock up on water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach but a little too windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clean beach but it was windy when we went there during the end of march and the water was cold. However, it didn't stop us going into the sea :).I'd go back there again but just at a different time of the year.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes nudity but great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to the beach at Playa de Maspalomas. We parked our hire car just off the street by Palace Rui and walked across the Dunes to the beach. When we hot near the beach chairs and umbrellas which cost €12.50 for 3 chairs and 2 umbrellas we were immediately noticing lots of naked people, predominantly older men, but also some older women and a couple of women in their 30's we decided to stay the sea was lovely the sun was shining just a couple of times older men appeared to be wanting to be "looked at" by " fiddling with their private parts"

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful clean sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was 5 minutes walking distance from our hotel, and wow is it beautiful. Stretching for several miles all the way to the dunes, it is very clean and family friendly. There are plenty of sunloungers wher they charge €2.50 each and an umbrella was also €2.50 and you had this for the day. The sand is very hot to walk on so make sure you have flip-flops or shoes. Toilets are quite close and there are a few bars situated on the beach which serve drinks and food. The sea is cool,  it not noticeable very quickly and can get windy and choppy but good. There are some areas where you can just rest a towel. There are quite a few beach sellers just say no, unless you fancy a massage! There is a nudist beach toward the dunes, and you can walk along the beach to the lighthouse but this is a couple hr walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean Beach.Nice sand and volcanic rock.People in every degree of dress from nothing to completely covered.We like to walk 3 km and then back to the Light House.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyable day. Make sure you have good walking shoes on and plenty of water it gets really hot walking over the dunes and you can be some distance away from shops

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach and nature resort. You must go in the sea. its lovely. Sunbeds are 7.50 euros for 2 people per day including umbrella.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous golden sands, no stones... beautifully clear water and plenty of beach huts offering beers, wine and spirits for about €4-5 each - can’t argue!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach is beautiful but be aware of the people!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went for the day to the beach which is lovely they have people surfing in the sea nice pubs and bars on the front its really nice. Sunbeds wasn't expensive worth a visit if you are their and the lighthouse on the beach at night is meant to be beautiful.  One thing please be aware of is the African ladies on the beach front, Me and my partner was heading towards the beach when two ladies come up to us shaking our hand seemed very friendly asking how we was, the lady then wouldn't let go of my hand and put this little cheap homemade African bracelet on my wrist. She had my hand so I couldn't go anywhere so I listened to her saying  about the beach etc next thing you know she got aggressive demanding money for this bracelet, ( the other lady doing the same to my partner) I said I didn't want the bracelet but she knotted it three times so I couldn't get it off. She still had hold of my arm so I gave her 2 euro just trying to get away quickly. She then said ' no a note' I said no she then said started asking me why I was racist and didn't like African people (I never said that, totally not true) She still wasn't letting go of me so I gave her another Euro to which she let go but walked after me shouting.. Be careful guys!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean beach.  Walked along the beach to Playa del Ingles but be warned there are naturalists on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach, good for families and couples a like.  Life guards on duty which is reassuring.  There are lots of eating places nearby and toilet facilities. A short stroll from the beach is the town which has lovely shops and restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beaches 👍
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visit the beaches from playa the ingles whit the children it was very 👍 nice we rented sun beds 👌price was good ☀️⛱

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Laid-Back !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas is ideal for those who like a more quiet atmosphere. There are plenty of activities to do within Maspalomas, ie -  Golf, restaurants, camel rides, walking, beach(some nudist), swimming and shopping. The temperature can be extremely hot occasionally and the locals are very friendly. Highly recommended for ALL types of couples.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderfull Dunnes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beatiful place. The sand there is soft, beatiful and warm. Great. Look like real desert. It's near gay beach Kiosk 7. Maspalomas Faro.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited here on our first day and couldn’t stop going back. It is so beautiful and the perfect weather. Lots to do and places to eat. Fell in love with this place!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Changing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The old strip of shops and restaurants is still there but all around us changing.Lots of building going on around, soon it will be another Melonaras.Be a new are still very good and you can get anywhere on the bus from the bus station.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's like being in a desert but with a beach, totally different. So beautiful to see as the sea is so close and you have all these dunes everywhere. Quite a site but it's a normal beach just awesome. Lovely experience and lovely to take photos. Wonders of the world. So beautiful. Yes I recommend all to see the beauty around us. Impressive. Xx

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach and dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach with impressive sand dunes. A beach to go for a long leisurely walk, or just soak up the suns rays. A great place to chill out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are very impressive and very clean as this is a designated nature reserve (certain areas are cordoned off but the vast majority is accessible) speaking with some other travellers who had been here before the dunes cover far less area than they once did.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying at the Sheraton up in the hills so a 20minutes trip away. But it was worth it as the beach extends for miles! There are some good bars there and shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach lots of space
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely place to chill, lots of bars and restaurants to suit all choices and pockets Can have a long walk along the beach to Playa del InglesOr the other direction to Meleronsa

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnifico playa in site of scientific interest
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This treasure nestled against the backdrop of a stunning area of scientific interest boasts a history which stretches back millions of years. The dunes and their magnificent flora and fauna are the habitat of wide ranging animals and wildlife spanning camels and the giant lizard of Gran Canaria. The 1,000 acres of land include the beautiful beach - explore and enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gay old time in Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Needed a break away from the English grey winter and spring weather so headed to the island of Gan Canaria for a two week stay. Staying in Play del Inglas, couple of good shopping centres with bars night clubs and restaurants and gift shops. Great place for making new friends and meeting up with friends that visit this place every year. Has a large friendly gay community with lots of gay events throughout the year, so if you’re homophobic this may not be the place to visit Never been to this island but had been to Tenerife many years ago, the islands are so different, Tenerife is a lot more lush and green where GC from our travels while there gave the impression that this island is a lot more barren than Tenerife and somewhat laid back which is great if your idea of holiday is to relax on the beach and a trip in to the old city of Maspalomas gives you the history of this island with its grand buildings and cathedral where you can overlook the harbour and the town. A further bus trip up to the newer part of the city will give you the changes of how most holiday modern cities are and there’s a fantastic beach. GC is a great place but for me it’s not one of those islands I would want to return to every year as I’m more of a city person but I would return in a few years time

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its what heaven looks like!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach is a beautiful place the sands are golden and soft also very hot !!!   To rent  sunbed on the beach costs around 4 euros each ! Depending on what part of the beach you go on the sea bed i sandy  ( some of it is pebbly ). The first 2 blocks of sunbeds are family then its more adults  but still ok then it gets into the nudist area  so if you easily shocked or have young kids or teenage boys who may shall we say need a dip in the sea to calm down !!!   Same as the sand dunes dont let the kids go exploring. In there !!!   It is a fantastic place i love it its like another world there sometimes you see no1. Other times you may meet a fellow explorer but he may be or she maybe naked !!!!And sometimes other stuff go,s on. So definitely. Not for the younger explorers  !!  But if you older go have a wee peek !!!! One other thing there are no toilets on the beach just pick a bush boys. And girls. And watch out for the lizards they bite and love worms !!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun in the Sun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic place to soak up some serious rays, the beach and dunes are kept immaculately clean. There are numerous beach bars along the whole stretch of shoreline from Playa del Ingles to Maspalomas. For the more adventurous there is plenty of fun in the sun to be found in the dunes 👌😂

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place, beautiful beach! Very friendly Visit the lighthouse the area is amazing amazing restaurants

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vamos a la' playa
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sand, ocean and sun is everything what i need.quiet and clean beach ist perfect for my vacation.i recommended this amazing place, i may is not to much hot.Fast pack your staf and vamos a la' playa:))

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful long beach. Good for surfing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely long beach set amongst the backdrop of the amazing dunes. So long it doesn’t look overcrowded. Large parts are nudist areas. This is the only beach of all that we have seen on the island that is not protected by some kind of inlet/ rocks and so had the biggest waves. The area has a lot of trade merchants selling fake bags etc. Not our thing. There were a few sand sculptures too - very impressive. Give a couple of euro and take a few pictures of how it generally works. Seems only fair to appreciate their hard work. Felt safe with local Police patrols and huge life guard presence but there were a few signs warning of pick-pockets/ thrives. The sea was a bit too choppy for us to feel comfortable to let our kids go in.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beach with something for all
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely go here if you're in Gran Canaria and staying near the area. It's a lovely beach surrounded by the most spectacular dunes. There are plenty of places to get something to eat or drink, and sunbeds to rent if you want them. If not, you can just sit on the sand or on a towel - that's what we did. We liked how the beaches in Gran Canaria have rinsing stations at the edge so that you can get rid of all the sand between your toes! When we were there, there was a sand artist making a giant sculpture with lots of animals. There's also a lovely little lake just a few hundred yards from the beach which is home to a variety of wildlife. We really enjoyed Maspalomas - you could spend an entire day here, or just a few hours. It's got something for everyone - you can take a long walk along the beach, or stay put with the kids. You can watch the birds, or watch the local sand artists creating designs. You can bring a lunch or sit in one of the cafes and have some food and a drink. You can hike the dunes, or paddle in the sea. Or you can do all of the above. Recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Busy at weekends but stretches for miles so always a space to be found. Great sand, shallow beach to the water so feels quite safe. Options to hire sunbeds etc and a collection of small bars, shops at the lighthouse end. Really nice to walk along the sand and overall a fabulous beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not for the faint hearted
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although staying in playa del ingles, we caught a bus to maspalomas after hearing the walk back across the dunes was incredible.It certainly was, although some of the sights were more so.The place is beautiful, like something out if the Sahara desert. Massive dunes running down to the sea, inhabited by countless nudists. It took just over an hour to walk slowly back to civilisation and the dunes and beaches are amazing. Hundreds of other people do the same walk in both direction.  The sand is fine, the beaches are for the most part pebble free, with small refreshment kiosks scattered along the beach. The waves are gentle and warm.Beautiful place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing and breezy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s actually quite cloudy during early May so not the best place to get a proper tan but it’s nice and relaxing. Lots of restaurants and bars around the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the Best Beaches in the World
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa de Maspalomas is one of the best beaches in the world I have been to. When you are in Gran Canaria, it's somewhere you need to visit. Whether you are a family with children, solo traveler, prefer to sunbathe in the nude, or are gay, there is a portion of the beach for you. Make sure to take note of those around you to make sure you're at the part of the beach you are looking for. Each section has a snack and drink stand, and there are plenty of chairs and umbrellas for you to rent for a minimal price. The beach is surrounded by incredible sand dunes and waves crashing to give an unbeatable experience. It's somewhere I can't wait to go back to, and somewhere you will be happy to spend a day or week.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ferie
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always  wisit this wonderful place dunas maspalomas gran canaria spain wnen i am on my vacaion here its very lovely there nice to walk in the sand

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Have visited here a few times now and always love to return. Beautiful beaches and plenty of good bars and restaurants.Definitely make another return trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MUST VISIT HERE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: when in grand canaria make the visit to maspalomas its a great place to see and the sand dunes make this place feel like you are in desert . my girlfriend and i enjoyed walking around here for a day very much amd would definitley return

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A town fully build with hotels. In the evening very quiet but at night very busy with young people going out

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved it , clean tidy , plenty shops around , nothing is overly priced   Plenty bars to have a cocktail too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is clean and there's a very nice private sunbed food and drinks area if you don't like sitting on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Desert feeling in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are amazing, but beware of the sand: It can be so hot that it burns your feet. You can cool them in the Atlantic ocean which is close by...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ladies brightly dressed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Watch out for the ladies brightly dressed harrassing people on the promenade. Very touristy area plenty of shops etc

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely walks along the waterfront
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked over the sand dunes a couple of times,TOUGH going! Be careful, sand is very hot, if you go over could easily twist your ankle! However well worth it when you get to the waterfront, can walk for miles, be aware many nudists flaunting their bits along the whole stretch. Only pain in the backside are touts trying to sell you rubbish constantly up in the shopping area, up from the beachfront. They are a NUSCIANCE and should be BANNED! They are constantly harassing you and can be rude and aggressive!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just so beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We've been visiting maspalomas for 24 years now and could never tire of it. Beautiful place will be here again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: amazing place must see by your self lots ammilities around magnificent view long beach we highly recommended

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must be seen!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is well worth walking all the way to the mirador at the end of the walk-way and then following the path across the magnificent dunes; then walk back to Playa del Ingles along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
