reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really enjoyed the sand dunes. Clean and tidy beach. Children had fun. Near the central bus stops and seafront shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Many naked people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is amazing and the kids loves to play in the dunes. But I was surprised that there was so many naked (complete naked men) at the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Provides new views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very short walk from the well-organized beach life. If it's a hot sunny day, it's best to wear some kind of shoes, the sand will get around noon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing to look at. Worth the walk from the centre of the resort. We would have liked a bar or at least a toilet near to the far end we got a bit lost and came down next to the Riu hotel so had a long walk to the main bars etc on the front

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautify, windy, sandy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. During our visit there it was very windy. Walking distance from the parking place to the beach is long we even got sunburned on the way. Liked the small English pub nearby (don't remember the name): good beer and nice view on the Ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Winter Sun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great value 5 star hotel with excellent food and comfortable sun beds. Spotless clean with friendly helpful staff. Good spa with great therapists. Nice walk from hotel to shops, bars, cafes and restaurants. 15 minutes if you go out the front door and 25 mins if you walk along the promenade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice walk. You'll get sand in your shoes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice wiew. Real sand. However you will get sand in your shoes. The sea is a bit inaccessable. Best to walk on the pavement aliong the coastline

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach with a dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has free parking and starts with some dunes. There are some hotels, apartments and restaurants literally at the beach, so you don’t need to walk so far to get what you need.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great and sunny place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach and nice wheather . If you dont have sun in Las Canteras just one hour trip by bus nr 30 will take you there and you will get some sunbath and enjoy the ocean .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely playa
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have been there few times  in June 2017... it was quite busy but everyone can find their own spot, lovely sand and dunes, adults could swim but kids not really as waves far too big..showers available...quite difficult to park close to the beach so walk if possible(free parking) some nice restaurants in walking distance not so expensive or you can buy some refreshments on the beach..enjoy;)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven on earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a free bus taking us to this beach. Has been a couple of times while on holiday. Really enjoyed the place. Had a nice walk on the beach, a swim and a bit of sunbathing. Really enjoyable day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take Your shoes of and walk bare-footed! Sand is so soft! Afternoon it's quite warm... You can see very small tracks on sand, they are made by small, black beetle!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing little beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Weather was glorious for march, considering it is 2c in England.There are plenty of restaurants and excursions along the beach.The dunes are worth a visit as there  is a mini microclimate in that area and you would think you were in the Sahara desert. Very very busy so if you don't like crowds then maybe try Las Palmas instead.Definitely coming back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beutiful sand dunes and beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a MUST when in Maspalomas or in the area. Walk by the sea from Maspalomea to Playa del Ingles, or go through the dunes. A very, very nice walk, both of them. Be home if it is windy! Be prepared to see a lot of naked people on your way. It is a paradise for nudists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really amazing views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If your visiting Gran Canaria, you really need to make sure you visit! This was one of the most memorable parts of our trip - such amazing views and an unique experience that you won't forget. It is though, a very tiring walk up and down the sand dunes, so prepare for the long walking and muscle strength needed to get up and down the steeper areas! You can walk where ever you like, but to see the best views you need to be at the top of the sand dunes!It can also get quite windy - you'll find your clothes full of sand at the end of the trip, but everything is so worth it. You'll need an hour least to visit here and take in all the sights.I would advise to be careful and abrupt when walking to the beach - there are quite a few foreign 'sales' people who seem a little dodgy, and try taking money off you for making you a bracelet which they basically force and tie onto your arm - we fell for this and they were demaning 5 euros for a piece of thread.Also, beware that this is a nude beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches (has nude sections for starlight and gays)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is one of the most comfortable and beautiful ones around. There are sand dunes stretching in every direction that lead to the beach. Nearby boardwalk, restaurants and entertainment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love going to this beach when we visit Gran Canaria,  always plenty of people watching to do!  We were lucky as we had a fabulous week of sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really nice beach, lots of space. If you prefer beds and umbrellas or just your own towel. Few bars and restaurants, also minimarket. Stunning views, dunes walking distance, maybe not very comfortable for swimming when low tie, but otherwise superb!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice indeed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed the beaches and services around the beaches. Be careful of wandering on to nudist beaches by accident. We felt very safe during our entire visit and will return.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beach of grandeur
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golden sand for miles. A real treat. The lifeguards are efficient which is good as today there was an undertow. The dunes backdrop is dramatic and the nearby shops and bars provide a solution for those times you want to de-beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Second year here still good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are  looking for fresh air and lots of sand this is the place for you. Even in March very busy but sea cold however with spectacular dunes and miles of beach to walk its worth a visit. Only negatives are the lack of toilets  along the beach and  annoying people selling you stuff as you head on from Masapolomas end. Stay away from African woman trying to shake hands and force bracelets on you. Kiosks for drinks and snacks along the beach, life guards and loungers for hire. Nude section and gay section for sunbathing a long way down the beach but ad in most of the Canary islands sunbathers wear or don't wear what they want. All casual and cool. Away from the beach good shops towards the lighthouse end and lots of places to eat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, sea, sand and dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach from Faro to Playa des Ingles. Can be quite windy. Lovely soft sand and the dunes are worth climbing - hard work though. Several beach bars offering cheap drinks and snacks, but very limited seating. Large nudist area near Maspalomas. It's a good walk, can easily take a couple of hours. Plenty of places to eat and drink at either end.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beach is a beach. It is what it is! But expect the following. It was very busy when we visited in March. Mainly people walking between the two resorts. There is a nudist section and a gay section. Going underfoot was difficult at times due to quite lengthy stretches of stones and pebbles. The dunes are very interesting although quite difficult to walk across due to the softness of the sand. The whole area is much larger than you might think from the map so allow plenty of time to walk from one end to the other.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand, sand and sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Interesting to see this miniature desert and if you're health, it's a nice long walk between Maspalomas and Playa del ingles. If you want the easy (but boring) version, do the board walk from Pdi and go through all the shops and restaurants all to the end and have sundering to eat or drink while watching the dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Interesting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would recommend a visit to this beach and especially the sand dunes. It is really quite an amazing sight. We went in February and it was lovely walking barefoot in the soft warm sand, up and down the dunes. There is also a nudist area around there but we did not venture that far!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach & amazing sand dunes. You can walk all the way around to  Playa del Ingles if you don’t mind joining the hoards of other people doing the same thing & going past the nudist beaches ;)Golden sand all the way & plenty of space to sunbathe if you like your privacy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great clean nudist beach. Bit of a trek across the dunes but worth it when you get there. Bar and sunbeds available

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place for a walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Area around the lighthouse is best position for shopping walking and of course the dunesPlenty to see and do and taxis cheap to go further afield

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Extensive sand dunes by Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Day out to the beach at Maspalomas. Very hot. Supposed to be camels to ride but didn't see any. Commercialised area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing dunes. It would make you to feel like you are in Sahara desert. Hope for a sunny day and warm breeze for agreat picture.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and well worth the visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth the walk but be careful to avert your eyes when you get to the section which is nudist. Bars along the way to buy refreshments if needed. Lifeguards strategically placed and sun beds for rent should you need them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well looked after and dramatic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Protected area which was lovely to walk along. Big enough to offer privacy if you wanted to spend some time relaxing here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A "must see" in Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: During a two-week holiday in Gran Canaria, my wife and I decided to take a hike along Maspalomas beach and then return to Meloneras through the sand dunes. Parking was a bit of a nightmare and it took us a long time to find a vacant space, which we eventually did in the Av. del Oasis in Meloneras. It was a windy, overcast day but we decided to walk the entire length of the beach around Punta de Maspalomas and saw numerous wind-kiters taking advantage of the windy conditions. We then headed inland over the sand dunes.a "must see" if you are in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love the dunes!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can not not visit the dunes if you’re coming to the south of Gran Canaria. Absolutely beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely little beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great few hours at the beach. Very clean and tidy. Plenty of little cafes/restaurants on the beach for easy access to food and drink. Beds at a price but we used our towels.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Proceed with caution
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach. When the weather is right the water is lovely for the kids to paddle in. Can get choppy and is used frequently by surfers. A word of warning, stray to far up the beach past the little shops and cafes and it becomes a naturist beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stay by the sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are really nice but im seeing a lot of litter the deeper into the dunes you go. Its fairly clean by the seafront but by the golf course in the middle its getting pretty gross as winds take litter in. Its not the fault of anybody who lives here but all tourists must start taking their stuff with them! Lovely on the huge dunes in the sun by the sea.... perfect for naked bathing. Beach huts sell drinks and snacks. By the sea front you wont see much litter. It is literally (pun intented) at the back bit where Most people dare not venture. Im not saying its all bad or giving it a bad review, i love it! Take your litter home to your hotel to bin if you visit!!! Thats all.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes walkabout
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can’t go to maspalomas without a visit to the sand dunes and a walk along the beach to playa del ingles takingin the sights and scenery around you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing area with a unique beach and to my knowledge creates a unique beach in the world. It is such a huge area so you won’t miss it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand dunes and more
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas sand dunes , beach , Faro lighthouse and the pond ! A great way to spend time in the sun , lots of restaurants line the edge of the beach , wooden walkway winds from the lighthouse to the pond , the beach is awesome , what’s not to like !The pond is a bird sanctuary as such in middle of beach where herons flamingos waterbirds stop off bring your camera if your a wildlife lover

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas Princess Hotel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I am currently staying at this hotel and to say im dissapointed is an understatement.    I have been all around the world abd never came accross what i have witnessed here.We paid alot of money for half board for one week with the family. When booking they failed to tell us drinks are not included not even water! You are not allowed to bring a drink from the bar. You are not allowed to bring a bottle of water with you. The staff follow the children to make sure they are not getting drinks. The staff stare and hover over your table to make sure you have no drinks.You have to pay for literally everything even wifi and its only available in the reception area. Its very bad value and would not recommend this hotel its a complete rip off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nothing negative to say about this place. Beautiful. This is our 4th visit and we will be back.plenty to do and close to other resorts. It helps to have a car if you don't mind driving and I would defo recommend one as there are some lovely surrounding resorts. The mountains are good to explore too and have little villages etc. Getting to the highest point on the island is a bit scary but the road is good and the views are spectacular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely sunny beach. The waves are not to rough for young children. The beach is easy to access with a pram. The area is nice with a good selection of shops, resturaunts and pubs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for children
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Recently visited this beach. It’s nice & flat with golden sand. Great for children wanting to build a few sandcastlesThe area near to the water was a little rocky..but the water was so cold we didn’t bother paddling.Lifeguards were visible.Lots of bars restaurants around the beach for a snack or a meal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: good beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: lovely seafront walk plenty of bars and shops and restaurants whatever the weather worth going to there was a few touts around

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love this playa. Walking on the dunes is great. You can walk for a few kilometers without seeing any buildings and listening only to the sea and the wind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspolmas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely area Nice walk along the water frontPlenty of bars and restaurants at the end of the walk so you can sit and relax and watch the world go by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I travelled to several beaches during my time on Gran Canaria and this one was the cleanest and best by far. Not too crowded, all the amenities you need and I particularly enjoyed the watermelon/coconut/cocktail seller regularly announcing his products were 'fresh fresh fresh fresh'.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lovely beach that was quite clean. It was very windy when we went so you couldn’t really swim but we enjoyed watching the surfers and playing in the sand. Lots of options for food, drinks and ice cream on the beach front. Shame you have to pay for the toilets and all the ATMs were out of use. We enjoyed our days there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, can be windy and if it is don't bother . Cost 7.50 euros for the day to hire umbrella and beds, nice beach bars for a drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited in January. Meaning not to crowded. Temp was maximum 21 °C which was pretty warm besides two days there was remnants  of a storm. Sand dunes and beach gives you a feeling of dessert and coast. Visit in off-season period.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The dunes are a must to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a bit of a sandstorm when we went but worth seeing. Beach lovely and clean.  Shops and bars very touristy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A Hollywood desert  with more sand than the real thing.Amazing to see so many people walking along the sands not that there was anything else to do.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely town to visit, relax and eat. Lots of things to do and see including the sand dunes and some fabulous restaurants

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand Dunes at their best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You do not have to go to the Sahara to experience sand dunes. These are just as good. They are great fun to explore and definitely worth a visit. Avoid on a windy day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loads of sand.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's sand dunes. I don't know what I was expecting. It's cool if you're really into sand.But on the brighter side, there's a nudist beach and that can be fun. Also the sea is fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely walking along the promenade
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful area, especially walking along the promenade.Many cafes  bars and restaurants to choose from.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing and very windy.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When we visit this place it was very windy making it almost impossible to walk in the dunes.We tried twice and the second time we made an effort in covering our face.It was very impressing to see how the sand moved around in the wind.It was also funny to see all the other people  trying to walk in the dunes.Be prepared to get sand everywhere and have fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A fantastic clean beach, fun waves to jump in, clean, lot of space. We loved our morning walk/ run on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic when the crowds have gone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A really interesting natural landscape surrounded by the worst of tourist developments but still worth a visit. We parked near Meloneras and walked along the promenade past some very high end hotels and shops to reach the dunes which are a natural wilderness. The shore has a few areas of restricted “ public beach” with patrolled sun loungers but these don’t detract from the experience too much especially if you go in the morning or at night. Watching the sun set over the dunes is an amazing sight.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A windy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On this long beach it is nice to take long walks and admire the dunes on one side and the ocean on your other side. It is often windy there but brings breezes in the summer and it's not cold in winter.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: stunning views and weather
reviewsWithKeywords.text: unspoilt , amazing weather and views.grab a beer on the beach from  many a kiosk.plenty of people around to say its january.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand dunes of Maspalomas is absolutely breathtaking! Spent a few hours playing in the sand and the view was just great! Be aware though, sand will get slap you from all sides if it’s windy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning dunes and beaches, gorgeous to have a walk along and sit at the many cafes and watch the world go by. Unfortunately too many Africans trying to sell bracelets, sunglasses and actually approaching people in bars and restraints who are eating or drinking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No the most Family Friendly Beach But Really Good for Nudiest/singles/couples?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very good walk around this beach,  I think is a great beach but not for young kids as waters are a bit of a problem , also you got strong winds and sand storms, also is a lot of nudist which  I  don't have a problem when is only for nudist.  you have to be on alert at all times in this beach, a lot of scammers and been a nudist mix beach a lot of perverts, again not the nudist people but others.recomend this beach but not with under age.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Christmas Day 2017
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing sand dunes which have to be seen to be believed. Very windy so sandd blows alot. Washing areas to clean sandy feet and toes are plentiful. Suggest taking a small hand towel to dry feet afterwards. Lots of food choices in the cafés and restaurants. Recommend a visit to the Chinese section where staff are polite and efficient. Poor advertising resulted in one cafe charging more for beer than expected. Suggest using the cafe toilets as you have to pay to use public toilets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand sand everywhere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just walked from Maspalomas to playa del ingles and back again It’s like a mini Sahara desert Amassing. If you like walking this is for you. Keep in mind there is a large area of nudist beach so look the other way you will be offended the majority are 80 plus old men. Joking aside, great walk

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stayed in a Dunas Maspalomas Bungalows. very nice, the Beach was a good 20 minute walk but well worth it, i went down there everyday. But there is also a shuttle bus that went down to beach 3 times a day. few bars and cafes here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoyable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean, lots of Bars and Restaurants, Good Shopping and fantastic beaches,, Good bus links to rest of the island

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but can be breezy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice sandy beach right next to the dunes Maspalomas, plenty shops bars and restaurants and even a few snack huts on the beach. Just be aware can get quite windy even when sunny.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic place and incredible dune experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I will never forget the maspalomas dunes.Unbelievable experience, with wide view all over.Some services all along the beach, to eat and drink snake, the red cross and police car are always going up and down for safety. 2 fkk areas, and many fkk in the dunes. The sea is quite cold in January, but I did it. Good spot for kite.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely place to visit with the high end Melanores one end or Playa del ingles the other if you prefer more bars and clubs

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful, the water and waves are awesome. Nice breeze keeps you cool.The sun lounger rental company needs to ensure they clean up after lazy guests. Cigarette butts and plastics need picked up. One woman I was next to stood on sharp item and cut sole of foot.The public toilets, that charge €0.60 to use, are disgusting. Have no toilet seat, no proper flush, no proper hand wash/dry facility. Need urgent modernisation. Only charging 0.60 as they have a monopoly and when you need to go you need to go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An unusual place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to visit the dunes here, and was amazed we spent so long there. Feels like you’re in the Sahara desert, yet your never more than 1000 metres from civilisation. Well worth a look, with or without children

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Me and my husband were here the week before christmas lovely place with shops bars and restaurants. The sand dunes are a must to see

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Faro de Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa de Maspalomas is perfect not only for the sand-Playa-lovers, but also to use as a promenade for peopel who like long distance walks. In the morning by sunrise and in the evening there are also lot of peopel who do their daily jog. The Playa from Faro to Playa del Ingles and back offers a nice jogg possibility with its. appr. 7-8 km.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand and beeches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Maspalomas beeches are so big that there are room for everyody. You will be able to find a spot of your "own". For me, it was fantastic just to go in the sand and look at the waves, the sky and the ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Sahara with a beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand dunes here are just amazing. It's exactly like the Sahara Desert. I believe there are camel rides here too. This is also the location for several Hollywood movies which were set in the Sahara. The best thing is that there are shops and hotels close by!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved my visit to Playa de Maspalomas. Nice boardwalk along the dunes make it easy to walk along the dunes without having to walk in the sand. Well worth a visit. Should be obvious, but just in case: Be mindful that this is sand, so if windy, the walk will be less pleasant.Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunningly beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely breathtaking and spectacular view, during the windy day you actually can see the dramatic changes of the landscape. Stay away when there’s sand storms. We had the one day of mid harsh wind and walking on the dunes plus against the wind ? Oh my gosh that’s the hardest thing to do...but don’t you worry I am well and still in one piece ha ha haWe mostly spend our day on the kiosk 7 as convenient to get a pint of beer or cold drink or even light lunch plus there is cube box toilet you can use (€0.50) but the only downside is the smell and it closed by 1500 and the lady who work there constantly on the phone and arguing but worsening is she actually sit inside the male side and I find it uneasyTake and drink plenty’s of water whilst you are on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a cool and beautiful place! The sand dunes never end. Although, watch out walking here during a windy day : sand everywhere!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best for winter
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So windy and so cold water. Rocky ground when you enter the sea. We had maybe around 10m/S in wind. Could not keep my eles opned cause sand blew all over. And sittning in a chair was 7,5 euro... expensive and not worth it. Try get another beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but too much waves for small children
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach but too much waves for small children. Clean and lots of space to play on. A good beach, go there once at least

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great sandy beach and clear rock free swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On a good day without wind the beach in front of the Dunes at Maspalomas is fabulous.  The only downside is the wind which sometimes becomes intolerable whipping the sand which blows into everything. Often the current here is also very strong and the red flag is up, which means the lifeguards will endeavour to keep you out of the water. We usually find that if there is a red flag here then if we ask them what the situation is at Playa del Ingles beach, the answer is generally that it is much calmer and on a yellow flag meaning that you can go in the water.  Playa del Ingles beach is a 20 minute walk along the shore.  On a good calm day, I would challenge anyone to find a better beach, at any time there is always rock free clear water with waves ranging from flat to vigorous. Well worth a try.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach but windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the sand dunes and the restaurants around the beach but it's windy .Tried to go twice and had to leave because if the wind other then that a lovely beach to walk along and climb the sand dunes and take cool pictures

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beware
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not much too do you have to get a cab to nightlife;; hotels are ok dont stay in Sonneland nothing there the people are fine be better if you are English to stay in playa de inglis or peuto Rico very windy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, nice shops
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa de Maspalomas is the closet beach to our hotel ( Sheraton Salobre) and there is a shuttle between the hotel and the Sheraton Beach Club, is which is about 20 meters from the beach.The beach is small but pristine and well kept. It’s also a short walk to the restaurants and shops. The lighthouse is also worth a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: ​Dunes de Maspalomas Nov. 2017Great place to walk into the nature and admire the breathtaking dunes.Recommended also to visit at Sunset.Nice beach and swimming place. (part of the beach is a nudist beach)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This a a huge stretch of sand. At first you see a high density of sunloungers, but it gets more spaced out as you walk along the beach towards Playa del Ingles. The sand is very soft, and unless you are along the shoreline on the hard sand, its not an easy walk. Further along the beach you will pass the nudist area. The wind can pick up sometimes and it picks up the fine sand and blows it about. There are lifeguards.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great vistas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good for long walks. Water's pretty chilly for swimming. The views are great.  However, prefer Plays Las Cantares any day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tons of Nudes and no boardwalk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is a typical beach BUT with tons of nudes as a nude beach is part of the beach and there is no way to avoid it if you plan to walk the entire beach. As I did walk the entire 5km beach, I wish there was a boardwalk so I would not have to walk on uneven sand. My back is still in pain many days later and will not get better without professional care. So, in all, I would not walk this beach again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach and sand dunes. Very popular walk which can be difficult at high tide where space to walk on hard sand is reduced.  Just remember there are large areas of nudists and gays sections here, so not for everyone.  I didn’t mind as so relaxed, but don’t know if I would be comfortable taking young children to this area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great walk along the seaside. Very relaxed. A jump into the ocean is a must. Take some water as there is limited opportunity to buy some.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must visit beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach. Amazing dunes. A huge expanse and wildlife protected space with a lagoon . Take plenty of water with you if exploring the dunes. Quite mountainous in places. There are little kiosks doted along the seafront for refreshment. This is also a naturist area so expect to turn the corner and see some wobbly bits. Sea can be quite rough here if you fancy a dip to cool off so be careful if you not a good swimmer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Endless dunes, freedom of nudity and clean water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Refreshingly, the nudist mingle amongst the dressed swimmers and no-one cares! Access is free and a few bars offering refreshments, planted directly on the beach, where the dunes descent to the Atlantic Ocean, provide a few stools to take breath for those who choose to walk between the lighthouse and the far end of the beach in Maspalomas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great dunes and fab beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can feel yourself like in a desert walking there. You can even sunbath in the middle of sanddunes if you do not like seafront. Beach itself is very clean and organized, shallow and suitable for kids also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place to visit because of perfect views. The dunes are huge. Sand is fine to walk. Near the dunes are restourantes and small shops. Easy to find this place. Where is car parking places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the beach every day of our 1 week holiday. It was clean with lots of lovely bars on the beachfront and a beautiful promenade that was buggy friendly. The ocean was freezing but the kids didn't seem to mind!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quaint
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Free bus from our hotel took us here. Quiet area with a small shopping and eating complex. Found a bar called Paddys Irish bar ran by a couple who were friendly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lot of people but beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach and dunes are beautiful. You can walk there up and down or just take sunbathe. Lovely place! For everyone who like beach and sand. :) But the beachfront was crowded. There were so many people walking along the beach!!!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hard to find a better beach with its mix of quiet areas and busier spots with sun-beds and snack bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a walk along here during a day trip that we took to Maspalomas, but not too far, we didn't venture as far along as the dunes! For those that don't know what I mean by that, just be aware that the 'sand dunes' is a nudist area!  We found that the boardwalk along the top part of the beach made for easy walking.A beautiful and warm day when we visited, a nice sandy beach, very busy with people, and a pleasant area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Inreresting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a nice beach. Town is very touristy but if that’s your thing it’s great. Lots there.  The sand dunes are worth visiting. Look spectacular but are a bit of a tough walk. We tried to avoid the nudist section but they were everywhere. So be aware if you’re going there. You’ll see everything. :p

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You must visit the dunes if you’re in this area but be aware that you will probably encounter nudists within the dunes and obviously many in the nudist part if the beach. The walk across the dunes to the beach is a bit of a slog but worth the effort. The sand can get very hot so choose some suitable footwear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand Sand Sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A real oasis great for pics long shadows and blue sky !!!!Worth a visit any time of year but October Sunsets are not to be missed !!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Evening meal
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved the beach bars resturants and the shops were good. This is a modern area with vast shopping and resturants. We throughly enjoyed our time at the beach especially on our last day to going for a evening meal. The  19th hole resturant we recommend as they have evening entertainment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beaches and plenty of eateries/shops.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really enjoyed visiting here, it has plenty of places to eat/drink and shop in. The beaches are really nice, and soft sand clean warm sea water. There are  lots of lucky lucky men about but they don’t really bother you, just say no thank you and they leave you alone. Loved the sand dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great sand..   pick your section
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing sand and dunes. There is a bit of beach for everyone and anything goes on some sections. Maspalomas loves everyone and that is part of its charm. Family at the town end, then nudist, then all male with posing.. not sure what came after that. Big waves so not toddler suitable . Dunes fun for medium sized kids. Camel ride quite fun but go early as probably pretty hot in the middle of the day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow & omg
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ummm maspalomas well what can I say it's certainly a eye opener, Town is very geared towards holiday makers party goers nudists & the pride community. great shopping, The sand Dunes are simply breath taking picturesque and just WOW,  But please be aware if taking kids/teenagers or your just a prude this maybe not your ideal destination to go to as the beach is full of nudists my poor kids were desperate to see the dunes but spent the whole time tutting and snap chatting naked men parading themselves  in disbelief for their friends back home to see, altho just along the beach which is golden and beautiful there  is a lovely non nudist beach which you can enjoy relax and sunbath

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing sand dunes and beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The desert is amazing. We got there around 12:00 noon and was able to walk on it. I think the cool breeze from the ocean helps keep it cool. Though i should point out that some sides of the dunes are much hot compared to the rest as it the slopes that don't get the breezeDefinitely recommend a visit as the beach is amazing fine sand and good waves for surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really long beach with more naked people than I prefer to see in one day. Fabulous for a walk along. Very busy in places. Very busy walking but lots of space to lay out a beach towel and sunbathe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: super surfing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a stroll or family playtime or watch the surfers and parasurfers - enjoy the sand and surf (no lifegurds on parts of the beach). Walk further and you will neter the nudist area of course. Still open to the clothed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Views from Hills
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is conveniently located to most of Playa Del Ingles and Maspalomas. There are great views of the beach and the dunes from afar and make for brilliant photos. Sunsets are beautiful too. The beach is generally always clean apart from lazy holidaymakers leaving rubbish, but is generally always busy even in autumn/winter. This is the driest and sunniest part of Gran Canaria and a lot of the Canary Islands, so its a great place to visit for a good tan. Normally always a nice gentle breeze as well to cool you down whilst you bake in the Canarian Sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa de Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach with lots of variation. If you keep to the far side of the city close to las arenas there are large waves great for surfing, in the middle you have rocks so it's more suitable for strolling and on the other side you have the tourist strip with a large sand dune and lots of shops, restaurants and calmer sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: These dunes are amazing, a moon like spread of sand that must be ever changing.  Great for kids to climb and play on in areas not designated reserves.  Great to walk from them to the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best beach on the island! Possibility to hire chairs. Nice restaurants in the area. Very good! Spent there most of the days.             Will go again!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach shops cafes all within waking distance . Sun beds sand dunes . Waves . Sellers on beach selling massage ice lollies .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Villain0
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is a great place for the more adult naturist visitors but never the less very relaxing and beautiful beach area

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with clean salty water and lovely temperatures. Nice shops nearby. Massages and refreshments offered on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes are great fun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great time with my two kids playing on the dunes. It’s like a small piece of the Sahara desert. The dunes appear to go on forever.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The  Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach if you don’t mind walk a  distant to the water also it’s a nude beach  and a bit windy at time. Great view from the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dune walks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Maspalomas for the day whilst staying in nearby Puerto Rico.Famous for it dunes which I suppose you have to see if you are here visiting rather than staying in the resort. Its much flatter than the more volcanic parts of the island (apart from the dunes of course) and you will find the streets are clean, easy to navigate, lots of choice of shops and food.You will also find open green spaces and parks, golf courses even an open air amphitheatre.If you are considering staying here, you will find most of the hotel and high rise style accommodation around the town area, but closer to the sea you are more likely to find yourself in a bungalow style building set out nicely in little “village” complexes.Scout the beach out first, find out where you want to be as there are 3 areas to it, gay, nude and beach-ware. It doesn’t  look particularly strictly enforced so you can make your own choice. Good for a day, worth looking around but to be honest we prefer Puerto Rico.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are amazing. Take plenty of water although there are kiosks selling drinks, at a price ! Lots of people promonading up and down the full length of the beach all the time. Beach divided into textiles, nudist and gay but all enjoy freedom of movement. Very windy on our 2nd visit with sand being blown along the beach and sea rough. Settled down later in the day but we felt we had been effectively exfoliated.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We made two visits to the beach whilst staying here on holiday. In the morning the sea was right out so the beach was long and wide and not too busy, we had a short walk up to the sand dunes that were difficult to walk on but the views were amazing. The second time we went in the afternoon; the sea was in so the beach was considerably smaller and it was very busy. The nudist area isn't quite as secluded as a I'd like it to be as they literally walk out in front of you as you are walking along the beach. The beach is very clean and obviously well maintained. There isn't a lot to do or see when walking along the beach but there are quite a few bars and restaurants that are set up away from the beach. Would recommend a visit just to see the sand dunes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not much to it.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Playa de Maspalomas are sand dunes leading to the sea. There are beaches, one for families, one naked and one gay, each quite a distance away from each other. But to get to each one you have to walk over proper sand dunes. Distances don’t look too bad when you set off, but it’s very deceptive. Be prepared for a hike and remember you’ll have to hike back after a day in the sun! Gran Canaria could make a lot more of this area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent place we loved it and will certainly be back . Easy to get around . Good range of shops and excellent restaurants . Taxi service good, reliable and economical.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, very well maintained. Don’t think I saw any litter at all. It’s obviously a very popular beach but if you wander up towards to dunes you can get a little privacy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is clean, plenty of room, loads of loungers, and plenty of sand. Sea.seems to be safe, a bit rocky when tide is out,  Very busy on hot days. Didn't see any nudist so cannot comment. But worth a visit, A gental stroll from were the coach drops you off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good in the 'family' areas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed the beach nearer to the resort, less so in the more distant areas where anything seems to go ... The sea can be rough being the Atlantic, it was quite warm in comparison with the Med in June. The beach shelves quite steeply in places, and there are strong currents, so take special care with children or weak swimmers!Enjoy !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely sand dunes .not keen on the nudist beach .Lots of designer shops and restaurants. Nice walk along the front .Lots of people asking you to go places .wanting money and begging .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of places to see including the two large shopping centres. Beach is lovely but very busy. Great choice of bars and restaurants to suit your hunger!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches anywhere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The combination of the miles of golden sand curving round the edge of the Maspalomas Dunes in my opinion make this a unique beach for such an accessible location.The sea swell and currents can be strong so not great for small children or inexperienced swimmers.Very relaxed nudist friendly beaches  also.This was my 3rd visit and I will definitely be returning for a 4th.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the bus to Maspalomas beach, the bus stops by the nature reserve. If you walk towards the beach there are shops and restaurants you can then turn left for the Dunes or right for a great walk along a boulevard about 8km long to Playa Melonares (Millionaires Beach) Great safe beach with sunbeds and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely clean beach.  Not too crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very nice,  clean beach which isn't overcrowded.  The sea was nice and warm in late September temperatures of 30 degrees plus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see, there weren’t many naked people and the other kind. so it was suitable for a family trip?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very busy and hard to find parking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just not what we look for on a holiday. We like to sight see and this beach is just full of people, bars and restaurants. Would be a nice beach in the evening I am sure.The dunes nearby were much better.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited twice on our holiday, lovely beach and sand dunes are worth a stroll, make sure you have plenty of water though. Beware African ladies on the way to the beach trying to bully people in to buying bracelets. Avoid eye contact and ignore there selling tactics such as "excuse me and where are you from" and avoid shaking hands with them or you will be wearing an over priced unwanted bracelet.  Sunbeds available on the beach and plenty of sellers as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach. Something for everyone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were based at the molenaros side of this wonderful beach.It is sort of split into sections as you walk from the light house.First part is mainly just topless or full costume. This is served by  kiosk no. 3The next part is more or less separated by the lifeguard station. This is mainly heterosexual full nudist. Can be quite busy around kiosk no.4 and the sun beds, but plenty of space for shy folk on the sand or further back in the dunes where stone circles are available to provide a small degree of privacy.Next is the gay beach, with mainly nude men as far as I could tell.Well worth a visit to either nudist beach if you are a veteran or a novice. All are naked so no one bats an eyelid....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favourite beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This has become our favourite beach in Gran Canaria. Loads of restaurants and cafes along the beach. You can hire two beds and a parasol for 7.50 euros. Parking nearby is a nightmare.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: lovely clean place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved maspalomas, very clean place, nice friendly people, beautiful beech, great shopping and some great restaurants and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy Busy Busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very busy part of Gran Canaria, with a beautiful beech and plenty of shops.  Plenty to do for all the family.  Many different shopping Malls and a great market.Some of the area has sadly bars and shops that have closed down, but the main part is very busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely beautiful Beech an views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very clean plenty of bars an eateries On the beachWith superb views of the sand dunes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely setting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa de maspalomas is a beautiful town with fantastic beach and excellent surroundings not too many shops and bars very peaceful and clean. A must to visit while in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see dunes and great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see if you are in Gran Canaria! Start from Faro Maspalomas side, have a good coffee in the restaurant and head to the dunes! (we took Bus 30 from Las Palmas SAnta Catalina for 7 euros). The dunes are huge - wear comfortable sandals (the sand gets super hot in afternoon) and prepare for some exercise! Lots of people just walk the shoer, but try to climb the dunes, too! Very nice view! The beach is very long and you can walk from Faro Maspalomas to Playa Ingles. The water is clean, nice, long waves, good surfing sports, too. Be aware that there are a few nudist (FKK) beaches and some nudists walk all the way along the shore completely naked. Playa Ingles gets super crowded in afternoon, but Faro Maspalomas side is not so crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful place miles of sand dunes, so peaceful, and tranquil. You need to take plenty to drink as you can walk for miles. The coastline is also beautiful, well worth the walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes as far as the eye can see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must visit here when in Maspalomas. The beach is a blue flag beach and it is evident that it is looked after by staff patrolling, clearing up anything that sunbathers have left.Bare in mind when entering the sea closer to the lighthouse it is very rocky so go further along the beach with the lighthouse behind you and there's less rocks.The dunes can easily be walked along if you've got good footing and it's lovely to see the view when climbing some of the larger ones. Great at sunset!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to the beach but it was very windy and sea was choppy but still beautiful and had a nice lunch and saw loads of lizards !!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vacation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful long beach with fine sand, a perfect place to enjoy a relaxing vacation at sea. The area close to the light house is full of bars and restaurants and there is a shopping area close by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Harrison
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand piles are a must along with the shops and restaurants. The night sky's are also a must and take a boat trip you will not be disappointed. Have fun when you go

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach is quite a spectacle with its beautiful sand dunes. Be careful though as the sand can get very hot and actually burn the bottom of your feet. One problem with the beach is it can be quite windy at times. If you don’t mind been sandblasted then it’s great. On a calm day you can spend many hours here. There are life guards and drink kiosk scattered around. Get yourselves there it’s beautiful. If you have little ones then be warned that there are nudist on these beaches. Enjoy. Nick R. Leeds. West Yorkshire

reviewsWithKeywords.title: the biggest beach I saw in my life
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The biggest beach I saw and really pretty. There was so plenty of space to relax. This beach was very sandy, clean with water which wasn't so cold like I expected. Great place to get the tan, for walk , to sunbathe naked for activity. I can recommend this beach for everyone,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Okey beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beach it self was fine, several restaurants & bars around.the only down side was - several nudist around and as we were there with our 3 year old, it didn't fell too comfy for us.  but you'd see them in every beach..If you happen to be around the area i'd more likely recommend puerto rico or playa da mogan beach, they seemed slightly nicer :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Over rated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Supposedly lovely vast sandy beach suitable for everyone. Actually a crowded windy sand blasted hell on earth with dangerous bathing conditions. Sit by your pool with your G & T and save the €15 Euro rip off for faded broken sun bed and umbrella.......miles to the nearest toilet - you can imagine what else you have to put up with.....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hot hot hot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We only managed one trip to the beach this year as it was absolutely roasting. We travelled July 25th - August 8th.There was quite a long walk from the promenade to the actual sun beds which would have melted the skin from your feet, the sand was like lava and there were no wooden board walkways to stand on to help. We had a toddler and a buggy so was even worse. Our 15 year old was there to help. Thank goodness.Once finally on the beds it was glorious. But again the walk to the sea was roasting. Once on the damp sand it was fine but it put our teenager off even trying for a dip in the sea.There were drinks/snacks units nearby (if you could bare it) or the usual men selling refreshments. I imagine this beach would be glorious in the cooler months.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a lovely beach.  Bars and restaurants pretty much on the beach or if you fancy being a bit more adventurous you can go for a walk on the sand dunes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy or peaceful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great for morning walks, miles and miles of walking. I like to have a break away from the crowds and sit watching the waves. No clock watching just simple relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family fun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is lovely goes on for miles. Sand dunes are fantastic great to see. Nudist beach was entertaining 'dangly' bits everywhere

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Happy holidays
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying for 2 weeks at Princess Bungalows, Maspalomas and cannot but say that it was great, very friendly with great facilities, clean and well maintained in a lovely garden setting. There are 2 large swimming pools, an excellent restaurant and friendly pool-side bar, the accommodation was spacious and spotless and the rooms were cleaned bi-daily. A free bus took us to the beach where we found the naturist beach we like and if we wanted to return later that the last bus, taxis are so cheap. It was quiet and relaxed which was for us perfect. Going again we might stay in somewhere less geared to the English but we were not often at the complex for long but visiting other places and beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, amazing dunes but don't look too closely at couples you may come across!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful with plenty of room for everyone and the dunes are just stunning. We walked up from the beach to the top of one of the dunes to take some photos. When we turned around to look back at the sea, there was a naked couple behind us, very openly having sex on the beach........and I'm not referring to the cocktail! There are lots of restaurants nearby and plenty of sunbeds/parasols for hire at a reasonable price.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great walk along the beach from maspolomas to playa del ingles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we did this walk along the beach took about 45 minutes you can climb the sand dunes if you feel energetic mind you don't get lost.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vast beach area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you're looking for a beach to spend the day, or more, this is the place to be. It's big, it's clean and if you do not mind nudist in your vicinity, it is a must.We didn't see any parking lot, but there are plenty of parking opportunities in the area. Food and drink can be purchased in the surrounding area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes in maspalomas are beautiful,if you want to really relax and spend a few hours on your own in perfect silence this is the place to go, and then pop in to one of the bars or restaurants near by.  Have a lovely holiday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Decent day out...beautiful ...resort is very good...lots of places to eat a decent meal...or have a quiet drink

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is truly enormous, lovely and clean.  Regular beach bars along its course.   Nudist accepted but not compulsory approx half way along the beach.  Watersport's and family beach further to the east.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely setting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular scenery from the backdrop of the sand dunes. Be warned though that the walk from Meloneras to Playa del Ingles takes you past both the gay and nudist beaches and as they are walking amongst you without any clothes on you cannot miss it and those with children may to to avoid it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: one word
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning.I felt like I was in Egypt and the beach section is like 2 mins away. Amazing place to take pictures ,not hard to climb up and I show people roll down for fun. The sand is soft and comfortable.I will recommend to go explore it .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Camel rides
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really good fun. Getting on and off was a little hairy but very relaxing walking through the dunes. They take a photo which you can buy. The beach itself is lovely, but be ready for quite a long walk from the bus stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Sand Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very impressive sand dunes stretching for miles.Well worth a visit but very hard to walk in especially if one is getting in on years.Enjoyed our afternoon visit there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: good beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: good beach and a real eye opener, naked people everywhere, be careful walking through the sand dunes as you'll probably find naked guys playing with themselves,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Huge space. Amazing sands and dunes something for everyone. Families. Nudest. Couples. Very relaxed environment. Nudist and none nudist all mixed in but works. No one worries or cares.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Windy but a Must See !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: a nice beach, the usual beds for hire and a few shops and bars at the back of the beach.  Very stony in parts (in the sea, not the beach!) so bring shoes.  Blowy too - we left feeling like we were covered in sand.  The dunes appear to be in parts, fairly spread out - it has a family area nearest the promenade, the middle section is for nudists and the end section farthest from the promenade and hotels etc is the gay section.  Stunning views of the dunes which are really a sight to see !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice mini desert and lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very long beach with nice sand and big waves. Behind it you have the desert. If you want to take a stroll, make sure to be prepared, since the and will get on the shoes, but the sand is very hot for bare feet. It's a must see if you are in Maspalomas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see and do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy review. It's a mini desert next to the ocean and a must see. The sand is hot "derrr" so wear decent trainers or sandals. We got the bus to he nearby shopping centre. 10 min walk

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes of Maspalomas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the beach on our second day here, the dunes are absolutely stunning, we walked for what seemed to be miles and never got fed up of the spectacular views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very well kept
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very well kept. Not so crowded, but probably just because August is a low season period for this island. You can reach easily the lighthouse area by taxi and then walk down the beach from there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very pretty!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We really liked it here!! So beautiful! Really good restaurants too! Was great watching the sun go down over the water and watching crabs do their thing! We even saw a big lizard!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Interesting beach but not exceptional. The sand is very fine and because of the winds and salty air your skin can get irritated. The water is not clear because of it and most often are a lot of waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible Vista
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No trip to Gran Canaria would be complete without a visit to these remarkable dunes. The view across them is quite stunning and whilst a walk across them can be quite strenuous, it's certainly an experience. The mixture of sands combine to give a unique colour. Relax and enjoy the sun or have a drink or meal in one of the many outlets. How long you stay is dependant on what you want to do, but they are certainly worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very beautiful and quiet location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a few minutes walk away from the hustle and bustle of the resort or busy beach front you can enjoy the peace and quiet of this area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We only visited for a short time but the sand dunes are worth looking at.  The beach is lovely but be aware that once out so far it becomes very rocky.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We travelled as a couple to playa del ingles and went to the beach everyday. It was beautiful and so relaxing. €7.00 for 2 sunbeds and an umbrella which we thought was reasonable. Sunbeds very comfortable and reliable and in a nice location. Bar in the cabin on the beach is quite dear so would recommend going to the nearby shop. McDonald's very close to the beach as well as lots of Spanish restaurants and bars. There was a section of the beach where people were completely nude further down, didn't bother us but for those who may. Overall it made the holiday and was the main attraction for us (top tip: wear suitable footwear as sand burns your feet!)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Basic Elements in One Lovely Stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Many Europeans visit the Maspalomas dunes, a slice of Saharan sand on the south of Gran Canaria. Indeed, these great shifting mounds need limited recommendation, they whisper their own glories. But it is worth mentioning that, in certain circumstances, this protected natural area provides great family or individual peace and even spiritual uplifting. This is not to belittle the perils of heading off into the dunes under a scorching sun or sandstorm. That would be foolish, by anyone's estimation. But in the late afternoon and darkening dusk, this area assumes an unrivaled majesty. My children's easliest memories as wee kids include venturing into the dunes to a point where they could only see golden sand and blue sky and hear the distant Atlantic as its tide beckoned. So, at 630 in the evening, stroll into the dunes with your children and let them roll and tumble into the sand. It is an unforgettable experience which I dare say can feed our human souls. Don't go until the penumbra but enjoy the evening as it gently descends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Interesting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomas beach has something for everyone. The whole area is an amazing feat of nature. Be aware that it covers a huge area so have sensible footwear & lots of water with you. It has naturist & gay areas so if you are a bit sensitive to any of that then research before you go. It amazes me how many on here are 'surprised' to find themselves in these areas. One word of caution. There are useful showers at the town end of the beach. The wooden slats are VERY slippy. My feet went out from under me and I landed very heavily. Sadly people avoided me like I was a leper. I managed to get myself going again after a few minutes. Disappointing but that's people for you!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovley place would defo go back the seafront was brilliant clean tidy an no lucky lucky men mitherin you the time

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand,sand,and sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Early start to venture over the desert dunesGreat to get back to natureWhen we visited, several parts were mentioned as "naturist"I will admit, it was great to walk round in my "birthday suit " !The three of us made a pact not to take photos!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sahara desert ?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking dunes...can feel like in the middle of the Sahara desert.Best to have a stroll there is early morning...sand is not so hot and you can walk barefoot.I would recommend to continue a walk along the coast to Faro de Masplomas...Watch out! Dunes are full of nudes ;-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The lighthouse beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's magical around this area. Beautiful sand. Nice restaurants. Various prices. Great holiday atmosphere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand Storms on Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dunes are nice to look at - but stay away from the two beaches connected by the Dunes - particularly when it is windy.It was like a sand storm and you get sand blasted - seriously.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspolomas sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: These are breathtaking views and not to be missed.The sand is to hot to be walked on barefoot, make sure you have footwear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand dunes are beautiful to see, you can't believe you are not in a desert!We went for a stroll on them but had to come back to the walkway quickly as the sand was VERY ot the further you went. Worth a stroll down the walk way where there are lots of shops and bars before you get ther.We were advised not to go over the dunes as this is supposedly were the nudest beach ect is.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take a selfie stick you won't be out of shot with these amazing dunes and none ending beachfront loads of space's to sun bathing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We Loved This beach ! The best on the whole trip through gran canaria ! The big Waves & the mini desert so cool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's sand. Just that.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: And lots and lots of sand. Sand so hot that you can't wear open toed shoes to walk on it. Save your time for something more rewarding. Unless you have a thing for sand or foot blisters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous place and lots of beautiful views, sea is not that cold, plenty of walking on the sand dunes which are absolutely beautiful. Food is gorgeous at most places

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach and dunes brilliant very hot and windy but great place with wonderful hotels. Some parts are nudist but place is great loved it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely sandy beach with nice little beach bars serving ice cold beer. Nothing much to add except to go further along the beach towards the dunes to avoid the rocks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Dunes!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is one of the places you must see while in Maspalomas.  The best way to walk this beach, as the sand does get so very hot and can burn your feet, is to get down to the waters edge and wander along.  Be aware that there are sections on the beach and you will soon come across the nudist area.  The dunes seem to go on for ever but a good few miles and it was great fun to walk in the waves of the cool and refreshing Atlantic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A trip to Maspalomas would not be complete without a visit to the famous dunes. There are four zones of sun beds so do check these out. There is a family zone and a naturist zone amongst these. A fee is payable for the beds and umbrellas. The beach is lovely and the dunes provide for some exploring. There are kiosks along the beach for refreshments.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in island.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the bus 39 from Puerto Rico which cost 2.75€ per person and took us 20 to 30 min to arrive. Great location with loads of luxury resorts and shops, just 10 min walk from bus station and you are already in between sand dunes and great beach. Water was warmer than other beaches so far and much cleaner but bigger and stronger waves. Between 4 beaches in island which I have been Maspalomas is my favourite.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great dunes walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy to navigate the dunes from the beach at playa del Ingles to maspalomas beach and resort.Takes about an hour. At the end of the medium difficulty walk you reach a really nice beach with a kiosk for drinks...and then you can walk the beach to the resort which has well established shops and restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well maintained walk along the beach. Some good bars and restaurants to be found here. Ignore the street sales people as they are not pushy and only want to make a living. Nothing wrong with that. Can recommend for a alternative place to walk instead of the Playa des Ingles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand dunes and nudist beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hot sand in places and it burns so watch out - that's mainly near the dunes - basically big mounds of sand to climb up . Not exactly the desert but similar . Lots of nudists walking around on the beach . What can I say ? You won't miss them . Lots of shops and restaurants around . Buses available Good day out

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love It!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So beautiful everywhere. I would recommend to put on your walking shoes as the sand is so hot, you'll struggle to walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great large beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean, large and popular beach. Nice to spend the day with friends and family. Not crowded and the best in the whole Island. Better on weekdays.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Have spent many hours on this beach.A very big expanse of fine golden sand,and huge sand dunes edged by a azure blue sea and sky with a mountainous backdrop.A very mixed place to spend some time first clothed then nudist the far end of the beach before it turns the corner is predominantly gay.Along the beach are small kiosks selling soft/alcoholic drinks and food.You can rent daily sun loungers and parasols.The nudist beach is by far the best I have used,very clean and rubbish bins all the way along the beach. The whole beach is raked and cleaned through the night.If you don't intend to rent a lounger it's worth investing in a parasol from the shops near-by about 6 euros and lashings of sun screen,it gets incredibly hot the sand  is unbearable to walk on.The sea can get a little rough and the current can be strong,but very clear and warm to swim.The beach is patrolled by the local police,red cross and has look out life guards. I feel very safe using this beach. Saturday and Sunday it can get quite busy with many of the islanders using it too. Too  the rear of the dunes is a scrubby vast area it has many grasses and tamarisk trees growing,and many lizards scuttling about, it is a nice walk through to Playa del Ingles.Coming off of the beach there are showers (free)and foot/leg washers the sand is very fine and sticks like glue.A fantastic day out to chill in the gran canarian sunshine and to get a lovely tan.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach lovely and clean not much activity in the area.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A big shopping centre called yumbo, bars in the town & eating places, but we were all inclusive so only got drinks while we where out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful view and quality walk around the sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked along to Playa de Maspalomas one evening from our hotel in Playa de Ingles. Lovely clean beach with views right across over the sand dunes. Plenty of things to do in the area whether it be activities on the beach, wandering around the shops or eating in the restaurants. I imagine the sand would get hot around midday and always worth watching where you stand as it can be quite rocky!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday 10 days.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Briillent  stayed rui place hotel 4 star. Could not fault it . A very beatitfu location , hotel grounds and  facilities great. Tip use taxies they are cheap . Hire cars waste of money and  load of grief risk accidents.  I would go back with my family 12 yr old  boy and wife.A lot of good shopping  go to the market on Monday or Wednesday.  Will be going back again .Ps if you are looking for traditional Spanish fish an chips all day breakfast.  This is not the place for you. Steve.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Clean Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clean beach compared to playa del inglesOnly niggle be careful i ran in and nearly broke my ankle as was big rocks under water.we moved up a bit more and was much better.Very Very hot so apply sun cream regular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice walk around the Dunes.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good place for a walk, just be aware that the sand can get very hot mid day onwards.  Worth a visit if you are in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sample of the Sahara
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are on holyday in Gran Canaria, a visit to the sand dunes and beach of Maspalomas is a MUST! Perfect clean water smaller waves and beautiful sand all around. Walking among the sand dunes are more enjoyable preferably in the 'winter' months.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a stunning view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a stop over here on our Jeep Safari day tour. The dunes across the beach looked so beautiful. There were a lot of families making their way to the beach armed with their coolers etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely afternoon on the beachSun beds 2.50euro and umbrellas the same loads available Lots of lovely restaurants along here too so could do a full day and night

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long walk from playa del ingles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long but energetic walk for about 1.30 hours through two nudist sun areas....lots to see and climbing sand dunes a must for the younger at heart

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Never been on a beach as clean as this before. Got very burnt. They don't advise Factor 50 for the fun of it!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Dunes

If you like swimming in the sea beware, some of the waves are very energetic.The beach is very clean and there is a nudist are if that is your thing. Sunbeds and brollies 2.50 euros eacjh from 9 till 5.  The dunes are great to walk across (there are some nudists there too).
