reviewsWithKeywords.text: What can you say about Maspalomas beach? As fantastic as it was the first time I came here 30 years ago. Incredibly hot if you choose to walk through the dunes do take a drink. You will likely stumble upon the nudists who are fairly brazen in the dunes and on parts of the beach so be prepared.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great clean beach for a family visit.lots of places to eat and the option of sun beds or sitting on the sand.surf board hire is on the beach as well.Good shops with in a short walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: These sand dunes are fantastic ,although you are meant to follow a path though them the fence was broken and flattened in places, its to protect the wildlife that live there.I found it was much too hot to go across between 10 am and 6pm. Certainly worth a visit .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nature at its best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We travelled here on the Global bus from Puerto Rico during our holiday.  I wanted to see the dunes for myself after reading about them.  It was very hot and i would advise you to bring plenty of water.  Enjoyed pretending we were all in a real desert.  A nice half day spent here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great to see and the kids loved it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the dunes and beach while staying near Maspalomas. We visited the dunes at night and the beach during the day. The beach looks great but it quite rocky in places so wear beach shoes to stop your feet getting hurt.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOW !! Still stunning after 28 years
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked these wonderfully breathtaking dunes twice on our recent visit. They are still stunning after our last visit 28 years ago. Take enclosed shoes/trainers to wear. The sand is extremely hot. Get your cozzy on and slap the suncream on very thickly and walk. You will get the most amazing suntan. Oh and dont forget to take and drink plenty of water. It will take around an hour even at the shortest point. It's very deceiving how far the sea is away. Oh and hopefully you won't be shocked by the number of naked human beings when you get to the sea. It is a nudist beach afterall. Your sunglow should hide any embarrassment you may experience. OH MY WORD there were some sights. Hahahaha

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sea beach hotels walking boulevard and especially the sand dunes are fantasticWe have been here in winter and summer never disappointed!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach to have a stroll on especially after dinner when it is a bit cooler with your partner letting the water soothe your feet as you walk. Very safe but if you have small children with you be careful how far you walk as they might see more than you would like if you go as far as the nudist section. Each to their own

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brilliant walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is beautiful to walk from Faro to Playa Ingles One area close to the Faro is nude section of the beach - be considerate

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was the first beach we went to, and was the best. Clean sand. clean water. They have sand dunes a bit further down. There is a lighthouse. Hard to get a sun bed here unless you arrive early as this beach proves to be quite popular. We put towels down and relaxed while our daughter played in the sand and the sea. Really lovely day, also they have various restaurants and shops around the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This sandy beach starts at the lighthouse and extends to playa Inglese. The lighthouse end is a family beach with kids having great fun playing in the sand and surf. Here there are shops, bars restaurants and some basic beach showers and foot washing. There are is a lifeguard watchtower and red cross post. There are some further beach bars and sunloungers for hire. It becomes a nudista beach further up and much quieter if you wish to get nuddy or escape the much busier family beach. Something for everyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beaches ,yellow sand but heavy so dont have to clean yourself and towell off sand.Also good if you want to go topless or even nude near Kiosk 4.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Huge beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely big beach, very clean, will definitely be going back there, the sand dunes were amazing and lots of lovely restaurants and bars close by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely the best beach in Gran Canaria. Would strongly recommend for everyone to visit as the sand dunes are breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful classy resort
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love this place..stunning hotels..wonderful beaches..up market shopping and stunning views.lovely bars to just chill and relax in..have come here several times now and resort remains pristene and beautifully maintained.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach and dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach and dunes at Maspalomas are always stunning and relaxing. It's always clean and very safe. The waves and under current can get tricky at times, but in the ocean people should always be careful and mindful of children. Though the atmosphere is completely different in the winter and summer, both times of the year are great. I do prefer Gran Canaria in the winter, there are more retirees and people wanting to get out of the cold and dreary weather in northern Europe. It's a quieter and more laid back experience. In the summer, there are more families, children and noise. Though there are often lots of people, the beach is large enough to always be able to find a quiet spot. I love walking from Maspalomas to Playa del ingles along the shoreline. It stretches more than 5K. The dunes are also stunning and very interesting. You feel as though you are in another world. Definitely bring a couple of bottles of water and decent flip-flops in the summer. In the winter, spring and autumn the sand is cool enough to walk barefoot. I'm always amused when I read reviews here of people who aren't prepared for nudists and gay people in Maspalomas. That is what Gran Canaria is all about and people are attracted to the island by the live and let live attitude. Those offended should probably look elsewhere to holiday. Maspalomas beach is probably the main attraction of Gran Canaria and well worth the walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not enough sunbeds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beaches but not enough sunbeds....not much good if you are disabled in any way....very very busy location

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, uncrowded beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easiest way in is via the Lighthouse area in Maspalomas. Beach bars doted along the beach. Clean and warm sea. Nudist area a 15 minute walk away from lighthouse.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mountains of the Moon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: amazing sand dunes unspoilt and not really crowded despite loads of trippers. Quite a long hike to lots of facilities

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best golden beach sand on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a must see while on the island. I would rated it as the main attraction of gran canaria. We were there on a windy day and my girlfriend was annoyed by the sand because it was flying everywhere. Besides that you should know that there are many nudists around there. If you don't mind this two things that you will love the place. It is great for photos, desert photos and beach photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: superb but take supplies
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fabulous area although it gets incredibly hot. You HAVE to take supplies of water and a hat. If you do go wandering be aware that there is a specified 'gay'area and this is not for youngsters

reviewsWithKeywords.title: worthwhile visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: an easy walk from Meloneras, where we were staying. good to experience sand dunes, although very, very hot. take a hat and water! glad we went.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This place is nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most warm places at Canarian. You can really enjoy the big sea line, desert, shops and restaurants around. Ive been here three times and will visit it again!))

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good waves, busy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach. Friendly people, big waves (sometimes), not too expensive drinks on the beach. If you go up to the restaurant to have a lunch, choose the restaurant carefuly. Do not accept the first guy offer who just pushing you to have a lunch at his restaurant. If you walk more far, you will find better prices and more warm welcomed staff. I would recomend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An experience!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We recently stayed in a nearby hotel. The beach is clean, and very crowded up until 8pm in the evening. It was lovely walking by the water where there is a lovely breeze. The beach is divided into sections, some nude.We felt entirely safe here. The atmosphere was people having fun. very pleasant.Would I stay the whole day? Probably not, space was limited and the sand was sticky and black. It was nice to visit for a short while.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Something for everyone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We didnt stay in Maspalomas but we visited twice to eat and use the beah. The area itself is huge and there are some great shops-low end to very expensive. The beach was very busy but there were spots to sit . We walked along the seafront and went to the dunes which were empty of people and peaceful...we ate in a couple of different restaurants. Excellent food and 26 euros for 2 with drinks. Too touristy for me and too busy but worth a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach. The sand in the south is very hot and the water is pretty cool. Strong wind makes tanning easier, but after 16 o'clock sometimes sand storms appear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hot hot hot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here in June, the average temperatures were suppose to be around 21 however, we experienced between 27-33 on most days (and evenings).The beach is split into four areas;1) family (the largest section)2) partial nudist 3) gay community 4) nudist The beach is clean and scattered with plenty of seating. You need to hire the loungers and parasols between 09:00-17:00. The sand gets extremely hot as the day goes on so make sure to take flip flops if you intend on going in the sea to cool down. Like most tropical beaches be very mindful of the misleading breeze. Reapply sunscreen and cover up during the peak sun. Also pay attention to the UV index to determine when is best to stay in the shade.Best time to visit the beach is early morning or after 18:00 when the sand is cool. You can take a pleasant stroll along the beach with the sea lapping at your feet. The police patrolled the beach several times an hour in their 4x4 which was reassuring. There are also bins placed strategically along the beach to help keep it clean.Depending on where you are on the beach you can either take a couple minute walk (or longer) to the bars and shops for refreshments. If you'd rather stay put there are sellers patrolling the beach but obviously much more expensive (I overheard one sale - 6 euros for two cans of cola).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes area at Maspalomas (El Oasis) are a protected reserve. They are a stunning site on the south of the Island, stretching from Playa del Ingles to Meloneras.The sand here can get very hot so don't be tempted to go bare foot unless at the shore.The area is well known as a naturists haunt, so there will be many people with no clothes on at all...you get used to it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely clean beach with a few sights to behold!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a great walk along this beach. I'd thoroughly recommend it. It's about 4 miles from Maspalomas to Playa de L'inglese. It's a great way to get some exercise and the sand dunes are spectacular. Be warned though, it is a nudist beach and oh my we saw some sights!! The beach was beautifully kept and we saw very little litter. In fact two empty cans in the whole walk!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So peaceful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was like being in the middle of the Sahara desert but with the sea nearby.  Beware the hot sand will eat your flip flops and give your calves a great workout!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's 40 years since I last visited Maspolomas...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are still impressive, though the beach seems a lot blacker than previously. The walk across from the Rui Palace Hotel to the water is a good 30 mins, hilly, and soft, hot sand. BE WARNED, bare feet is not an option! It's  not easy if you're not reasonably fit! There is no direct access from the Duna Beach Bungalows, where we were staying.An alternative is to park your car (or get a taxi) to Calle Las Dunas, San Bartolome de Tirajana, 35100.  That's adjacent to the town beach of Playa del Ingles.  The walk along the waters edge is much flatter and firmer.  10 mins or so will get you to the FKK, naturist, nudist area though it's not compulsory..... Clothing is optional!A 30 to 40 minute walk will get you to 'Bongoland', which is essentially a gay area, though I gather there is a region too for swingers and so on....The dunes are not as big as I recall previously, and the stone circles seem to have largely disappeared.My wife and I enjoyed a nice day sunning on the beach, though I did notice close by, a young lady (alone) attracting unwanted attention from a solo male (nude) who insisted on displaying his wares. (Not very impressive! ).  Regrettably, these sorts of incident are fairly commonplace around naturist beaches, though the perpetrators are not naturists.... On the beach itself, there are a variety of 'stations' serving refreshments, typically ice creams and drinks, including alcoholic.  Prices are quite reasonable considering the logistics.To avoid unwanted attention, I would suggest staying in mainstream areas, or close to the water where there is an almost continual stream of folk, walking between Playa del Ingles and the Faro lighthouse at Maspolomas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this beach during my holiday in Gran Canaria this year and thought it was fab. Lots to do on the beach such as jet skis and paragliding. It was €9 to hire two sun beds for the day which I don't think is too expensive. The sea was lovely and clear and could see the fish swimming around my feet. Would go back again if ever on holiday here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great place to visit, just come back from a holiday there, loved it well worth a visit to see them amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful  beach, it was very busy there when  we  went for the  day.  Plenty  of bars on the  beach for  thirsty people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach in maspolomas is really good however I would advise not swimming too close to the light house one side is all rock and the other towards the dunes you need to go 200 yards to escape partial rocks and sharp coral I found out the hard way. That said I would recommend maspolomas beach. If you like a good walk you can follow the beach all the way to Playa del Ingles .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed here over a couple of weeks in June of this year,it's a lovely resort with lovely rolling sand dunes and beautiful beaches, the sunshine is guaranteed,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach. Sand dunes look great especially from a distance. We didn't walk across them cos it was too warm. Definitely worth a visit.

People all packed with brollies, towels and picnics children in tow all trekked across the dunes to finally arrived at the most beautiful clean Sanyo beach and blue blue sea. reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maspaloms
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspaloms is so beautiful place and amazing shopping and also lovely restaurants. And the Beach is so beautiful 😍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of sea front restaurants with and lots of different types of foods only walked through as your get hassled into the restaurants lots of German restaurants seems to be that type of area

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: one of the best beaches I ever been to. the sand part before reaching the actual beach is absolutely amazing. stunning views and really really nice resorts.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved the beach we sat at paddy's Irish bar for a drink friendly service with a smile and a chat. You do get bothered by the bag and watch sellers. But if you know it's fake say so. Beach cleaned daily

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golf holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalomaa is a flat resort with plenty to do on a low key no rowdy british or irish bars more good restaurants and cocktail bars for a quiet holiday good for families with the amusement park and a good beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: All creatures great and small
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really good beach. Very fine sand and plenty of nudity if that floats your boat. Wonderful stroll along the front for miles. Suitable number of beach bars interspersed along the way. Very clean as well with no rubbish and plenty of bins.  €7.50 for two loungers and a brolly. Worth it.Very shallow sea, but still swimmable. Best attraction in Masepalomas for a reason.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Glorious
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Miles of clean sandy beach. No rowdy groups. Beautiful clear sea and big waves to enjoy. Nice little cafes and clean facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Purpose built
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Maspalamas is very pretty in parts , all very well done , plenty of shop's , bars , restaurants , café's , the outdoor cinema is based there plus plenty of other activities .But it is purpose built for tourists , nothing vaguely Spanish or Canarian here , no history or culture .If you want beach life , night scene , shopping and restaurants this is the place to be , some very high end hotels here beautifully done .Sand dunes are spectacular to see .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely views and great sands on this wonderful beach. Great restaurants and bars along the way. The natural.made sand dunes are a must see whisky in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: sand go on for ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the beach and dunes are well worth a visit they seem to go on for ever a walk a long the water line is recommended, if your going to walk the dunes take plenty of water with you can be hard work walking on the dry sand hills

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Southern tip of Gran Can
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice resort featuring a working landmark lighthouse, plenty of shops , bars and restaurants, a long promenade for leisurely strolls. Large beach with watersports and a huge expanse of dunes which you can tackle Lawrence of Arabia style on camel or on foot. The dunes also host the naturist sunworshippers but there is plenty of waterside space for those who want to keep their costumes on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WARNING hecklers!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wanted people to read this as a warning. As soon as you're off the bus and past the main row of shops there are a crowd of African ladies who will say hello and try and entice you. Say NOTHING, make no eye contact and move on quickly with hands in pockets. Don't engage them. They managed to get hold of me and strap a tacky bracelet on to which I said I didn't want it, thank you and to let go of me. I walked away and she started to get aggressive, not realising I'm from Glasgow and wouldn't put up with her intimidation. I was polite but told her to stay away from me. She'd managed to heckle money from my partner because they try to separate you. There are police cars on the beach but looks like they turn a blind eye. Beach itself is overly crowded and feels touristy, not relaxing. The dunes are nice but overshadowed by this. It's a shame.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing desert-like area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The dunes are amazing. It's such a vast area of sand, with such enormous dunes, that you really get the feeling of being in a true desert. There are small huts which sell water and soda, which you really need after walking about in the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long beach with great sand dunes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice long beach with large sand dunes at the end.It's a very nice beach but it does get very busy so you may want to go towards one end. We found a nice cove in the afternoon slightly off the main section which was pretty quietThe sand dunes make this a highlight but remember to wear some shoes as the sand gets very hot

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely place to go for a walk with beach, shops restaurants, a lighthouse, lifeguard on duty on the beach lovely views you can walk to playa Del ingles along the beach would take a while though

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice place nice walk from hotel plenty restaurants and drinking spots lovely beach would recommend a visit here

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk along the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great long beach plenty of wonderful sand dunes.  Lovely walk along water edge.  Plenty of shopping opportunities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for long walks exercise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just really a very very long beach, but nice for exercise and a long stroll. Not really a beach-person, but was nice as I could several kilometers in the sun.Nice walk either to or from Playa del Ingles to Maspalomas. Good restaurants in both ends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: excellent family stay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stayed here Oct, lovely complex, great staff might be returning, close to amazing sand dunes.plenty to do.visit the watermark and souix city must do

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches on Gran Canaria
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's easy to see why Maspalomas is one of Gran Canaria's most famous beaches. The dunes go on for miles and are part of a protected nature area. If you like you can go on a camel ride through the dunes if you don't fancy walking. Overall a great clean beach to spend a day. There are lots of little cafes and restaurants along the beach to eat. I would say though watch out for the gypsies who will try to put 'bracelets' on you and then force you to then pay for them. They sit on the boardwalk by the beach and approach you in groups and can be a bit intimidating. We found the best way to avoid them is to just walk with purpose past them and don't engage with them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: SPECIAL AND NICE BEACH!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very special and nice beach cos here is small desert + very very large beach ... sand is hot ... very long beach .. many people ... but i think everyone could enjoy when you go there...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy Busy.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went for a walk along the beach here as many thousands of people do. The sand dunes do look great but make sure that you have something on your feet as the sand is very hot. The beach itself is very busy especially at the weekends when a lot of Spanish people come down to chill out. Water quality not that good. Lots of nudists further along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful resort
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really exclusive resort with a great beach, sand dunes and lovely shopping. The promenade is great for an evening stroll.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded and dirty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was quite disappointed when I visited the beach which backs on to the sand dunes. The beach was crowded and dirty and wouldn't return again. Ive never really been a fan of the beaches on gran canaria, lanzarote beaches are much more cleaner and ideal for swimming. The sand dunes are impressive however, which continue in to the distance and are worth seeing and taken snapping some pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely but very windy. Had sunglasses on and sand still got in my eyes. If taking children and happens to be a windy day please make sure eyes are covered

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clean beautiful beach.We had a drink in a restaurant called Antonio unfortunately we found the guy a bit moody and our fizzy drinks were flat.We got the free bus from our hotel occidental margarita. There was a lovely little restaurant near the pick up point and they sold lovely ice creams.There was plenty of sun beds on the beach €7.50 for two.Watch out for the ladies walking towards the beach.They go to shake your hand and tie a bracelet around your wrist. Well more like a piece of string and then want money from you!We kept saying no but they wouldn't let go!We was silly and paid them They wasn't going to give us change from a 20And then only gave us 5 change So 15 for two pieces of string!Beware

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Marie
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. Very clean. Sun loungers and parasols available. Very relaxing. Sand dunes worth a visit they are lovely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the bus from Puerto Rico to Faro de Maspalomas around 30 minutes. The lighthouse is amazing by the way. Lots of eateries around and an up market shopping mall but we only stopped for a beer. Our aim was to walk along the beach to Playa del Ingles about 3 plus miles. We found that it was easier walking at the ocean edge than on the dry sand. The beach is very clean in fact in the whole of our walk we only noticed one piece of rubbish. There are places along the way to buy drinks etc although we did not use them. There is a warning that you are entering a nudist area and there were plenty. We remain clothed on this occasion. All in all a very lovely walk to help burn off excess holiday calories.

reviews.title: Really nice place…. Far better than others nearby beaches etc
reviews.text: Lovely place….. nice bars and restaurants. Museum and gardens…. Very nice place to visit for few days. Beach is wonderful and near The Dunes. Will go again

reviews.title: Nice but often windy
reviews.text: Great beach. Found glass and needle on the beach. Wear shoes and be careful. If it blows, it blows a lot here. Toilet costs money. Lunches are expensive. But it is so nice with the dunes and the beach itself. Big waves all the times we were there

reviews.title: A day in a turquoise paradise.
reviews.text: Beautiful turquoise sea and beautiful beach with great Italian takeaway restaurants. I recommend the boat teip from Puerto Mogan. The walk from Puerto Rico to Amadores along the sea is breathtaking.

reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.text: Maspalomas beach is one of those places that stick with you: wide, scenic and dominated by dunes that create an almost desert landscape, unique in the Canaries. It is perfect for long walks, relaxing in the sun and enjoying truly spectacular sunsets.The water is clear and the beach is well maintained, although at times it can be a bit crowded, especially in areas closer to services. However, just move slightly to find quieter corners and enjoy all the beauty of the place.Overall it is a beach that is definitely worth a visit: suggestive, wide and with an atmosphere that invites you to slow down and breathe. A little jewel of Maspalomas.

reviews.title: Eden
reviews.text: A lot of place, white sand and everything what you need. Sunny place with a great atmosphere and beautiful water - ideal for families

reviews.title: Greatest beach on Gran Canaria?
reviews.text: Kilometre by kilometer with beach and "waterhole" and bathing possibilities all the way from one end to the other 👍 ♂️ 👍 check web camera before the trip and weather forecast for wind and strong waves

reviews.title: Long sandy beach
reviews.text: It is a beautiful sandy beach several kilometers long. Great for swimming and sunbathing. Two sunbeds and an umbrella can be rented for a slim 7,50 euros per day (unfortunately until we were on the beach everything was always occupied, so again only the towels).  There are some beach bars (including toilet at the back), and some detached nudist areas. Protected dune areas are separated by ropes.Adversity, as usual, lies with visitors rather than nature. Columns of tourists march along the beach as if it were a highway in rush hour traffic. Windy sellers try to turn on their goods. Tourists ignore the barriers of the protected areas, destroying the nature reserves, and last but not least some nudist visitors, who absolutely must present their physical deficits to the world in the textile sector. It is definitely the opposite of a deserted beach, but worth it due to its length.

reviews.title: Always beautiful dune
reviews.text: We went for the umpteenth time to Maspalomas, this time Bull Escorial hotel in Playa del Inglés, from there a few minutes and you are on the immense beach of Maspalomas, desert sand, beaches that reach 50 meters between the sea and the promenade, dry heat always, magnificent dunes, the experience of the Sahara in small, a must try

reviews.title: Natural Beauty of the.world
reviews.text: Stunning unique and a magical natural place and with a sea and climate all year round Spectacular with pleasant places where you can bathe and be relaxed, its coasts its dunes beaches and its wonderful people and delicious food all in general a visit where I will return safe always

reviews.title: Just a little different than usual
reviews.text: There is much to explore on the island and definitely recommended is a tryke tour through the mountains. Further beach of maspalomas a place to go. Verer puerto morgan is fantastic.

reviews.title: Noise from dealers
reviews.text: A very nice,clean beach,but here it's like the fish market in Hamburg.Here you have no rest.Every few minutes drink dealers walk around and shout so loud that you can burst the ear drum.Then the Chinese masseurs run and whether you read books or have eyes closed,they stick the massage card in front of your nose.After that the dealers come with bags,beach towels or sunglasses.I don't know why they don't ban that.There are many bars in 100 meters where you can drink something or shops with beach towels and sunglasses.It's really so annoying.Here is no recreation.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach shame about people making it cheap!
reviews.text: Don’t get me wrong this is a beautiful beach but it’s what goes on, on the beach which is disturbing. Me and my husband were off to explore this beach and it’s is long stretch of sea and sand. Now we knew there was a naturist part and been on one before but we wanted to get to the high sand dunes. This is a naturist beach buts it’s more than that! I’m not allowed to say what is happen but theses things should not be happening on a pubic beach. Beware don’t take your children through this part of the beach. It’s disgusting.

reviews.title: Still a great beach despite the erosion
reviews.text: This was our fourth visit to Playa del Maspalomas and as usual it didn't disappoint.  We got to the naturist beach at kiosk 7. Here there is a beach bar with a toilet. Sunbeds are 7.50 euros each and an umbrella is also 7.50 Euros (payment by card only).  The sunbeds are just in front of the dunes set back from the sea. They are available from 09:00 to 17:00.They have a wind break which they put up around the sunbed area when the winds are high (which is needed when the sand blows off the beach and dunes). It's a laid back atmosphere with mainly couples giving a good balance of males and females. During the week the majority of people are naked here. On the weekends there are some people wearing swimsuits who use the area. There is a gay section at  kiosk 6 where there are mainly males. It is also safe to leave your belongings unattended at the naturist beach area  if you want to go for a swim or a walk along the beach. The naturist area stretches from Kiosk 3 to 7.The one sad side I want to highlight is the apparent erosion of the beach by the sea. It has become more apparent this year.  I've shown this in the attached photos. On one particular stormy day the sea was coming in as far as the start of the sunbeds. They seem to have tried putting in flood defences further down the beach by protecting the beach with pebbles. Hopefully  this erosion is only temporary as it would be sad to lose such a lovely beach.Despite the erosion I still highly recommend this beach. It's my favourite naturist destination.

reviews.title: Disappointing and careful: pushy traders and brash thieves
reviews.text: The beach is long and wide and there is the adjacent dune landscape, but we have seen more beautiful beaches. The sand is brownish, suffused with black sand and therefore it is not particularly inviting at the front of the waterline, as the water appears brownish-dirty due to the sand (even if it may not be at all). The beach is very crowded in many sections at peak tourist time. But now two very negative points: there are countless “flying merchants” who want to sell fake sunglasses, handbags and T-shirts and beach towels in a very intrusive way. You might expect this in other holiday destinations, but not on a beach in the Canary Islands in this massive and intrusive form. And worst of all, there's brazen stealing on this beach: We had a backpack stolen from us, lying right next to us in the sand, when we were apparently distracted for a moment by something else. And although there were plenty of people all around, the thief probably escaped just like that. The police we contacted were completely disinterested and said they could make a report for the insurance company, but otherwise they could not Enterprise. This would not surprise you in some holiday destinations if you had imagined otherwise in an EU country like Spain.
So many stones in the water... not pleasant to swim here, they only take cash for the rent of sunbeds and umbrellas. Strange I think

reviews.title: Mooi strand
reviews.text: Nice beach and dunes. Many rocks and stones in the sea.  Nice restaurants and bars near the beach. Little shade, a parasol is needed.

reviews.title: A quiet and warm place
reviews.text: Hello my readers, it is the second time I go and without hesitation you would return infinitely times, I was with a friend and her parents. What I like most is the crystal clear water and lying in the hammock is the best thing.

reviews.title: Alone worth the holiday!
reviews.text: Alone worth the holiday! Enjoyable especially in the early morning and at sunset, when the sun seems to play with the ocean waves and golden sand dunes giving unique and always new views...

reviews.title: Lovely beach.
reviews.text: Fijn strand. The sea wonderful not too hot or too cold. There are also shops and cafes along the way. Only downside is that it is often very busy if you do not arrive early enough then all the sunbeds are already taken but there is a lot of place to put your towel. Still, I would recommend it if you are in the area. A little further on are beautiful dunes.

reviews.title: Walking in the sandstone! And celebrate the Sun Juan with Latin bands
reviews.text: I took a walk in the sand dunes and it was enjoyable!And because I visited this beach "June 23" I was lucky to live the traditional celebration that takes place in the sandy beach. "Noche de San Juan"The locals from the afternoon become groups, families, friends, and have their food and drinks in order to spend many hours having fun!!We were enjoying the concert with two wonderful Latin bands (we danced a lot) and at 12 p.m. they threw fireworks and all fell into the sea to be washed off by the bad energy.Although there were thousands of people in the sandy, it was impressive that everyone was calm and in a good mood. Don't hesitate if you are a tourist to put your feast on the sand and enjoy the special evening

reviews.title: Dirty and neglected. Dangerous at night around the pond. We will not return.
reviews.text: Many years going at least once a year. Large and pleasant beach. 4 or 5 star hotels. The maintenance of the surroundings is disastrous, dirty and disgusting. The San Bartolomé town hall is completely abandoned, and they say it's the jewel in the crown. After five there is no police or surveillance. We were scared by some foreign minors unaccompanied by two older ones. During the day, the police only make sure that the dogs don't step on the beach. They are anti-pet and have made a mess of everything.

reviews.title: The only thing indigenous to South Island.
reviews.text: It's all that's left of the South Island. The beach is fantastic for those of us who think that our concept of the beach is to walk it, swim and not be back and forth. I walked from St. Augustine to the Lighthouse, a good hike that must be done early, then it is too hot.They should for the little that is natural in the south island control more people who get on the dunes to take the selfie and fine. I am funny about all those German guiris who get on them and paint the monkey, when in their country, which I know well the citizens are the police themselves and there they would draw attention to whoever climbed and here they come to do what they do not do there. It is the fault of the one who indulges him. They are not only German, English, Spanish.... But this strikes me with how civic they are in your country...

reviews.text: Actually we only went to visit the dunes because it was not beach time.The dune landscape is fantastic, it almost looks like a desert but with the sea in the background.

reviews.title: Visible deterioration of public areas.
reviews.text: Visible deterioration of public areas dependent on the city council. They haven't bothered to even change or remove the blue flag, which is a rag.  The carelessness, the abandonment and the abandonment is total, as seen in the photos. Last night in front of the Maspalomas pool a group of six ores surrounded my older parents and me to scare us. They threw the smoke from their cigars in our faces and challenged us.  I have been coming for over 30 years and in these last two this has become a place where you can not leave the bubble of your 5-star hotel because all the public spaces are depressing and completely left. Never Maspalomas again.

reviews.title: Blessed inaction
reviews.text: Good weather, good food, beautiful hotel as well as the surroundings; possible buffet as well as several à la carte restaurants

reviews.title: Worth a visit if you like the beach :)
reviews.text: Maspalomas beach is definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area, it’s easily accessible and has lots to do and see. Take a taxi to Maspalomas lighthouse & start from there!The beach caters to a lot of people; mostly families and quite a few nudists, there is a section of the beach which is specifically nudist. There are plenty of shops and places to eat along the front; make sure to grab a couple of cold drinks if you’re planning on heading to the sand dunes as it gets hot out there! Or you can just relax on the sand and take a dip in the refreshing sea. After you’ve been to the beach, take a walk back along the front and stop off for a Starbucks in the sun & then hit the Fund Grube shopping centre for everything from perfume to Pandora jewellery.

reviews.title: Nice place to visit
reviews.text: Lovely huge beach very busy though and no sun beds free. People egnoring the do not all on the dunes. Lots of shops and restaurants

reviews.title: Unique dune landscape
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in Gran Canaria. Super extensive and the dune landscape is unique. The beach as well as the water are always super clean. We love coming here.

reviews.title: Recommended!
reviews.text: Recommended 😊 In summary....Dunes of MaspalomasRecommended entrance: behind the Hotel Riu Palace Maspalomas, via a wooden walkway that leads to a safe and easily accessible viewpoint.La Charca de Maspalomas & Maspalomas LighthouseWalk along the promenade to the lagoon and lighthouse, ideal for observing nature.Playa de Maspalomas (family area)Quiet beach with fine sand and shallow sea, perfect for children.El Senador Restaurant & Beach HouseLunch with children's menu and sea view.Park of the LighthouseShaded green area where the baby can rest or play in peace.Holiday World MaspalomasEntertainment center with rides and play areas suitable for children.Nomad Gastro MarketInside Holiday World, it offers different snack and dessert options for a delicious snack.Playa de MelonerasIdeal beach to end the day admiring the sunset.

reviews.title: Beach and various options
reviews.text: It is not a beach of dreams, sand and water are normal. But there are many options for adults. Shopping options and many restaurants nearby. If you walk to the dunes there are zones of nudity that people walk without problems.

reviews.title: Town beach
reviews.text: Beach is at one end of the promenade and has a wide expanse of sand with the famous sand dunes further along.  There’s a large area with sunbeds and umbrellas to hire at reasonable rates - 7.50e for two beds and an umbrella when we visited at the end of April - sit where you like and someone will come round to collect your cash.  Plenty of cafes, restaurants and bars nearby on the promenade and I think there’s also a beach cafe further along nearer to the dunes.

reviews.title: The horror has a face!
reviews.text: The beach is a joke! 1.5 sq km of sand dunes, completely crowded in most hours and surrounded by a Disneyland-like belt of cheap attractions and accommodation for an estimated 500,000 people.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach.
reviews.text: A stunning beach. The best on the island by far. It’s immense and had loads of space. Top tip - there are toilets at the back of the beach kiosks.

reviews.title: Lovely place.
reviews.text: We got a taxi from our hotel to Maspalomas today. We got out near the lighthouse. Where there is a long promenade to walk in each direction. Along the first part are several me designer shops and good restaurants. We stopped at one for coffee and cake. (Although for me the didn’t do gluten free) I had to have an ice cream. We sat outside with the ocean behind us on some lovely garden furniture. No one rushed us which was good. There are toilet blocks although where we stopped also had there own.

reviews.title: Beautiful and clean beach which
reviews.text: Clean and beautiful beach. Great refreshments and even toilet facilities on the beach. Sunbeds are €7.50 per day for 2 beds and parasol.

reviews.title: Striking dunes
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, suggestive dunes. Free parking is available nearby.Nice promenade and bar for eating or drinking. Recommended at least one visit while staying on the island!

reviews.title: Playa Ingles 2025.

I conducted the trip barefoot, but recommend good shoes to avoid gnash ulcers

reviews.title: Visit the sand dunes

reviews.title: Declining quality
reviews.text: We've spent dozens of holidays here. The dunes and the beach have changed, due to dunes are only partially accessible and due to many stones on the beach make a walk the whole beach impossible.Unfortunately, many hotels also lack service.

reviews.title: Fantastic location and fantastic weather
reviews.text: We are currently in Maspalomas in September week 1. Thought it worth updating and correcting some earlier reviews.The beach is huge with plenty of room for everyone and all persuasions.We enter from the Lighthouse end and find plenty of sunloungers for families and everyone wears a costume although a few ladies are topless. Further along the beach towards Playa del Ingles is cabin  8 with tables and chairs for customers to enjoy their drinks. Shortly afterwards is a Red Cross post and this seems to signify the clothing optional area. At cabin 7 there are a number of sun loungers and parasols frequented mainly by nudists, as is the beach around it. The loungers are good value at 7.50 euros for the day but payment is by credit card.Further along is Cabin 6 which flies a Pride flag so aimed at the gay community. No dogs were seen on the beach and beach sellers/massage guys were around but certainly didn't hassle anyone. They knew how to take no for an answer and just moved on.A walk on the dunes gives a new perspective but wear shoes as the sand is scorching in the hot weather.This has just turned into our favorite place in the Canaries.E

reviews.title: Fabulous
reviews.text: Fabulous, vast never create crowds, its location and beauty are postcard. Part establishments, mostly free and equipped. Clean. In some places there are stones when entering the water

reviews.title: A lot of dogs. Big change
reviews.text: We visit this area for many years, and love it. Recently I don't know what happened and why, but it used to be area with no dogs around at all. But now there are many, and I mean a lot of dogs around, and unfortunately a lot of dog poo on the ground now and barking at night. This is big change, as there were literally no dogs in this area, place was clean. Now the roads are dirty with dogs poo and nights are not quiet as before. Big dissapointment, starting to think of another place for the holiday. Unfortunately.

reviews.title: Day at the beach ⛱️
reviews.text: Had a lovely day at this beach.Chose to do a shore excursion while on a cruise to the Canary islands. So glad I did.Lovely beach with good facilities.Nice restaurants that are reasonably priced.Will return one day.

reviews.title: Huge beach
reviews.text: Immense beach to walk and sunbathe without burdens, nudist area without limits, the whole beach is... Fine sand but also area with many stones.

reviews.title: An exotic beach
reviews.text: The dunes are incredibly beautiful. Go there at sunrise for an unforgettable experience. However for swimming it is less top, there are many pebbles!And when the wind blows hard, wear a scarf and glasses to protect your face.

reviews.title: Nice and extensive beach
reviews.text: Possibly the best beach on the island, surrounded by dunes and nature. How inconvenient the difficulty of parking. It has access from the lighthouse area and from the English beach area. There is an area dedicated to nudism. It is worth walking along the shore contemplating the nature and vastness of the beach. Another drawback is the large volume it has, but that is inevitable on an island where tourism is overflowing.

reviews.title: Sand dunes wow!!
reviews.text: Visited from Mogan and came on the bus, really good as the bus station isn’t a far walk to the beach and sand dunes.We walked to the sand dunes - how wonderful those hot! Great water areas to wash your feet after and plenty of cafes etc to get a drink and food. A high end little area of shops near to the beach which also had a supermarket. Really lovely and upmarket area Maspalomas is! Really impressed and world visit again!

reviews.title: The dunes of the desert
reviews.text: Immense dunes, expanse of endless fine sand, children had fun rolling through the dunes some over 10 meters high, very nice place and certainly pleasant, for those on the island of Gran Canaria is a must visit

reviews.title: Very good beach
reviews.text: Very good beach with sun loungers and municipal umbrellas for rent. This makes it affordable to the pocket. Very wide and long beach with option to use your towel if you do not want to rent. I miss showering at all beach access points but, knowing there is drought I understand. Recommended beach if or if

reviews.title: Suggestive
reviews.text: Immense beach, with the dunes of maspalomas behind. Possibility of both free beach and to rent umbrella and sunbeds for 7,50 €. Around 5 pm they start to collect umbrellas, but you can stay safely and for those arriving from that time onwards can still use the sunbeds for free. Apart from perhaps the first "lido" coming from the parking lot, the next (from kiosk n.7) are mostly nudist beaches, but not exclusive (you can therefore also stay in costume). The various kiosks have just a drink, some ice cream / snacks, so it is recommended to go equipped. We stayed in mid-August and still found it quiet.

reviews.title: Too bad.
reviews.text: The sea and beach is great but why too few sunbeds and umbrellas?sale of liquor is minimal, toilet open until 17.00 and also the umbrellas are removed at 17.00 depending on the catering industry which can not process the mass no water activity no.... Have had better beaches there is much more to get out of this...😎😪

reviews.title: Nudists have ruined the beach and dunes
reviews.text: Terrible, nudists and especially naked men walk around everywhere and these lie among the dunes waiting for other men to visit. Nice dunes and beach, but I feel that because of the freedom of the LBGT doctrine the island has been totally ruined. Starting point is entirely aimed at the WOKE people and sex toys are sold openly on the street and supermarket. Too bad and no second time for a holiday with my family with young children on this island. Next time Turkey

reviews.title: Fint
reviews.text: Nice place to swim, but there are long walking distances to the beach itself and the sand dunes. The duvets themselves were not as beautiful as in the pictures, there was, among other things, a lot of garbage there... but very fun to swim in the sea

reviews.title: Okay, but nothing enchanting
reviews.text: Better than anything in san agustin, but a further away from the beds (7,50eur for 2 beds and 1 umbrella) to the water, in which unfortunately many large stones lie. It was clean, but it didn't invite us to swim. The restaurants all seemed like 0815 touri-bequatcher, only the surf burger stood out STRONGLY with loving furnishings - but we were not after burgers. Various "beach towel" sellers and massage providers annoy almost every second (sometimes even touching to persuade the massage, which is not even clear) that it is already annoying. From 1000/1030 it quickly became full. For the dunes it was too hot for us with a small child at 34 degrees, we can't say anything about that. all in all ok, but no reason for us to come back again, because it comes close to playa amadores here in nothing.

reviews.title: Lots of sand but not on the beach
reviews.text: The dunes are fantastic but the beach is not even bathing, apart from the cold water as everywhere in the Canaries, even in July, waves, difficult currents and there is no sand in the shore but stones and stones.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach BUT......
reviews.text: Beautiful beach we hired two loungers and a parasol which was a great price, but unfortunately we was absolutely hounded by men constantly trying to sell you rubbish, then there were men and women offering massages etc then a women selling drinks, than a man selling fruit / drinks absolute nightmare we couldn't wait to get of the beach and back to our hotel never again, surely something needs to be done to stop these people annoying others, how I kept my cool I don't know....... I was looking for a nice quiet relaxing time, at one point I actually pretended I was sleeping to stop these men trying to sell us rubbish l.

reviews.title: Maspalamos !!!!
reviews.text: Spectacular beach in the south of the island, mountains of blonde sand in continuous motion, which makes the landscape constantly change no day is the same, you can observe these dunes from the viewpoint, it is a natural beauty

reviews.title: No nudist beach
reviews.text: The dunes are beautiful, but the so-called nudist beach is 'clothing optional'. In fact, 95% are clothed. It doesn't feel right to be naked in there. Everyone looks at you and keeps clothes on themselves. Not recommended!

reviews.title: Beautiful site
reviews.text: Exceptional site the beach is perfect.A dream vacation.You have to do it if you go around.I highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Nice excursion and grateful if there is sea breeze
reviews.text: Very well to walk the marked paths, a pity that people do not respect them and go where they want.The INFO staff very willing to give recommendations and explain us about the history of the place under their experience.

reviews.title: Excellent sandy beach
reviews.text: Lovely sandy beach. Sea was lovely and warm. Wear swimshoes if going swimming as there are a few rocks before you get far out. Also the sand burns your feet so they are a must ! We walked to the sand dunes, nothing to see but sand really. People come around selling things whilst you are sunbathing, which is a nuisance. Paid 7.50 eur  for 2 sunbeds and parasol, which was worth it, but when you have paid, you dont expect to be harassed by sellers. Also payment was by card only. Walked along the prom, past the lighthouse and visited a few shops.  Lovely area, would definitely visit again, a lot nicer than Playa del Ingles

reviews.title: Beautiful sand dunes, breathtaking views
reviews.text: The beach is absolutely beautiful, with miles of sand dunes and plenty to explore. There is a walk you can do from the Dunes to the light house following the nature reserve path, it is mainly sand though. Please take a drink with you as it gets very hot. Breathtaking views!

reviews.title: Dunas
reviews.text: It is very beautiful nature that you should not skip there.not always easy to walk but still recommended. Beautiful

reviews.title: Kiosk 7 beach
reviews.text: The gay beach is now one kiosk #5 further along with rainbow 🌈 flags a few hundred yards along.you can’t miss it Kiosk 7 was busy & frequented with mainly middle aged& older couples/solo mostly all nude. Sunbed+ parasol E7.50 card only. Kiosk has snacks/ice creams/ drinks/bar area with chairs and parasols plus  toilets. There’s a big LOVE sign on the beach If coming from Maspalomas lighthouse end of beach  10-15 mins walk, easier to walk along the shoreline than through the Dunes. Sand gets very hot. Take only your sandals/beach shoes to the sea when going for a swim in the sea. Naked swimmers and clothed people walkers all on shoreline, no issues. Some couples left their sunbeds & bags for a bit to head into the Dunes behind kiosk for a nude afternoon stroll.

reviews.title: The most beautiful on the island...
reviews.text: The most beautiful beach on the island of Gran Canaria....services and restaurants available, white beach with sunbeds and umbrellas at honest prices.Easily accessible by bus (Faro Maspalomas stop)Not to be missed..

reviews.title: Sun, Sand, and Freedom...
reviews.text: Looking for a beach with a vibrant LGBTQ+ atmosphere in Gran Canaria? Look no further than Maspalomas Gay Beach! Here's your ultimate guide to experiencing this slice of paradise.Getting There:RIU Palace Passage: This route is perfect if you're staying around the RIU Palace area. Follow the designated poles and path – it's important to stay within these boundaries to avoid fines.Playa del Ingles Walk: Enjoy a scenic stroll along the beach from Playa del Ingles. Keep an eye out for the gay section around halfway. Look for the festive rainbow flags near bar number 8!Beach Bliss:Lounging in Comfort: Ditch the bulky beach bag! Convenient cabins are located along the access road where you can rent sunbeds and umbrellas for a reasonable price (around €7.50).Clothing Optional: Feel free to embrace the freedom! While nudity is common here, you can choose what makes you comfortable. Most beachgoers tend to go without clothes.A Word on Cruising: Be aware that cruising in the dunes, which used to be more prevalent, is now discouraged. Police patrol the area, so it's best to enjoy the beach for what it is – a relaxing and fun atmosphere.Final Tips:Relax, soak up the sun, and enjoy the welcoming vibes of Maspalomas Gay Beach. With its stunning location, convenient amenities, and open-minded atmosphere, it's the perfect place to unwind and have a great time.

reviews.title: A day at the beach
reviews.text: Attention to all visitors. The beach chairs from the municipality are available for a fee on maspalomas beach, no problem its everywhere , we paid in cash, which is still allowed according to European legislation, but is normally only possible here with a bank card, which is not mentioned anywhere, but the collector did point it out to us using threatening language in a not so friendly way to be sure to take the card with us the next day, otherwise he would send us away.

reviews.title: Pleasant.
reviews.text: The weather didn't help, it was always cloudy in the morning. The water in the hotel pool and on the beach was cold and therefore not possible to enjoy. It's a place to visit once because the island is small.

reviews.title: Definitely an absolute must with a little detour into the dunes.
reviews.text: Fantastically spacious and very clean beach with a view of the adjacent dunes and the sunset. During the day, adventurous skydivers land in the adjacent dunes. Due to the enormous space, there is enough space to lie down here even in high season. The sand heats up a lot during the day, so a visit to the dunes barefoot is highly recommended, at least in the evening. The transition from the beach to the dunes can occasionally be a bit rocky.

reviews.title: To have
reviews.text: Park near the Rui Palace and take the main access to arrive at the start of various walks.  Avoid leaving the santiers because it is a nature reserve but some people also frolic there (see more...)... too bad for the lack of control.Otherwise very nice walk also possible just in the dunes.

reviews.title: The best of Gran Canaria
reviews.text: The views were amazing. We took a lot of photos! Awesome . You can't miss it if you go to Gran Canaria. Unforgettable

reviews.title: Protected place?
reviews.text: A magnificent place which is supposedly a protected place... The fact remains that people happily cross the limits and go frolicking in the dunes without anyone finding fault: too bad...

reviews.title: The Dunes a must see
reviews.text: Very relaxed area with stunning views you do feel like your in the desert. Enjoyable visit as part of a walk to playa de Ingles

reviews.title: Magnificent landscape and canary
reviews.text: A truly peaceful, splendid place and if you want to go for a walk, there are several marked trails available. Choice of beaches for all tastes… family/gay/nudist! The only problem is the water is cold: you have to be brave to swim (but doable 😜)

reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.text: Very strange and not worth the climb because of the view of nudists and the shrubs which shelter shady encounters

reviews.title: Nice view for nice photos
reviews.text: Very nice experience. You can park for free in the street of the RIU hotel. You walk under the arch of the hotel and you are there. A tip: take good sunglasses with you, as the sand blows into your eyes.

reviews.title: To recommend
reviews.text: Magnificent view of what very much resembles a desert! Park near the Riu hotel and then go down to the esplanade where walks begin. We followed the one of +- 5 kms: very pretty. Along the beach towards the lighthouse and the nature reserve and then return via the dunes. To recommend !

reviews.title: Hot days at the beach
reviews.text: Was on holiday with my partner May 2023 and came the beach a couple of times. Beautiful beach with some clothing optional areas little bars/cafes here and there. Surrounding sand dunes are something else. Can be a little rocky in places

reviews.title: Unique surroundings. Relaxed stay
reviews.text: Beautiful walks along the beach, relaxed atmosphere. Walking barefoot through the dunes is just wonderful (better in the morning, afterwards it gets quite hot under your feet). Lots of opportunities to take a break at kiosks. Toilets available. We will definitely come back.

reviews.title: Amazing  sand dunes walk
reviews.text: Amazing walk through the gorgeous sand dunes. Just follow the wooden stakes and you'll not get lost. Amazing  views of the sea all along

reviews.title: Dunes Maspalomas
reviews.text: You definitely have to walk from RUI through the dunes to the sea!! It's really exhausting, but the experience is worth it. It's best to go barefoot. There's a kiosk by the sea, you'll be thirsty. Enjoy 😊

reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.text: Essential visit if you go to Gran Canarias. Very extensive beach with immense yellow sand dunes, where it is a joy to climb them and with spectacular views.On very sunny days the sand can burn quite a bit, but with sneakers or t-shirts it is easily solved.In some places nudism is practiced.

reviews.title: Magnificent
reviews.text: Just saying awesome. Everything very careful, very clean.The sand burns quite a bit but it can be solved with flip flops or beach shoes.

reviews.title: Holidays 2023
reviews.text: Wonderful beach on the islands, for walking or sunbathing, a wonderful place, it has spaciousness to be quiet and depending on the time of year you go, few people...

reviews.title: Absolutely 💯 worth seeing
reviews.text: It was an absolute highlight for our children to climb the dunes and slide down. The view over the sea and the beach is also wonderful.

reviews.title: For a walk on the beach
reviews.text: The dunes are unique and worth a trip. The beach is very busy in some places with walkers with and without clothes. It's inviting to go for a walk. The spot at the lighthouse is suitable for surfers. But beach experience to swim. Maybe for half a day.

reviews.title: Dunes and sand and wind
reviews.text: Large expanse of sand dunes that reaches the sea with a very large beach on the open sea, very windy with waves and cold water. It didn't excite me

reviews.title: Get it right
reviews.text: Siting on the beach for a few days know kiosk 3 ,weather and beach beautiful, great staff in the kiosk,one let down 3 toilets only one being used ,lock broken on the door for the time we have been visiting the beach.....low and behold a guy turned up in the middle of the day ,took 2 hours to fix it so no toilet facilities, just gone about an hour and guess what the lock doesn't work on the toilet.Its beyond me why he bothered it's the same old story when it comes to the tourist facilities, especially on the beach .I guess we are lucky the flusher works [he didn't have to touch that] for a few years coming here they're were no facilities as they were waiting to see what contract the governing body were going to offer,they only ones that were inconvenience by this was the tourist ,the ones who spend there time and money here to keep the economy going.....wake up and smell the roses lads [people running the island] people will eventually go somewhere else.

reviews.title: Nice Holiday
reviews.text: We had a wonderful time on Holidays in Maspalomas in February 2024 where we stayed in Vista Oasis Bungalows for 1 Month. We visited the beach and restaurants most days and enjoyed evening walks along the promenade

reviews.title: Island "Dessert" Experience!
reviews.text: A very unique experience to walk over these sand dunes to the sea, making use of the well-marked pathways (distances markers included). This experience can be undertaken after walking or swimming at the beach or vice-versa after a walk toward the sea across the dunes. There is also a wonderful pathway along the top to view the whole "dessert" scene in all its glory. The latter option is ideal for the more physically challenged as walking the dunes needs considerable determination and not a little strength. I personally walked along this paved pathway to the Riu Palace Maspalomas  Hotel where there is a small viewpoint with excellent indicators of the pathways available  and the distances involved in taking each. The very adventurous head to the lighthouse!

reviews.title: Desert in Gran Canaria
reviews.text: Unforgettable experience in this amazing place. I felt like in different planet <3 Must try if you have your vacations on the Gran Canaria island.

reviews.title: Playa de Maspalomas
reviews.text: Long and nice beach that is connected to the Dunes (desert). Several different places to rent sunbeds or just take your own pick and pack and take a seat. Nice views and in addition to the beach, it works well for a walk or a run!

reviews.title: Do not miss
reviews.text: Dunes impressive with their surfaces and the feeling of desert. A marked trail, otherwise don't hesitate to get lost there.Be careful not to leave your trash behind.

reviews.title: Wonderful beach
reviews.text: Amazing beach. Very big and with a lot of people. The weather was wonderful and I went swimming and walking for the whole afternoon.

reviews.title: Dunes are Incredible
reviews.text: Totally unique experience walking the sand dunes of this wonderful natural reserve. Expect lots and lots of sand and a fantastic beach.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach but..
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful beach and light house however ruined by tourist traps trying to sell you rubbish and time shares. I lost count how many times I was approached on the beach by people trying to sell me beach towels. Walk past restaurants theres people trying to get you to go in or you have a look at a menu and they are already setting up a table to get you to sit down. What should be a relaxing day at the beach turns into the opposite.  Too touristy and too many people pestering. Has put me off visiting this area again.

reviews.title: Not Phew!!!
reviews.text: For the dunes, it's nothing extraordinary... when we saw the Pyla dune!!!! Not at all the impression of desert as they sell us for excursions… in the middle of town and along the tourist beach… big disappointment. Paid parking required!! Because no place to park

reviews.title: Everything we wanted
reviews.text: Everything we wanted, brilliant sun sea and sand, plenty of entertainment in the evenings with ample choices of places to eat and drinks

reviews.title: Very average
reviews.text: Very average beach. Lots of black pebbles. Sand not really golden. Waves too big to swim in. Fairly pretty dunes but traveled by thousands of tourists which is a bit of a waste. And above all, very clever pickpockets try to steal from your backpacks. A couple along the main promenade average size. Woman with black and red hair, traveler type. Caucasian man.

reviews.title: Naked exhibitionists
reviews.text: We did this walk with our girls a few days ago.   Naked people sun bathing in the dunes is one thing but these guys are walking butt naked on the path with their tackle swinging. Definitely an exhibition element to it.  Wouldn’t recommend for families

reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.text: The Maspalomas dunes are a wonder. There are several viewpoints from the paths but you can walk into the dunes and after 5 minutes the people disappear and you get to experience the dunes almost to yourself. Beautiful !

reviews.title: Handsome
reviews.text: To see, breathtaking panorama, easy to reach on foot or by bus, very particular and evocative with a wonderful peace

reviews.title: Beach to escape
reviews.text: Too windy, it’s usual here!What has unfortunately changed is the ban on retreating into the dunes where we were protected from the sand and the wind, it was happiness.And as always, for a small percentage of people who do not respect the place, everyone is prohibited from doing so.But of course, these people are still there.I've been coming here for a long time but it's over forever.

reviews.title: one day visit
reviews.text: Spectacular views and nature. Loved exploring the dunes then spending time relaxing on the beach. local bars and restaurants for tapas.

reviews.title: Love this place
reviews.text: Fantastic beach weather and laid back people are friendly and the water is warm for this time of year

reviews.title: Nice clean beach alternative naturalists
reviews.text: Beautiful place sandy beach goes for miles Atlantic ocean fab Beware of nudists if that's not your thing.It is a gay beach in parts and we did see mangrove areas being used for hook up place but kept on walking.We don't offend easily some may do.Relaxing places to chill  up near playa ingles part 😎

reviews.title: Nice to have seen.
reviews.text: Nice to have seen. Not very special for a Dutchman who regularly visits the Dutch coast. Dutch dunes are also beautiful.

reviews.title: Too many rocks
reviews.text: The most beautiful thing about a beach is being able to walk on it barefoot, a feeling of freedom which unfortunately is lacking on this beach because due to the many stones that are not removed it is almost mandatory to wear footwear.

reviews.title: A must on the island
reviews.text: Just great. Very spacious, well-kept and you can surf. The surrounding restaurants are a bit weaker, as they are very touristy. But the environment is fantastic

reviews.title: Walk to the lighthouse
reviews.text: Long beach that, among other things, leads to the lighthouse in Maspalomas. If you go from San Agustin/Playa del Ingles on the beach, it takes about 1.5 hours. At the bottom of the bend there were very large rocks that made walking barefoot a little uncomfortable, but you can walk further up from the water.

reviews.title: Nudism without ifs and buts, but not forced ;-)
reviews.text: The beach between Playa del Inglés and the Maspalomas lighthouse is very long and wide. Large parts of it are open to nudists, although the beach is very tolerant. You can choose between being completely covered and being completely naked. The walk from one end to the other takes about an hour and is not exactly a pleasure when the wind is strong.

reviews.title: Dunes
reviews.text: The views were amazing...it really did feel like we're in the middle of a desert. we took loads of photos.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Really impressive dunes that you can walk around, up, down and through. Well marked tracks to the lighthouse and the botanical gardens. Need sensible footwear as some bits are stoney and some sharp bits off the trees

reviews.title: Long beach
reviews.text: Lovely beach to walk on, my tip is to walk from Playa del Ingles towards the lighthouse and have a good lunch there and take the bus back if you can't bear to walk 😁

reviews.title: Playa de inglis restort
reviews.text: Sandy beaches but many steps to get to them. Although the German Bath and sun bathe naked it's worth walking over the sand dunes, take plenty of water as it's extremely hot. At the other end the beaches are split by rocky groins to break the waves but its very safe for kids and poor swimmers like me.take your litter with you as there are bins at the steps and water to clean the sand from your feet. A few eaterys on the beach but many places at the top. Sat and wed market well sign posted but be warned pickpockets are around and if the have no prices on products haggle hard cos a 45 euro leather wallet came rapidly down to 20. Local bus to Morgan was very simple and so was the aquarium,  pay cash or by card we used a revelute card aquarium was about 12 euros for 2 each way and Morgan was about 4 euros each. Its a long way to the view point so do it slowly and early and again warning of pickpockets. If you like dancing it's free at the kasbah shopping centre in the evening. Lots of other activities available Inc go cart racing, the buggies are mostly on winding roads with only a tiny section off road but still great fun. The downfall is they tout for tips at the end ,and I think it's wrong if you need more money ,charge more. Great hotel so we are considering going back for longer.

reviews.title: Trip to Meloneras
reviews.text: It's a long way to walk in loose sand if you don't have healthy legs. From RUI we took 35 minutes and from Maspalomas lighthouse it takes approx. 20 minutes to walk. Sunbeds with parasol cost €7.50. Otherwise, you can get plenty of good drinks in the kiosk.

reviews.title: Beautiful long sandy beach with lots of public traffic
reviews.text: A great combination together with - or better yet after - hiking through the dunes. At the western end there are many places to stop for a bite to eat, and you can also look at the natural brackish water lake.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, but the dunes a little further on are more impressive!
reviews.text: Through beautiful dunes and then past the beach to go to Meloneras. On the far left there is a kind of bar for the LGTBQ community and nudists.

reviews.title: The Spanish-style dunes of Pilat
reviews.text: Dunes as far as the eye can see, running along the sea. Classified as a nature reserve, a very pretty walk in sight. Don’t hesitate to choose a hotel with a view of the dune.

reviews.title: Quick visit and awesome dunes.
reviews.text: My wife and I didn’t have much time to explore the dunes, but it really seemed like a good place to visit. You can cross the sand dunes and walk to the beach and enjoy the water if you want to, and lots of people were.

reviews.title: Maspalamas Beach
reviews.text: The beach is fantastic and large. Sea lovely for swimming and body boarding with the quite large waves. Downside is why some men on the nudest section think is it ok to openly play with themselves and get away with it!

reviews.title: a little overrated
reviews.text: The dunes are well worth it. Nothing else, everything prepared for foreign tourism. It's not worth more than an hour. There are better areas in Gran Canarias to visit. The beach is acceptable, but the naturist area is for old couples. I lost my desire to run the Maspalomas marathon. Nothing attractive about the area itself.

reviews.title: Necessary visit
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, wonderful, with a bit of waves almost permanently, but beautiful dunes for photos.

reviews.title: Walk, swim or sunbathe
reviews.text: Long beach with huge dunes as the backdrop.  Spotlessly clean with grey sand. I walked from Playa de Ingles to Meloneras which takes about an hour. Expect to see nudists  mingling with you as you set off to Meloneras. I didn’t swim but there were plenty of people in the water. There are a couple of  bars on the beach should you need refreshments. Take a walk in to the dunes as they are amazing.

reviews.title: Dunes
reviews.text: Quite an experience, it is a mini desert.Great for walking or taking a camel ride.

reviews.title: Brill awesome superb best place iv  ever see with my  eyes.must see but be carefull.very hot.from above and below.wind can cause
reviews.text: Fantastical area of the world.you can find a seat and watch the dunes roll with the wind.magical.not to forget expierience.

reviews.title: Nice to see.
reviews.text: Beautiful dunes if you are in the area, definitely stop by. Sand is very hot on the feet on sunny days. Be on time, it can be very busy.

reviews.title: windy and decadent beach
reviews.text: almost unlivable beach: always windy and full of old nudists up to the Maspalomas lighthouse. It's just worth a walk. Lack of toilets. I do not recommend taking an umbrella and sunbed.

reviews.title: Without a doubt one of the best beaches in the Canary Islands
reviews.text: Maspalomas beach is par excellence one if not the best beach in the Canary IslandsThere are almost seven kilometres of beach surrounded by an extraordinary dune parkOn most of the beaches you can enter the sea peacifully because the sand reaches a long distance into the waterWhen there are high waves it is wonderful to jump with them The beach has no currents so you can swin calmyThere is a beautiful promenade full of restaurants where you can eat buy taste an ice cream or simply have a coffee or a beerThere are a number of hotels of all kinds of categories and prices to stay and enjoy a few days of this wonderful beach

reviews.title: not a green island,only  maspalomas and mogan are beautifull
reviews.text: island with verry much old dated hotels,maspalomas is verry nice,mogan is the most beautifull place on the island.we had a car for 3 days to visit the island but it is not verry nice everiwhere it is so dry, no flowers nothing.we had a good hotel near the golfna green place with palmtrees.

reviews.title: The food and drink kiosks are now open!
reviews.text: For the last three years, since the pandemic, the food and drink kiosks at Maspalomas beach have been closed. Now the upgraded and renumbered kiosks are open. They serve a variety of food and drink, although more expensive than the local supermarkets (see price list in the attached photos). Whilst we were there we found only one open toilet. This was at the storage kiosk B between kiosks 5 and 6. There is an attendant there who will charge you 50 cents to use the toilet. At all the other kiosks the toilet was locked. Lack of toilet facilities is still an issue at this beach.Sunbeds and umbrellas are still cheap as 2.50 euros per item (7.50 for 2 sunbeds and an umbrella is a bargain). They fill up quite quickly at kiosk 7 with most sunbeds taken after midday, even on a weekday.The kiosk numbers are now:Kiosk 4 at the Playa del Ingles end of the beach is naturist.Kiosk 5 and 6  at the middle of the beach is populated by mainly gay beach goers and naturists. These kiosks are close together.Kiosk 7 at the Maspalomas end of the beach (where we went) was naturist.Kiosk 8 near the lighthouse in Maspalomas  is non naturist.I never walked as far as kiosk 3 in Playa del Ingles. I assume this is non naturist.This was our second time on the beach at Maspalomas. We would highly recommend this beach for naturists and non naturists too. Be warned though that the waves can be very strong and it can get very windy. At kiosk 7 the sunbed attendants do put up a wind break around the sunbeds when it does get windy which is a nice touch.With food and drink facilities now available this beach has become our favourite beach.

reviews.title: At the beginning of the dunes…
reviews.text: From the beach you can admire the lighthouse, the luxury hotels and the immense sand dunes that act as a fantastic appendage to the city of Maspalomas. Beach with sunbeds and umbrellas for a fee (€7.50). the beach staff begins to collect the umbrellas, leaving the sunbeds, as early as 4.00pm, 4.30pm. The sunbeds are therefore fully available to those arriving at that time. Many characteristic places to dine or drink. It can be reached from the city by bus or taxi (€7/8).

reviews.title: A lovely Beach to visit.
reviews.text: We took a trip to beach as our Hotel (Vistaflor Bungalows) laid on a free bus, as did a few other hotels. We were dropped off near the Sand Dunes to the left of us as we walked South a short distance to the Beach. It was a glorious day, very hot with clear blue skies. We wasn’t quite prepared, and I would advise on taking a sun tent or a parasol. However we keep topped up with Sun Cream and kept Hydrated. The Beach was very clean. There were a few traders asking to sell blankets, hats, glasses etc, the usual. We took shelter in a few of the bars for drinks and Ice Cream, there are so many to choose from. However from experience, I can highly recommend Dunnes if you want a child friendly menu too. If your are in Maspolomas, you must visit the beach, you will not be disappointed.
