I have attached a few photos, but a camera phone in the sun doesn’t do it justice.

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: A beautiful beach where you can walk along the shore of the beach for kilometers from Playa del Inglés to Meloneras, for me one of the best, if not the best beach in the Canary Islands.

reviews.title: The dunes make it
reviews.text: Let’s face it you are there because of the dunes. The beach itself is okay. Wavy and full of sand so it’s not clear. It’s a bit shallow at the beginning so that was nice. The way the waves come in leaves a nice pattern.  You can walk and walk and hit the dunes. There are shops and restos close by. But I’m sure there are better looking beaches elsewhere on island

reviews.title: THE SPOT
reviews.text: Without a doubt THE Spot on Gran Canaria.The Dunes are magnificent and rather well preserved.They extend over a few kilometers and several routes start from the Mirador de las Duna next to the RIU hotel.A must see !

reviews.title: Pleasant day
reviews.text: Huge sandy beach surrounded by the beautiful dunes of Maspalomas. Presence of several kiosks along the promenade by the sea. There is a series of paid sunbeds and umbrellas in one area only at a cost of €7.50 all day. Showers are free while public bathrooms have to be paid for. Near the sunbeds there are several places to eat and shop.

reviews.title: In the dunes
reviews.text: Sublime landscape with numerous sand dunes, beautiful water, clean and pleasant beach with good places to eat.

reviews.title: The dunes and beach of Maspalomas
reviews.text: Splendid location: beautiful beach, beautiful and well-kept seafront (really long), try the camel ride along the dunes. A place that makes you dream.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Huge sandy beach. Large part for nudists and gays. Deckchairs and sunshades at a reasonable price. 2 deckchairs + a sunshade -7.5 euros/day. Too bad that at 5 p.m. they remove the sun visors

reviews.title: Absolutely an experience to do
reviews.text: The entrance to the Dunes is simply crazy, it looks like it was the entrance to the desert of old Egypt, a truly breathtaking cisa with its immensity

reviews.title: OK but better beaches that are quieter.
reviews.text: Although nice wide sandy beach, not enough sun beds for hire, very busy and a lot of beach hawkers flogging everything you didn't want.  Promenade and area by shops were quite nice. We only visited the once, which was enough.

reviews.title: True nature
reviews.text: Natural and wild place, still uncontaminated. To be visited at different times of the day. Spectacular at sunset.

reviews.title: Desert in Gran Canaria
reviews.text: Kilometers of golden sand with incredible dunes that extend from Playa del Ingles up to the Maspalomas lighthouse... breathtaking landscape with animals of different species that live inside camouflaged between the sand and the small green oases that can be found here and there ..

reviews.title: Probably the best beach on the island
reviews.text: This is probably the very place that our imagination pictures when we hear the phrase “ocean beach.” Soft sand, rolling turquoise waves. A coastline of several kilometers, along which you just want to wander alone or holding someone’s hand. At the beginning, near the lighthouse there is beach infrastructure - sunbeds (7.5 euros for 2 sunbeds and an umbrella), cafes, showers, a first-aid post, lifeguards and quite a lot of people. Further on, there are noticeably fewer people, the dunes begin and you can be almost alone with the ocean, throwing off all conventions and the remnants of clothing. The sand glistens in the sun, there are areas where it is almost black, and others where it is very light. . After lunch, umbrellas are removed and you can use sunbeds for free. The ebb and flow of the tides are very pronounced. So even if you are vacationing in another place, it’s worth coming to this beach.

reviews.title: lovely beach
reviews.text: Incredible beach. We came twice during our holidays. Plenty of restaurants and snack bars. We had a lovely time

reviews.title: Very beautiful but supposedly closed to visitors...
reviews.text: Free parking allows you to visit.Small sandwich and drinks seller next to the site. Be careful, site apparently closed to visitors....a ranger told us that it was closed even though there was no clear sign, just a long piece of tape around a passage... Nothing clear, so lots of people who go there and are fined... Otherwise very beautiful site with a 1.5km uphill walk which is a bit stinging, provide drinks and snacks for the children when it "reopens"....

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Very hot sand so don’t go barefoot!   Beautiful and clean sand and it too far to walk to the water. Plenty of bars, shops and eateries nearby.

reviews.title: Maspalomas Beach
reviews.text: The beach itself is nice we were lucky and had brilliant weather it’s sandy and easy to get on to and plenty of space. I imagine on school holidays though it will be rammed (we visited out of term time). You can rent sun beds with umbrellas whilst you’re here. There is a natural reservoir you walk along to get to the beach is a 5 min walk but the walkway itself is concrete. The only reason I have given 3 stars is there are much much better beaches in Gran Canaria so if you are spending money to come here I’d maybe look more toward the south west coast like Amadores beach-which was gorgeous and Anfi which is also so lovely much much better than Maspalomas beach. Also you are harassed by beach sellers on Maspalomas beach every 5 mins trying to sell you stuff we had an unfortunate situation with a man who agreed a price for an item took our money and then upped the price, we decided we would rather have the money back and politely declined the item and he decided then he couldn’t understand us. To save a scene I told him he could keep the couple of euro he’d got of us take his item and go. Put a downer on our trip here within the first 10 min of arriving. Such a shame because if they weren’t here I’d have probably scored 4/5 just when you’ve got your children with you it’s alittle intimidating.

reviews.title: Wide sandy beach - room for everyone
reviews.text: The enormous expanse of Maspalomas Dunes ends at the wide flat sandy beach next to the sea. There's lots of room for everyone here -sunbathers, walkers, surfers and also a nudist beach.

reviews.title: No place for kids.
reviews.text: No good places for kids. We been in the dunes and unfortunately was many naked people. I was on shock and sad for my kids to see this miserable show... first and last time I will come to Gran Canaria.

reviews.title: Wonderful place
reviews.text: Clean beach. Plenty of quality bars and restaurants. One of the best purpose built resorts we have been to.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: You can access this beach from the resort maspalomas near the shops and restaurants. Or you can walk behind d the dunes from San augustin  to the large RUI hotel in PLAYA DEL INGLES . There is a path to walk along and u can access the dunes at any point . They are large and you can walk along the sea edge also. A must do if you are here

reviews.title: Maspalomas visit.
reviews.text: Walked into faro maspolomas from Playa del Ingles one morning. What a surprise when we arrived It is a beautiful centre with lovely shopssnd restaurants.  A great seafront promenade. Would definitely stay there in future rather than Playya del Ingles!

reviews.title: A bit disappointing
reviews.text: I did not enjoy Maspalomas as much as I thought I was going to. As I only stayed four days I thought it was not worth hiring a car. It would be more relaxing to stay in the area as I thought it would offer all I needed for a short relaxing break. However all people seemed to be doing there was relaxing, sunbathing and eating. The sea front near the lighthouse has a range of shops, but you cannot spend all your time here as the clothes are mostly expensive. There is an abundance of restaurants, however once you have tried one you have tried them all. They are all mostly outdoor seating venues which serve steak, seafood, paella, pizza, pasta and chicken. All the food is decent but not wow, and it's not that cheap as I thought it would be. Once you have eaten in one, you have eaten in them all as each new restaurant reminds you of the last place you ate.Player del Ingles has the same purpose built tourist units as Maspalomas, but without the designer clothes and perfume shops. It just sells the souvineers with 'I love Gran Canaria' on, the fake designer clothes, and the restaurants are the same as in Maspalomas but slightly cheaper. In Ingles there are bars too, most of which serve food and look like the restaurants but contain a few drunk pensioners waving Dutch flags to country music from the 70s. The bus services are terrible. You can never find a taxi however and wait at an empty taxi rank for half an hour. On a Sunday its particularly bad. The water park and zoo are very far away and difficult to access. The urban area is of very low density with lots of wasteland between buildings. Mainly low-rise tourist accommodation with big open spaces of rubble between them and a dried up river. Much of the area smells of sewage. You end up having to walk a lot, not knowing where to go. There are more non English speakers than people who speak English and the afternoon range is skewed towards the older tourist and is you are under 40 years old you won't meet many tourists the same age or younger. You will just see the odd one as you go about your travels.

reviews.title: Brilliant
reviews.text: It’s amazing! An experience once in a lifetime. I’ve seen the dunes combined with the Atlantic Ocean. So much sun and fine sand

reviews.title: Very Good
reviews.text: The Sand Dunes are so beautiful.However,was not aware that on the other side of the Dunes was a nudist beach.Was a bit of shocker,seeing people with their bits out😂

reviews.title: Servatur Don Miguel
reviews.text: Adults only hotel right in centre for everything. Chinese across road was great. Centrium restraurant in Yumbo centre amazing food and secret garden bar tucked away above BK was stunning

reviews.title: Something for everyone
reviews.text: Something for everyone here. Stunning dunes, great beach for walking, running (around 5k end to end) sun bathers paradise clothed or not. A few shacks along the beach where you can stop for a drink. Sea was even quite warm in Feb if you fancy a dip.

reviews.title: Absolutely amazing place
reviews.text: These dunes are amazing, you can't believe the enormity of them until u are there, stunning scenery, you can walk for miles, and its just beautiful. When visiting I would try go on a day that is not very windy,, they day we went it was quite windy and as you would expect the sand tends to get everywhere

reviews.title: Astonishing beach
reviews.text: We enjoyed the seaside walking from El Faro to Playa del Ingles (about 90 min). You need to know that a large portion of this beach is allowed for nudists. The walking from the beach crossing the Dunas reserve is great as well. Laying for sunbathing here by strong wind could be adventurous. Bars and restaurants around are offer a good choice for lunch while visiting the beach.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: It was a good walk from our hotel but it is well worth it. You can walk for miles on the beach. There are also paths to walk overlooking the sand dunes with great views. It is a beautiful area. A must visit.

reviews.title: High prize shop
reviews.text: For me it was a good expiriance I was having fun with my parents and all was good but a little bit windy but If I was you I will not buy anything in their small shops or what is that beacuse one Fanta or CocaCola is 4€ so bring with you food. I would not recommend you go if you don't want to see naked people). But it was good beacuse you have a place to play and discover.

reviews.title: Maspalomas
reviews.text: No good in January. Very windy, could not walk around.sand blown around. Had to get inside to escape the awful weather. Day trip. Would not stay here.

reviews.title: A vast beach for everybody
reviews.text: This three-kilometer-long golden sand beach is located next to the dunes and close to the lighthouse. It is usually windy here.The eastern end next to the Playa del Ingles beach offers family-friendly services such as lounger and parasol rental, and showers. To the west towards Maspalomas lighthouse, you will find the nudist areas.

reviews.title: cold
reviews.text: went in january and it was 5 degrees colder than Mogan and the wind was just awful. Felt like hundreds of pins hitting your legs. Sand everywhere - just horrible and it had been like this for a week apparently and Play de ingles worse. Would not contemplate going to this area in January

reviews.title: A nice leisure walk
reviews.text: Large sandune area between maspalomas & Playa de ingles. A great seashore walk with plenty of photo opportunities. Areas of deckchairs to rent and various watersports available. Except to see a few naturist sunbathing. You can find secluded Areas amongst the dunes for secluded sunbathing.

reviews.title: No cash for sunbeds
reviews.text: Excelle ya beach , just a small tip for any visitors the  sunbeds and parasols along the beach are now card payments only ,no cash accepted ,  there is a small area to the left end of the beach near the watersports centre that takes cash

reviews.title: Christmas on the beach
reviews.text: Never seen a beach like this before only on TV beautiful sand dunes and no litter can spend hours just walking carefree up to meloneras or just take in the views or wander along the promenade just spent Christmas here totally different Xmas and Christmas trees and decorations everywhere

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, fantastic views but beware nudist parts
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, and excellent views. The dunes are incredible and definitely a must see in Gran Canaria. Be careful when you are with children, there are nudists on the beach near the sand dunes

reviews.title: Great views
reviews.text: Just beautiful. Large sandy beach and amazing sand dunes , great views.Surf school on the beach.Some nice little bars on beach promenade.

reviews.title: Nice Beach !!
reviews.text: It's a beautiful beach spread over a long stretch going up to Meloneras.  The beach had sunbeds and parasols for 5  euro. Unfortunately no Kisoks were open. During long walk one can pass through dunes and nudist section. The water sports facilities were very limited. One thing I liked most  which I used to see everyday in the morning from my hotel balcony was  that beach was cleaned thoroughly  early in the morning. One can easily spend entire day on the beach.Very good for long walk...

reviews.title: Love this beach - as always.
reviews.text: Had 2 weeks of great relaxation on the "middle" section of the  beach.  Wasn't too windy, got quite hot, and was almost always blazing sun!I wish whatever battle is going on about the kiosks could be resolved; they are still closed.  They are very handy, and are a focal point also.  However, there is no shortage of vendors wandering the beach - though I don't think they're meant to. So, authorities, open the kiosks, or give the vendors a break!Also note; if you want to pay for sombreros/sunbeds you MUST PAY BY CARD - not cash.Great time though!  :)

reviews.title: Stunning views
reviews.text: Stunning views of the dunes from a distance and when walking through the path route which takes you along to the beach, be prepared and take some drinks

reviews.title: First Visit  Naturist Maspalomas Beach
reviews.text: First time in October we visited the Naturist beach ,we were staying at Magnolias Natura which is superb, the free mini bus dropped us off at the beach side of the lighthouse, Disappointed with the beach found the walk quite long and tiring on the sand we reached kiosk 7 which was naturist all the kiosks were closed , but a guy comes round selling drinks.The sea  was cloudy  sandy and grey the sunbeds were comfy but looked very tiredalong with the shades. The umbrella   and beds were only 7.50 euros which was good.We had a nice time at the beach , but have been to much nicer nauturist  beaches in Greece.

reviews.title: Naturist Beach Maspalomas
reviews.text: A week in playa del ingles,first holiday without the kids for a long long time.So decided to try the naturist part of the beach.Absolutely loved it to bits,hired sun loungers for €2.50 each some days,others just on the sand.Mainly Germans around us,who couldn’t have been friendlier.Lack of toilets was a negative.But can’t wait to visit again next year! 😎

reviews.title: Paradise for naturists and non-naturists alike
reviews.text: The non-naturist part of the beach is near to the lighthouse (kiosk 8). Further down the beach at kiosk 6 and 7 is the naturist beach. Kiosk 7 is predominantly gay whereas kiosk 6 is a mixture of people. This was our first visit to a clothing optional beach outside of the UK and what a great experience it proved to be. The beach is best approached via the 2.5 km trail through the dunes from the Riu Palace Maspalomas hotel.  It took around 30 minutes to walk from there as you are walking through sand. This will bring you to the Kiosk 7 area of the beach. The beach is sandy (and gets very hot so wear shoes on the beach) and very clean. There is plenty of space for sunbathing either on sunbeds, on the beach itself or near the dunes.We spent our time on the sunbeds at kiosk 6. As has been stated in other reviews only card payments are accepted for umbrellas and sunbeds. It is 2.50 euros for each item (so 7.50 euros for 2 sunbeds and an umbrella). The kiosks are still closed but there are people who come around selling cold drinks and snacks. Sellers on the beach seem to be carefully controlled as you see the same sellers every day and they are un-intrusive. At kiosk 6 it was mainly naked couples, which was great, with a few clothed people. One downside was that many people tended to smoke and as the sunbeds are close together it was difficult to avoid the smoke.It is safe to leave your belongings on this part of the beach when you go in the sea. We did this and never had any problems.The sea, being the Atlantic, can be very rough at times. However this didn't take away the fun of going in the sea which was warm. There are no toilet facilities at this part of the beach which is disappointing but I'm not going to knock off any marks for this as the overall experience on the beach is fantastic. Our best naturist experience to date.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: Lovely beach next to the dunes; parasol hire very reasonable Nice beachside bars and restaurants Nudist beach further on

reviews.title: Short trip to the south of Las Palmas
reviews.text: Beautiful sunny days all throughout our stay and the beach is clean and safe and the dunes are amazing. The water sports are reasonable and lots of shops and restaurants all over the area 🏖🍷🌞

reviews.title: Just Beautiful!!
reviews.text: Just returned from a wonderful week at palm Oasis.Palm oasis is set in the most beautiful grounds , the apartments are fantastic, equipped with what you need , clean and spacious.We stayed on a half board basis , buffet breakfast and evening meal . The food was fantastic , choices and variety to suit all tastes and the fact you can keep going back for more just makes it so worth while , especially when feeding 7 . The pool bar it great for lunch should you require . The staff could not be more helpful , polite and extremely hard working ! The site is a little distance from maspalomas centre but the hotel will have you a taxi in minutes and it’s around 5 euros .  This is the First holiday we’re I’ve actually had days around a pool , normally we would be going off sightseeing. Pool days in such beautiful surroundings have left us all wanting to visit again !Thank you to all at Palm Oasis !!This site certainly deserves more than 3 *

reviews.title: Very good
reviews.text: I and my family really liked visiting this beach Very beautiful beaches. I suggest you visit, you will really like it

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Very nice place to see and take some good photos there. Even though it was too hot for me to actually walk down there I enjoyed the view from the little pathway next to it. My daughter and my partner went for a walk there and enjoyed it a lot. View worth seeing!!

reviews.title: El Faro a Lopesan experience
reviews.text: Visited ElFaro at Maspalomas in July. Excellent location, excellent food and staff made this a wonderful break after 3 years without a holiday. The room no 1323 was a side sea view with a lovely large corner balcony looking onto the sand dunes. It is very grey everywhere inside the hotel including the paint on the ceilings which we found a bit dark. The beds were really comfy and lots of fresh towels every day and a chocolate biscuit every evening left by the maid. Only negatives were the air con was not great and the sink (grey ) was right in front of the entrance to the room and in the actual bedroom. Apart from this a really lovely hotel.

reviews.title: Lack of Kiosks and Toilets
reviews.text: With the nice new kiosks placed during lockdown it was a real disappointment to not have them open. Also a huge missed opportunity to have toilets installed in the middle of the beach as it's such a long walk to get back to either end to use facilities  if you're spending the day there. For visitors please note that only card payments can be taken for sun loungers and parasols, they are no longer accepting cash and a lot of people were caught out by it. Again forcing customers to take their cards and phones down the beach it would be nice if there were some kind of locker facility by each kiosk for a small fee. Aside from this still a gorgeous clean beach and the attendants were lovely friendly people so heartily recommend a visit

reviews.title: nice and clean
reviews.text: a lovely beach with great facilities also sunbeds are very good value for money they dont take cash so you will need a card to pay

reviews.title: Tacky tourist trap.. Reminded me of Benidorm
reviews.text: Dunes were very pretty (which is why I’ve given it 2 stars instead of 0) but the rest of the beach was a tourist trap selling tatty memorabilia and sorry attempts at English food such as fish and chips and eggs and bacon (undercooked and not very appetising) It is just for tourists basically and doesn’t show any real resemblance of Spanish culture or history. We were hoping for traditional food and tapas but it was just full of cheap market stalls with people that would constantly try and grab you and try and shove cheap looking bracelets on your hand. There was lots of fake designer bags and it had a Benidorm type of vibe, full of shouty middle aged English people. The beach was extremely overcrowded and barely had any sun loungers, everyone was just cramped on the floor (The sand was far too hot to lay on). Nothing much to do or see, there’s a chemist and a supermarket for the locals but apart from that there’s very little to do. There is a nudist beach next to the main one which was all fine and dandy as I like to sunbathe topless anyway (probably the most interesting part of the trip) but we did notice that there was a group of naked men hiding in the bushes which seemed weird and somewhat sinister for a place that openly embraces nudity. If you want to experience some culture whilst you are here, I’d recommend instead travelling to Las Palmas old town as they have art galleries, museums and cathedrals to visit etc. It is an hour bus ride away though so if you are hoping for somewhere nearer-by don’t bother.

reviews.title: Nice experience
reviews.text: Mini Sahara desert 🏜 it’s pretty cool. Lovely places to visit in Gran Canaria but in general island needs a bit of tlc.

reviews.title: Best place in the wold
reviews.text: Calm och peacefullLovely ro Wall in the warm sand lonely from other People.Then you can take off your clothes and swim naked in the lovely sea

reviews.title: Sunbeds
reviews.text: Fortunately there is a lift down halfway to the beach or the beach would not have been accessible to my friend and I as we are very active 70and 76 year olds but going down would have been ok but coming back up would have been a struggle. But once down on the beach it was very nice the sun beds were very reasonable although we just assumed we would need cash to pay so made sure we had this unfortunately it was card only so had to go back to the hotel to get this.one of the visits to the beach we went later in the day and at 5oclock the attendant took away all the sun shades much to everyone’s dismay so was still very hot so we had to leave which I think was obviously what was required.all this in place we still enjoyed our visit to the beach

reviews.title: Paradise
reviews.text: Beautiful wild beach You feel to be in a place outside the world, instead you are few meters far from bar, hotels and restaurant

reviews.title: Dunes and nudes
reviews.text: The dunes not as high as I thought but the experience was 5/5. Walked from the lighthouse with our feet in the sea. The came across the naturists which was plenty of fun to watch😜. Climbed a dune which was much harder then it looks but the view of the dunes inland worth it. Turned around when the beach got a bit rocky. Tried 10 minutes of naturism with the crowd which was a fun experience-All round a must visit wjatever  your enjoyments are

reviews.title: The sand dunes are a sight to behold.
reviews.text: Miles of golden sands, lovely sea and then there’s the sand dunes. Wow, I have never seen anything quite like it. Amazing to witness, even better to scale. You can’t quite imagine just how high and seep they are until you start to walk up one. Amazing. A word of caution though that the beach is quite popular with nudists and as a result, there are many men and women who walk around butt naked all the time here. Just bear it in mind when bringing young children here.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Well worth a visit . It is jaw dropping when you first see the dunes it is like something from a movie set or postcard such natural beauty.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: If you love nature you will surely love this place, suggest to go either early in the morning if you wanna walk the dunes or late in the afternoon after 6 pm when the sand isn’t that hot .

reviews.title: Great beach...HOT sand!
reviews.text: We visited for the morning with young children. They absolutely loved it, and there were a lot of families at the beach. We used the loungers, but note that you will get charged for these, around €5 I believe, per lounger. This is for the day, how ever long you stay. It was clean, and there were plenty of facilities nearby. The sand does get very hot though, so be prepared to carry children!

reviews.title: Wind and sand
reviews.text: The beach is really long. The dunes make the beach very special. A negative point is if the wind is blowing: since there are dunes it can happen that there is more sand in the air.

reviews.title: Very Google and clean
reviews.text: Excelent  Passwörter along the sea. Smart restaurants and Bars everywhere. We stand in Las Palmas but next time we book in Maspalomas near the sea.

reviews.title: Bad burns, good ice cream
reviews.text: This is a lovely beach and the dunes are beautiful. Didn’t go into a lot of the shops but the ones we did were good (more clothes shopping than anything else). The Pingüino Soul cafe on the boulevard is lovely - really nice pastries, ice cream and smoothies; you can takeaway and the staff are kind and helpful. Confusing system with the sunbeds - not sure how to rent those and there don’t seem to be signs anywhere? Please be warned that if you burn easily - or even don’t - that the sand can be VERY hot, to the point of burning skin off your feet (speaking from experience). Definitely wear shoes, even if they’re trainers. There are places to buy sandals near the beach also if you don’t have them. Bus station and taxi stands nearby which is good.

reviews.title: Dunes
reviews.text: Km of freedom , sometimes too much wind , free nudism in a special area, Little Sahara in Gran Canaria

reviews.title: Lovely beach and restaurants
reviews.text: We had two evenings down at the beach, plenty of lovely restaurants and bars. would definitely recommend

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful and very clean beach. Many surfers. You can have a great walk from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingles. Beautiful views of the dunes.

reviews.title: Lovely place to take a stroll
reviews.text: Beautiful walk along the prom, lots of bars, restaurants and shops to keep you busy as well.  We were there on a Sunday so it was busy with locals as well as holidaymakers.

reviews.title: Breath-taking landscape
reviews.text: Fantastic landscape and unique experience. Must have to see for everyone. Highly recommended for all.

reviews.title: Shopping
reviews.text: The shopping is ok sadly lots of shops were closed, I guess due to the COVID problem, the beach looks nice, nit much to do there. I’d rather stay at the hotel there is a lot to do there.

reviews.title: Nice place with lots of sand 😣
reviews.text: Nice place to go for a walk. Plenty of people and some bar’s a long the first part of it.Recommended is to not wear shoes and socks 🙃

reviews.title: Ok but I wouldn't go back
reviews.text: We visited from Puerto Mogan and were rather disappointed at the long bus journey through the enormous town to get to the Playa. We walked by the lagoon and then across the dunes intending to cross to Playa de Ingles at the far side but it was a bit monotonous so we cut down to the coast and then returned by the sea, with a long swim there. The sea was nice and warm for February. the sand was good for walking barefoot. There were quite a lot of people around in the dunes and it didn't feel very wild or special to us. We much preferred our trips up into the mountains.

reviews.title: Pleasant Afternoon.............
reviews.text: Nice walk from the lighthouse in Maspalomas along the shore to Playa Del Ingles and back along the rear of the dunes using marked trail.There are waymarked walks but people could be seen all over the area.Best to take some water and sun screen just in case!

reviews.title: Nude men hanging around  literally!!!!
reviews.text: These are just dunes...please be careful if you have small children as lots of nude men hanging about in the bushes, when I see him he was very brash standing there wanting me to look...even tho I was with my husband..

reviews.title: Dunas, sand and ….
reviews.text: Nice place - pure and wild. Recommended for all. Take the time, out of shoes and enjoy it barefoot.This place is really for all…

reviews.title: There is nothing not to like!
reviews.text: Coming from the north of England there is simply nothing not to like in this canary island destination. Blue skies and warm sunny days. We love it.

reviews.title: Walk on set pathways or go away seems to be the new policy...not good!
reviews.text: Don't think you can roam freely on these Dunes any more. There are now just a few  marked pathways when walking from the Riu Palace end of Playa del Inglés and these take you only to the beachfront. The official excuse is that it is a Natural Park and that this measure is to preserve it. This is not the only such Park in Spain and these vigorous restrictions have only been put in place here with, seemingly, such force with park rangers ordering tourists back onto the designated paths. There is, apparently, the threat of fines for transgressions but didn't experience or witness this although there are plenty of rumours circulating that drones and helicopters are being used to enforce a crackdown!!! Certainly there are signs and information boards about sticking to pathways as well as posts set into the sand marking these new routes.So, that seems to be the end of 'free roaming.'Although there are a lot of naughty tourists everywhere, including here where rubbish has been left on the dunes rather than taken away with them, the controlling measures do seem rather over the top. After all, shouldn't we be able to ENJOY this stupendous place without such draconian controls? This is just the sort of thing that many holidaymakers will surely be upset about as, traditionally, this was a great place for roaming free and naked even! There has been an official map released to show s totally forbidden to enter zone...o.k...fair enough but what about the rest of this huge space? Are we to be excluded from enjoying this landscape for ever?

reviews.title: Perfect dunes
reviews.text: Imagine you are in Sahara.Remember the sea is not far.Just some stupid naked men van destroy your imagination.

reviews.title: tired but still fun
reviews.text: well, what can be said. please remember that i am writing this as we are still in the grip of covid and will bear this in mind. i am here for a month having a break from travelling for the last 2 years. i wanted somewhere warm over the xmas/new year period and it has delivered. very comfatable. i go for a lot of walks and get to see everything at ground level and i have to say the whole place is a mixture of dilapitated and modern. i have been to 2 "shopping centres" which to say are derilict is bigging them up. all the concrete has starting to crumble and roofs missing and the reinforced bars are rusty and exposed. not closed due to covid as it looks like a few years. the medium sized hotels have sprung up and have been allowed to build without proper checks regarding safe building practacies. the dunes are really magnificent and only a brave person will try and walk it but the walk on the beach from playa del ingles to Maspalmas is a good stretch of the legs. plenty of bars and resturants along the waterfronts run by a mixture of scandinavian and european and some are keeping with rules and asking for covid passports. many well stocked supermarkets. a good bus and taxi network. on the whole an enjoyable break and if keeping out of the bigger more expensive hotels your money will go further.

reviews.title: Nice beach but Rocky sea
reviews.text: We loved the shopping and restaurants here but the actual sea entrance was rocky so not really good for swimming unless you have sea shoes. The gay beach is at kiosk 7 towards the dunes.

reviews.title: The dunes of maspalomas are amazone.
reviews.text: Exceptional experience ...the feeling that you are in the dessert 😁 climbing the dunes and then a dive in the sea!

reviews.title: NOISY PLANE OVER MASPALOMAS
reviews.text: Much is perfect here for a great beach-holiday.  Too bad, that all that is spoiled several times a day by a very noisy plane, which is cruising the sky for half  an hour at least each time. And shame on the municipality of Maspalomas, that does not act against it.

reviews.title: desert in canary 12/21
reviews.text: lovely walk in a lovely weather just be careful with sands going into your eyes breezey but worth a stroll always a nice place to visit

reviews.title: Maspalomas - Nice Area with Great Shops and Restaurants
reviews.text: Visited Maspalomas and found it much better than the edge of Playa De Inglis where we were staying. Great shops and places to eat and nice areas to walk too. Seemed a much classier resort

reviews.title: Wonderful walks
reviews.text: A bracing walk along the beach with sand dunes everywhere.  Lots of little places to stop and take in the view and at the start of the walk lots of little cafes to stop and have a drink and relax.

reviews.title: Pleasant circular walk.
reviews.text: Vast space with desert-like features. Pleasant circular walk from the large hotel at the entrance to the dunes. Wasn't expecting a huge nudist beach though. The shoreline can get very busy with people taking a stroll. If you don't mind lots of bare flesh, then the dunes are well worth a visit.

reviews.title: Not the best
reviews.text: We were staying at Mogan nearby but visited us for the day.I have to say, we left disappointed as the place we were staying was so much nicer.It’s facilities aren’t nearly as good and it is not nearly as picturesque.It is pretty good for walking as it is so big but other than that we much preferred where we were.

reviews.title: Disappointing changes to the amenities
reviews.text: It’s a fantastic beach but notoriously windy! Great for a walk.All of the old kiosks have been replaced but none are open. In all of the former locations from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingles the wind breaks and the sun loungers have been removed. Without the wind breaks, sitting or lying on the beach isn’t a pleasant experience! Best avoided for the time being.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: We have enjoyed this beach for many many years, and it is still beautiful to walk along by the sea or in the sand dunes, and it is still one of the most stunning places to see the sunrise or sunset, but it is not really a beach you can sunbathe on all day unless you have come prepared with windbreakers, parasols/tent and / or your own lounger. Gran Canaria is known for being windy, in our past holidays the kiosks have been open and have had sunloungers, parasols for daily hire and when the wind gets up they would put netting around for you. This is all gone now, we had two aborted attempts to be on the beach, it was not too bad until it reached midday and then you'd be eating the sand and getting sand in places you didn't no you had, it was not pleasant. We asked locally as we thought maybe it was a covid issue, but apparently it is not, the other beaches across the island have sunloungers and parasols out. Apparently, it is a contract dispute concerning the new kiosks, so until this is resolved we won't be visiting the island.

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: There is a reason this is one of the most visited spots in Gran Canaria... its gorgeous. There is a clearly marked path to walk through to get to the beach. This helps preserve the biodiversity. The beach is extremely windy so if you plan on staying long prep for it. Many were set up with wind/sand breakers and enjoying the sea.

reviews.title: Sunset at Paradise.
reviews.text: There is not much to add to what people already highlights about this place. But one thing that definitely impressed me was the sunset.... Probably the most beautiful I have ever seen in my life.

reviews.title: No longer any sun loungers on the beaches
reviews.text: I used to love the beaches at Maspalomas and Playa Del Ingles but not any more. The sun loungers and parasols have been removed from both beaches, which means you’re guaranteed a sand-blasting every day from 1pm when the wind picks up and the sand starts to blow around. On my previous visits the sun loungers lifted you off the sand sufficiently to avoid the worst effects of the moving sand and they also had netting around the sun loungers area to protect you further. Not anymore, they’ve all gone. Lots of very annoyed people being forced off the beaches this week. We won’t be coming back here sadly :(

reviews.title: Gran Canaria busy
reviews.text: Hi looking to travel to Gran Canaria is it busy and good not to much hassle please could tell me if been recentl thankyou

reviews.title: Dunes and hot sand
reviews.text: Sand ,sand ,sand ,just a beautiful environment with stunning views. Got to wear good shoes cause the sand can be very hot and burn your feet. Best time is in the morning if you don't like the heat.and don't go to far if you have children  with you

reviews.title: Nice clean beach
reviews.text: Nice beach. Would recommend to go west of the lighthouse, close to the tiny brown “hut” near the lifeguards as there are rocks on the east part. Other than that, don’t forget your shoes, the sand is burning!

reviews.title: Gay beach is gone!
reviews.text: Gay beach is gone!! Bar, sunchairs, space between gays and  heterosexuals, all is gone!! There are still nr of gay guys, a  small cluster, at old place but if you are visiting Playa del Ingles for the beach, do not come here.

reviews.title: So thrilling, a cool place!
reviews.text: A must if you are in Puerto Rico! The dunes are not smth you can see everyday. I would recommend to take the buss 39-90-02 if you travel from Mogan and you can walk like 10-15 minutes to the beach. Cristal clear water, dunes, simplicity and beauty.

reviews.title: Sand!
reviews.text: Sand dunes. What more can one say, apart from maybe a good idea to bear in mind that it can be uncomfortable when it is windy.

reviews.title: Sahara with beers!
reviews.text: Fascinating sand dunes desert landscape. Fine beaches often with life guards on duty. A serene contrast to the lively Playa Del Inglés scene where, however, you can have a well-deserved beer after hiking around in the dunes.

reviews.title: Nice Clean Beach
reviews.text: This beach is very wavy so if it's snorkelling you're up for, you're best off going to the west of the island. It's so much fun to play in although children will need a lot of supervision. Lots of restaurants and bars near by.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: The sands of the beach are beautiful. Sometimes when the wind is up the waves become quiet big which is great fun for body surfing. Currently the umbrellas and sun loungers have all been removed so go with that in mind that there is no shade.

reviews.title: A quiet stroll along Maspalomas Beach
reviews.text: It was a big shocking to see this very busy beach, usually full of people, umbrellas and bed lounges, to be quite empty.  Only few people were about and everyone walking along the beach are required to have their face masks on.  The beach was peaceful and very clean.  There were some people about either sunbathing, swimming or walking along the beach like us.  We really enjoyed our two-hours stroll along this beach and through the dunes.  A good way to have burn some calories that we have been stacking up throughout the holiday.If you are planning to walk this beach, it is highly recommended that you bring your own water.  The kiosks along the beach were all closed at the moment.

reviews.title: A Sunny, Friendly, Quiet, Safe, Stunning Location - Visit Maspalomas
reviews.text: Having spent 2 weeks at the Palace Oasis Hotel,  that besides the excellent facilities,  location, quality of the staff I wanted to comment on the impact of Covid-19.  Only 20 passengers on aircraft so a row to oneself. Levels of social distancing, at the airport,  Hoppa bus - good. The locals put us Brits to shame, the majority of all ages wearing masks including out of doors and on the beach as well.  Sadly low numbers of tourists,  and economic impact evident in the number of hotels/bars/restaurants closed. Locals are very friendly and keen to assist.  So if you want a quiet safe holiday,  set in a stunning location with expansive beach, stunning dunes and lighthouse as a backdrop,  and where isolation on return is not an issue,  then I would recommend visiting Gran Canaria.

reviews.title: A surreal and pleasurable trek.
reviews.text: The sands dunes conjure up visions of being on another world, a place to leave your earthly worries behind, as well as your clothes and inhibitions if choose.  And walking naked I found exhilarating, but even those that weren’t seemed to have acclimatised to the accepting surreality that accompanies the place.  And passing wearing just a back pack and anklet people happily nodded good afternoon as if both strolling down a country lane.  Whilst fellow naturists cast a smile like you’ve both come home.  And a place for all sexualities, a public kaleidoscope of bodies and lusts, some openly entwined in the freedom and the sun.   No judgement is made of it.  Just people being people, who they really are, normally disguised in a textile world.  With no obligation to join in, nor would you be approached unless so seek by lazing provocatively and retaining the pose under gauging gazes.  But should that be your thing, enjoy love with an indulgent flavouring of hedonism, then a plentiful supply of fellow pleasure seekers with whom to share the liberating joy of the lunarscape.  We stayed a week, and was an oasis experience 😉.

reviews.title: Great walk in those dunes and Long Beach
reviews.text: Top walk in those big large dunes in Gran Canaria, impressive place like in the Sahara. Beautiful Long Beach of 10 kms long 👍❤️

reviews.title: One of the best beaches in Gran Canaria
reviews.text: A fantastic beach with golden sand, plenty of space, dunes to explore and climb and best of all - waves!

reviews.title: Beautiful sand dunes
reviews.text: A must visit if you want to take a stroll on the beach, very different to other beaches I have visited before.

reviews.title: A safe and enjoyable few hours
reviews.text: The dunes are impressive and and something to admire. The main 'beach' area was well populated but everyone respected social distancing. The water was warm and the beach very clean. The waves were deceptive , great for everyone but if little ones walk out be wary as some waves were unexpectedly big. The facilities are good and there are toilets available and plenty of places to eat and drink.

reviews.title: A popular if slight overstated choice geared to younger visitors
reviews.text: Surrounded by the hotels of and apartments of Play Del Ingles and Maspalomas itself. This beach has as you would expect the most facilities of any beach in the area, this beach is the conventional expectation in the Gran Canarian seafront experience. You have numerous restaurants that’s presuming you aren’t based in one of the nearby hotels as well as number of outlets for water sports and entertainment. Because it’s more structured you don’t have the same feeling of density as you can get on the more natural beaches where space becomes a premium quickly. It is also more built up by its proximity to the hotels so can feel artificial but there is just enough natural beauty on view to still be interesting and worthwhile.Recommended if you want facilities over nature.

reviews.title: At last !
reviews.text: Wow after over 3 months of waiting due to lockdown actually got to go to this fantastic beach the weather was glorious sea temperature was 75 degrees and miles of space so no social distance problems see photo can’t wait to return tomorrow

reviews.title: Impressive dunes and a lovely beach
reviews.text: My wife and I stopped here for a short visit as part of a full day cruise ship excursion. It was fun to take in the desert scenes of the sand dunes and admire the beautiful stretch of beach. We saw a large lizard in the sand too. There were public toilets at the entrance to the beach and we thought it was well worth a stop if visiting Gran Canaria.

reviews.title: A long beautiful beach, situated by the dunes. Like in the desert.
reviews.text: A long beautiful beach, situated by the dunes. Like in the desert. Naturists can feel free here and can move freely around the entire beach.

reviews.title: One week near Faro
reviews.text: The beach is awesome. There are a couple of surf schools operating from 09.30 to 12 near the rocks almost every day. The best but most dangerous place to swim is neae the rocks. During high seas the resques swimmers stick redflags around the dangerous current area.

reviews.title: Flat as a pancake
reviews.text: If you like walking or cycling but don't like it being hilly this is the place for you. We go in February and the weather is always lovely. The people are friendly and nobody bothering you its just a great place to chill. Market day is Saturday and Wednesday and at the moment they are doing an upgrade to the indoor market. There is lots to do or just chill by the pool or the fantastic beach.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Very beautiful and you feel that you are close to a desert. Touristy sellers and the stuff that is Gran Canaria, but worth a visit.

reviews.title: Best place to make cool films
reviews.text: We come back to the dunes, no matter how often we’ve been here. Amazing place to be creative with your camera: we’ve taken cool photos of our shadows in yoga poses, filmed us when digging for water.... Do it, go and play!

reviews.title: the best part of our stay in Gran Canaria
reviews.text: From walking down the path under the Hotel Rui you get the most amazing view of the dunes and sea beyond. We loved spending time around here and walking along the coast too. There are nudist areas so don't be suprised to see a few wobbly bits here and there :)

reviews.title: Maspalomas Beach
reviews.text: I spent a day on Maspalomas Beach. There are lots of different activities you could do there, including a day trip on a boat spotting dolphins.From this beach you could easily get to Las Palmas on the blue buses (number 30 or 50), and you could visit Aqualand or Palmitos Park if you have children.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: The beach at Maspalomas is huge and although busy there is plenty of space to find yourself a spot. On our week visit to Maspalomas we only visited the beach once and the sea was rough so the red flags were up and the lifeguards were patrolling and chasing people out of the water which is a good sign, they're obviously thinking of public safety.The water was pretty darn cold anyway, a paddle was sufficient for us.The sand dunes are huge and very difficult to climb but good fun all the same and the views of the dunes is spectacular.It's certainly worth a visit, I'd suggest a calm day though as you get sand blasted. Speaking of sand, we just escaped on the second last flight to leave before the airport was closed because of the Sahara sand storm.

reviews.title: Not as in pictures
reviews.text: Dunes area is really big. It’s worth visiting as it differs from other natural beauties but I have seen sand dunes before and may be that’s why I wasn’t very impressed with Maspalomas. The colour of the sand and sand itself isn’t that great as you imagine when looking at pictures on the internet or travel guides. Facilities are quite poor too. Anyway, if you haven’t experienced dunes ever - then GO!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: The beaches of maspalomas are probably the most beautiful I have ever seen miles of golden sand walk over the dunes and all you see is sand make sure you take water with you

reviews.title: Best beach in Gran Canaria
reviews.text: It has the dunes, for walking on and sliding down, and it’s a big beach. All facilities and car parking.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and dunes, in the evening we got great pictures of the sunset and the sea water was warm

reviews.title: We sufferred the sand storm!
reviews.text: we were here when the now famous sand storm of 2020 hit- Boy was that an experience- never seen anything like it!Other than that, the area is nice, and the lighthouse area is good for a stroll watching the surfers or shopping/eating out.Beware the Migrants selling their wear on the beach- most are harmless when you say no- but on the walk to the lighthouse there are a number of females who grab males and try to distract you as they try to rob you of your wallett. Only saw this done to single or groups of males, and I had to be very direct to get them to back off from myself- its a con- beware (these are all over the world too I know).

reviews.title: Lovely Beech
reviews.text: The beech in Maspalomas is lovely. It is spotlessly clean and really well looked after. It isn’t over looked by naff high rise hotels and feels very authentic.

reviews.title: A great sand adventure
reviews.text: We have stayed in Ingles and enjoyed the beach and kids playing in the Sand Dunes. So long as you don’t mind coming across a few naked bodies on the beach it’s great. I really recommend the Camel Safari.

reviews.title: Brill place
reviews.text: Maspalomas  is just fabulous. Wonderful area, great restaurants and bars. Mainly an adult venue with brill restaurants. For a winter sun destination it’s got it all

reviews.title: Winter holiday
reviews.text: We went to maspalomas beach and decided to walk through the dunes to playa de ingles ! We stuck to the path and had a lovely slow walk . It took us an hour an half and the views were amazing. Really could have been in the Sahara desert. The next time we went we went the other way and sat on the beach near the lighthouse which is also worth a visit . Lots of bars and lovely shops are near and the beach is lovely and clean well worth a visit .

reviews.title: A must see
reviews.text: You have to be reasonably fit to walk the dunes but you MUST visit if you can. The kids will love it. Take a picnic and walk to the sea. Some nudist activity but we only saw one man who was clearly a pervert. All the others were most discrete.

reviews.title: Amazing dunes
reviews.text: Peaceful, beautiful, amazingly high.  I don't think you are meant to walk on them, some people do, but I think they need to be protected. You can walk along the beach, or there is a path marked by posts between and at the back of them. But just walking around and between them should be fine, great experience.

reviews.title: Windy
reviews.text: Starting from the lighthouse there is a great walk all along the beach to Playa del Engles.It is about two miles all on sand and is very popular.It is amazing to see a constant large stream of people doing this walk every day in both directions.There is a considerable amount of nudist activity for amusement.

reviews.title: Good place to take walk on your own
reviews.text: Very nice and calm place. Especially at the evenings. I happened to visit during windy night, you should have a jacket and perhaps a face cover in this situation, since the sand is pretty smooth and goes airborne to your face and inside your clothes easily. Take some time to empty your shoes after your walkabout :)But the scenery is picturesque, take your camera with you. Free-forming sand dunes with a sea shore. Go visit.

reviews.title: Wonderful views
reviews.text: Walked from the beach from Maspalomas to Playa De Ingles. Walking on the sand quite tough although the views are worth it. Be warned there are parts that where there are naturists sunbathing and walking on the beach.

reviews.title: Bare buns !
reviews.text: Walk along the waters edge to the naturist beach to get away from the crowds, and laugh at the 'textiles' as the non nudists are called as they walk up and down for a sneak preview  (ha ha) DO NOT walk inland to the road unless you have had SAS desert survival training ! There are beach bars on the nuddy beach, but take a hand towel to put on the bar stools before you sit down (you don't know who was sitting there before you)

reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.text: We visited the Playa de Maspalomas in January this is a truly amazing experience we walked all over the dunes which was fantastic, because there were loads of private sections to stop and chill out and just take in this wonderful place.If you visit Playa Dei Ingles taking in the dunes they are awesome

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Walking from Play del Ingles in the sea to a great beach warm ish water very popular but beach so long you can pick your spot, at dusk look like Sahara, itst a nudist beach so be aware if you not happy about this, otherwise great beach, but not many facilities

reviews.title: Very windy but nice...
reviews.text: Well it’s famous for good waves and so its a bit windy there is a load of highend shops  but we just went to the beach and had a beer at paddy’s as i had been there berfor👍🏻

reviews.title: Super beach
reviews.text: One of the best beaches in the world. Main area starts from shopping-restaurant center Anexo II. You access the dunes from the beach to avoid the sea wind if you don’r rent a sunbed

reviews.title: Super clean!
reviews.text: Amazing, clean, beautiful beach with bars around and lovely views.Going around it's magical, be ready to take your water bottle!

reviews.title: Nice  each
reviews.text: Beach and some great hotels in the area  but you have to look really hard to find good food or bars unless you like McDonald’s or all day English breakfasts / Bratwursts

reviews.title: Cool place!
reviews.text: A desert closed to the ocean 👌🏜. Nice to visit and walk through the dunes down to the beach. Good work out also.

reviews.title: Another great visit
reviews.text: This is our third time here and yet it's still unspoilt. We love it here as its relaxing as it's so big you can get away from the crowds. Restaurants along the front, lovely clear sea water. Lifeguards along this beautiful beach.There is nudity, but most take no notice.

reviews.title: Maspalomas beach
reviews.text: Lovely long beach that would never get crowded. There are lots of sun beds, only 3.5 euros for the day. Great setting, very relaxing. There are lots of good bars and restaurants close by.

reviews.title: Beautiful nude beach
reviews.text: We usually take a taxi to the Playa del Ingles beach and walk to Maspalomas.... as soon as the FKK beach begins, we strip nude and walk some 5 km totally naked along the water line ... taking little breaks to dive into the waves !Around kiosk number 7 is where all the gay boy are...That’s the time for a nice cold pint of lager....After that, we stop at the Strand Apotheke... for another beer and some fun with the boys.The beach and dunes are very beautiful and the sense of freedom is amazing!

reviews.title: Beautiful beaches
reviews.text: Stunning beaches that weren’t over busy. Had a cool spot by some music to chill to. Good range of restaurants. Enjoyed watching the surfers and paddle boarders. Had a cold swim but sea was a bit rough.

reviews.title: Very good beach to spend the day
reviews.text: A nice beach with plenty of space and nearby facilities. It is a good one for families. At the end of the beach there is the nice light house.

reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.text: Great place to visit, and to take long walks around sandy beaches. Beautifully views and soft sand makes it very enjoyable

reviews.title: Great walk
reviews.text: It was a cloudy day so prompted to leave our hotel and sunbeds and walk further than the lighthouse from our Riu Gran Canaria hotel. Didn’t realise that the beach is just up from the lighthouse. Lovely huge area to walk around and good exercise climbing sand dunes.

reviews.title: Nice but windy beach
reviews.text: A nice beach but quite windy. Not the best beach on Grand Canaria but interesting one which lures many tourists. From Playa del Ingles it is about 30 minutes walk. The beach is clean, water clear but still cold otherwise perfect for children, shallow water for them to play in. The chairs and umbrella can be rented. Dunes can give you some wind protection, do not be surprised when you see some nudes in the dunes. The dunes really impressive and worth to explore.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: We visited Maspalomas with our toddler and it was really nice. The watter was okay, but I think there are better beaches on Gran Canaria, Amadores for example. There are many restaurants near the beach, that’s really convenient. It bothered us that the umbrellas and sunbeds can be rented only until 5 o clock and then they take them away, so you’re on your own after that. The beach is not so clean, it could be cleaner, especially if you’re paying for the sun beds. All in all, nice beach, but nothing special.

reviews.title: Fine beach for all
reviews.text: Wery nice beach for swiming and having good day on the beach with family and friends. There are many shops and restaurants near the beach. You can laying on the sand or pay for chairs and umbrelas, 5 Euro for 2 chairs for a day. But i dont know how much is it on the season. Our family recomanded.

reviews.title: Go elsewhere
reviews.text: The beach is ok, the sea is ok. The problem I have with the beach is that it is so windy. It's ridiculous. The sand whips up and blows in your face. Its clean, part of it is a nudist beach. I realised this when I walked up and down it.I only managed one day on the beach near the rocks for shelter. I didnt attempt to even go in the sea. It's really choppy. There is no protection from the elements here.Every day since then I have stayed by the pool as its between buildings and gets no wind.To be honest the place itself is actually pretty boring. Nothing but restaurants and shops and quite expensive really.

reviews.title: December 2018
reviews.text: Stayed at the Afa right on the beach nice hotel allocated you with a choice of sunbeds which you had for the week so no getting up early to run out with your towel went half board food good rooms very clean staff friendly only down side we were on the main square and there was some sort of festival on the person on the Mike was very loud and it went on all day and lots of people about so if you want peaceful l would check before you go it didn't spoil my holiday there are some very good restaurants close by a little expensive but the food is of a good standard

reviews.title: Fab beach
reviews.text: Lovely sandy beach it starts at the light house in melonares with lots of high end shops and restaurants and then you walk past sand sculptures artists , bag sellers and  there are big boulders and rocks this end and then a sandy beach as far as your eyes can see you can have a massage on the beach there are a few places to eat and walk in further and there are Su beds to hire and then further still are the sand dunes

reviews.title: Nice beach to relax and have fun
reviews.text: Place worth to go there and enjoy on sun and big wavee and nice male nude and unnude company.Kiosk nr. 7 have good beer and ladies there are realy funy and friendly.renting a deck chair and umbrella is very convenient.

reviews.title: Camel ride was fun
reviews.text: This was a half hour ride on a camel in baskets either side of the hump.  The camels seemed well cared for and not overworked.  Fun trip

reviews.title: Perfect day around!
reviews.text: Even if we didn't swim the dunes of Maspalomas impressed us and the bars and restaurants were all very good with quality food and drinks and not so expensive!

reviews.title: Great Beach
reviews.text: We visited Playa de Maspalomas on a beautiful sunny day with no wind. Walked alongside the ocean and across the dunes.

reviews.title: Clean and beautiful
reviews.text: The beach was surprisingly clean and the dunes were beautiful I only regret that the wind made it impossible for me to visit more time.

reviews.title: wonderful beach and landscape
reviews.text: The dunes, the ocean and the sun : three ingredients to make you feel beeing in the desert. You walk and walk through the dunes, till you reach the ocean. Simply wonderful.

reviews.title: Fantastic beach
reviews.text: 8km gold sand with sand dunes, nudist beach, gay beach with a kioszk that serves food and drinks(alcohol too).

reviews.title: An Unforgettable visit
reviews.text: Skipping this beach would be a total shame, and will always be one of the top beaches I have visited in my life.The hot hot hot sun and sand, tempered with the cool waters will stick in my mind forever.  So many people, all doing their own thing, but still feeling part of the community of beach-goers.Loved grabbing a beer from the stands along the beach, sitting back and enjoying the peoples stroll by.  An absolutely memorable day.  Can't wait to go back

reviews.title: Impressive place!
reviews.text: I never see any place like this before in my life.You visited dunes and beach at the same time!Beautiful sunset from the dunes.Not so fan from nude beach, but for a place with so many tourist maspalomas area is very clean!Just impressive!

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: This is a beautiful beach although its a bit of a trudge to get there over the sand dunes but once there the perfect place to chill out or meet new people

reviews.title: Pre-winter pick-me-up
reviews.text: ALWAYS ticks all the boxes for me. Have have been coming here since 1996 and I love coming back here 👌🏽🥰👍🏼

reviews.title: Beautiful Maspalomas
reviews.text: We have been travelling to Maspalomas for many years, and.have always found it excellent.Classy and expensive, with a fantastic seafront esplanade

reviews.title: Clean clear beach
reviews.text: Open beach, very large. Sun beds for hire. Shallow kids end for them to play. Backed by the dunes and nature reserve. Sand sculptures tend not to change, year to year. Lots of bars and shops of variable quality. Viewing platform at the faro. Apart from the African women, fewer touts this year. Sand tends to blow a bit when windy.

reviews.title: Lovely Area
reviews.text: Great place to visit in any weather, places to eat as well as sunbathe. Unfortunately the red flags were flying so didn’t get to swim

reviews.title: Very windy beach but plenty of space
reviews.text: Large, long beach very sandy. Was quite windy but Sun beds have screens to cut this down. Shopping centre near beach with many places to eat and good variety of shops.Viewing platform near light house has information on local history.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Lovely beach .You must visit it. Beach is with nice sand and very clean water. Have sand sculptures.

reviews.title: Great long beach
reviews.text: Good long beach with sand dunes and lighthouse.  Lots to see.  Sand sculptures are good.  A great museum inside the lighthouse and good views.  We walked part of the sand dunes, and lots of wildlife. Also nearby are camel rides.  Had a maasage in a small salon. Was ok, nothing special .  Sand dunes are hot.  Wear trainers, not flip flops.  Good cafes, restaurants and shopping nearby, in maspalomas too.  Lots of watersports.  Nice places to swim in the sea, and shallow enough for babes and toddlers to mess about.  Soft  orange sand.  Beautiful natural lake for birds just before the beach, below the dunes.  Protected areas all over.  Love the nature.   Would go back and stay nearer to the beach .

reviews.title: Super beach
reviews.text: Very long beach with fine sand. Very much people. In water a few. People mostly walking around ocean to next beach. At beach is good WC for 0,60 €, also is shower and lockers for service fee. Some migrants offering fake products. Cruz Roja Espaňa have here a station. Its good also walk to EL FARO Lighthouse. Beach is also watching by local police.

reviews.title: Upmarket Town
reviews.text: Very surprised with the modern, clean town, very classy with lovely buildings.  Great places to eat and a fantastic range of shops.  Lovely beach.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: Lovely beach, really clean. Sun loungers and parasols are available to rent at €2,50 per item which is good value. The only downside is there are a lot of traders trying to sell you things which can be annoying.

reviews.title: Birthday trip
reviews.text: Had 7 days in gran canaria  visited maspalomas  several times to the beach and to the oasis centre for food and drink , la Bodega , was ok although a waiter who was on a dad day made our meal uncomfortable  as he reached over us to get salt cellar  to refill  in front of us , and again   later to wipe them down while  we we drinking, he was rude, he was short fat with a squint eye , it's a shame as previously  we had a lovley meal

reviews.title: Holiday Heaven
reviews.text: I was on holiday with my wonderful wife and we visited Maspalomas everything was emaculate well kept and the people were extremely friendly would recommend it to everyone for a wonderful holiday but I do feel it is not for kids.

reviews.title: The best beach of the world
reviews.text: You can find here the best beach, the best meals, services, hotels and the very best attention from the locals.

reviews.title: Chilly day
reviews.text: Walked back towards playa des ingles from our walk in the dunes along the shore past the playa de maspalomas. Still managed to almost bump into a man with nothing on his bottom half even when it was quite chilly. Probably not a beach to bring your teenage children to unless you are comfortable with naturism as a family. To be fair it wasn’t much of a surprise as we had come across a few naturists on the other beaches already in areas where they might not have been expected.

reviews.title: A day at the beach
reviews.text: Rented 2 beach loungers and an umbrella for €7.50. Spent the day enjoying the sun and the water. We felt very safe and secure here. We had ample space and did not feel crowded even though there were hundreds of people enjoying the beach on a beautiful day in the fall.

reviews.title: Walk from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingles
reviews.text: It's about a 4 mile walk but worth the effort. You pass through family areas into nude areas and then hay areas on this walk. Some right sights to be fair ! Some people just don't care. When you get to the other end it's cocktail time and you will have earned one.

reviews.title: Good walk to the lighthouse
reviews.text: The walk along this beach to and from the lighthouse sets you up for the day. The beach is great for sun tans and water fun. If you go to Gran Canaria you should try to fit at least one day in to visit the sand dunes at the back of this beach.

reviews.title: Ideal for beach lovers
reviews.text: Spent a few hours here whilst on our Canaries Cruise.Ideal for beach lovers but little else.Everywhere really cleanSand dunes really impressive Got some excellent photos of Lizards near the beach.

reviews.title: loveley break
reviews.text: Met some lovely people and had a very relaxing, care free time. Apart from the bigoted Celtic supporter.

reviews.title: Bit of an eye opener
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with fantastic views of the mountains. Follow the kiosks along this lovely sandy beach but don't be surprised by the goings on at kiosk 4 and further down. This area is for nudists, swingers and the gay community. If u don't mind stripping diwn this is the place for u,anything goes here, however if ur a little more reserved then stay between kiosks 1 and 3,its a little more family friendly.

reviews.title: Great day at beach
reviews.text: Fantastic day, sun bed hire very reasonable.Sea was great and really nice walk on the esplanade.Great meal at beach bar.

reviews.title: Fantastic beach
reviews.text: One of the best beaches we’ve found with something for everyone On the left the Playa Des Ingles beach is as commercialised as we’ve seen with hundreds of sunbeds arranged with precision backed by a solid line of bars restaurants and shops and varied watersports available. Not to our taste but plenty seem to like it.Walking along the flat wide beach that soon shifts to introduce the world famous dunes and clothes start to become rarer until at kiosk 8 there is a naturist zone.Keep walking along and you’ll find the “gay beach” too then another naturist section at kiosk 4 then it changes again to return to a more conventional scene.Locals, tourists, families, couples, naturists, gays and straights all mix on the beach with seemingly great respect for each other. The vibe is never less than chilled. The surf is fun to play in and in October it was still warm enough to swim comfortably The dunes are well worth a visit rising behind the beach and a great photo opportunity. We visited them for both sunrise and sunset and were spellbound. Walking trails are marked so you won’t get too lost The beach after 4 miles or so ends at the Faro lighthouse and the new upmarket resort of Melonares which is good for another sunset opportunity and people watching

reviews.title: Sand dunes
reviews.text: We went for day trip by car, but we had lot of trouble finding the sand dunes, as it was not very well sign posted, but the dunes were amazing..

reviews.title: Lovely beach and dunes
reviews.text: The beach was lovely with plenty of sun loungers which were quite cheap. The dunes are close by and absolutely gorgeous!

reviews.title: Maspalomas
reviews.text: Long sandy beach (5.5 km), excellent for long walks along the waterline. Fine weather, excellent hotel (Riu Palace Oasis) with superb food, relaxed atmosphere, top service, several pools (at least one of 25m length), big rooms, absolutely clean, small but fine fitness room etc

reviews.title: Beach trip
reviews.text: The beaches are very clean and there were plenty of sun loungers.  It is a lovely walk with plenty of amenities ie shops, bars etc.  The only downside is  people trying to sell time shares and products.

reviews.title: Can't knock it
reviews.text: Thoroughly enjoying 2 weeks of lying on the gorgeous golden sands of the beaches.A couple of times the heat and lack of wind has driven me further back into the dunes for a few hours; but no great loss. ( See other dune post ).I love the gentle slope into the water - ideal for people with kids - but sometimes the waves can be big enough to reduce your attempts at "slow immersion" into one all-over drenching.  But dont worry - unless you're very small, this is not an issue.Love the touch of the beach concessionary kiosks selling anything you would expect to find in a licensed beach-front cafe.Also, the fact that you can leave your posessions on the beack, or next to a sun bed, and they will still be there when you come back.Love it; heaven.

reviews.title: Stunning dunes But busy
reviews.text: We walked along beach to the sand dunes, along with many other people! We managed to climb a small dune on our own and enjoyed the quietness and views of the sea and dunes beyond. We had to pass the naturist beach to the dunes, which might be a surprise for some, if not aware.

reviews.title: Our visit here
reviews.text: Stayed here in September 2019 for 4 days, and were so very happy with cleanlines of the beach and there was a nice atmosphere here.

reviews.title: Holiday
reviews.text: Lovely town maspalomas  sandy beach nice 9 for Under 17  lively bars:drag shows: and nightclubs .You can book your boat trips from their .we went to see the dolphins anod markets just remember to haggle lol lovely place but quiet compared to playa de ingle. The sand dunes are must you can ride camel like in desert lol I couldn't as have bad back. Their is also palimospark,and Aqualand suitable for young and old

reviews.title: Lovely and huge beach
reviews.text: The water was lovely, and wave 🌊. Really enjoyed here. Sunbed and imbrella options, 2.5 euros for each.

reviews.title: Visit to Sand Dunes
reviews.text: Myself and my boyfriend visited to walk the sand dunes. Very beautiful and it is further than you think to walk it. It was very hot when we got there and it is better to go in the morning before the hottest part of the day and take water with you. There are toilets on the walk side up to the sand dunes and cost 60 cents to use pp. Be careful though walking up the promenade, we were approached by some African ladies and one grabbed my wrist and another had my boyfriend's wrist and the third was trying to get behind us to get into our bags. They slapped friendship bands on us and demanded money and asked what for as they had done anything. We have them a few euro s for the bracelets but it all happened so fast so be careful of these ladies.

reviews.title: stunning
reviews.text: Lovely place to visit either for a long or short walk lovely beach and at one end beach bars and restaurants and cafes etc

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Third time to the island and first time to maspalomas. Beautiful scenery and people. Would recommend the camel dune ride to do on a morning when you don’t have any plans. Otherwise watching the sunset around Faro.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: If you're looking for a relaxing beach, this isn't the place for you. Being on the  Atlantic the sea was very cold. There were many lifeguards patrolling the beach due to the massive waves from the sea, they were stopping people going beyond waist height.The sand is very soft, few pebbles but incredibly hot, could not walk barefoot.€7.50 to rent 2 loungers and a parasol which isn't bad. However, public toilets were a long walk away and charged 50 cents.

reviews.title: Stroll
reviews.text: A beautiful beach and promenade to wander along at a leisurely pace Lots of up market shops if you fancy some new jewellery or clothes and if hungry a great selection of goods restaurants to pick from

reviews.title: a very pretty island with beautiful mountain roads
reviews.text: the touristy areas cater to the elderly and gay people mainly and are nothing much to write home about. I was tired of this very soon. I then rented a car and drove into the mountains where I discovered a very different region with challenging roads, unspoiled nature (although a bit of damage from intentionally set fires was to be seen), friendly people and cosy little restaurants and bars.

reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.text: It was amazing hanging out at this beach .I was here for 2 weeks .the weather and the water temperature was amazing. Sometimes me and my husband even took long walk along the coast and it’s was so nice! Also at night ...this beach is Amzing!

reviews.title: Wonderful sandy beach & dunes.
reviews.text: The long sandy beach and inland extensive sand dunes just east of Maspalomas lighthouse “Faro” and running ca 3 miles to the east at Playa del Ingles are a real treat. This is the southernmost tip of the island of Gran Canaria. The sand is clean and the water very good for swimming as it shelves gradually.There is a reasonable tidal drop that means that the beach area does shrink at high tide but at low tides there is a very great deal of space for everyone. It is busy with strollers but the vast area copes easily.The beach and dune area has been well protected from over commercialisation in direct contrast to the 2 neighbouring towns at either end that are rather a large sprawl.There are occasional small huts selling drinks and there are some lifeguard spots as well as a couple of sections of beach with nude bathers.  Public buses , service 39, run close to either end and so you can easily make it a one direction walk or a there & back trek.Similarly it is easy to reach Maspalomas by bus from the Ressorts along the south of Gran Canaria and hourly from SAN Telmo bus terminus in Las Palmas, with bus Service 50.Walking over the dunes area is tiring and very hot but along the waterline is great.Highly recommended beach but just be aware this is a busy, not a secluded, place.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Beautiful place and absolutely stunning views.You could be on another planet, it is windy but that doesnt matter, it's a lovely but long walk between maspalomas and melonares.

reviews.title: OK for a quick wander
reviews.text: An ok place for a quick wander along the sea front. The sand dunes look interesting. The lighthouse is a landmark which you’re not allowed up which was a shame. Glad to have been there but wouldn’t rush back

reviews.title: Nice couple of hours
reviews.text: Heard quite a bit about this oasis. Wasn't disappointed the views are wonderful. As mentioned in other posts. There is a lack of clothing area that might put a few people off. But if you keep eyes on the dunes you will be fine.

reviews.title: Fabulous
reviews.text: If you love beach holidays then this is the place to be. Fantastic sandy beach, the sand dunes are so picturesque. Lovely shopping and bars.

reviews.title: Be aware
