reviews.text: Gorgeous beach but be aware towards the dunes end it becomes clothing optional shall we say was walking with my partner and 2 daughter's aged 18 and 10 and suddenly an old man walking out of sea naked 5 mins later a lady then another 5 and passed 2 men obviously had to cover wee ones eyes a bit embarrassing other than that gorgeous beach beautiful scultures and nice bars and shops

reviews.title: Beach day
reviews.text: Lovely beach 10 minutes away from where we were staying, plenty of restaurants and bars in the front with lots of choice...

reviews.title: Beautiful clean beach and sand dunes
reviews.text: We spent many days on the beach here. Lovely and clean though the dark sand stuck to your feet and legs! Sun beds and umbrella reasonable to hire and sea cooling for a paddle though a bit rough to swim.

reviews.title: Almost a Dessert
reviews.text: A desert in the middle of the island. A beautiful and gigantic beach where you can get lost among its dunes.

reviews.title: Just like being in the desert
reviews.text: Fantastic place makes you feel you are in the Sahara desert. Great peacfull location to sit and relax

reviews.title: real gem
reviews.text: stunning place to see, great views, great for a long walk, just make sure you have a decent shoes (sand is very hot!) and lots to drink!!

reviews.title: Amazing to see - Well worth the visit
reviews.text: We walked to the visitor centre by the Riu Hotel, there are information boards and toilets. You can then access the paths to the beach and take those amazing photos.  It was very hot and windy, the sand is burning hot and it is extremely hard work walking up and down the dunes! But you've got to do it because it is simply amazing to see.We also walked along the edge of the dunes by the sea from Playa del Ingles to Meloneras. This is a pleasant walk and gives a different perspective of the dunes, it took us about an hour but you might want to keep your eyes on the sea or sky when passing nudists :-)

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Definitely must see when on gran canaria, just be careful, sand is really hot!! Stunning place,!!!!!

reviews.title: Incredible small desert - worth to see.
reviews.text: Take your slippers, because the sand is really hot before 6 pm. You will have to pay 7 EUR for the beds and parasols - what the supervisor guy will take away at 5 pm. Ridiculous :) So does not worth to pay for them at 4:40 :)

reviews.title: Sand dunes
reviews.text: We went later in the evening, the “golden hour “ to take fab photos with the lighting just right and the temperature cooler. Magnificent .

reviews.title: Good facilities but rocky
reviews.text: NIce waves, good facilities safe but rocky beach so be careful otherwise easy to get injured. They have first aid and toilets which only operate till 17.00

reviews.title: Good place but be careful near the dunes
reviews.text: The walk along the front next to the nature reserve and the dunes is beautiful but be warned there are several African ladies that will ask you where you are from then offer to shake your hand. DO NOT EXTEND YOUR HAND . Ignore them. They will tie a piece of string around your wrist , chant a prayer and then demand money (the string is worth about fifty cents but these women wanted 20 euros !) Then become aggressive when you refuse. Just walk on by don't even give these "soft muggers" the courteousy of a no thanks. Why the local authorities do not intervene is beyond me.The main shopping area across the street from the bus station is really nice with PROPER shops and not those tacky market stalls you see all over the Canaries. There are some nice places go eat and drink at reasonable prices and there is also a casino is that's your thing.

reviews.title: Nice sandy beach
reviews.text: It’s a nice sandy beach that’s quite big/long. There’s plenty of sun beds throughout the beach but it’s best to be there early to get one. There are some stones in the water so you have to be careful. With big waves you do have to go a bit further to have cleaner water as just on the beach loose black sand mixes with water and it doesn’t look nice especially when it lands in your mouth. Nice for long walks.

reviews.title: Crowdy tourist spot
reviews.text: Typical tourist spot, head over head all day. Restaurants on the beach are aware of this and setting price high for mediocre quality at best. In the evening the main square in front of parking lot gets crowded with sunglasses dealers but they will offer you drugs instead. By their behavior I guess the man with leather belts holds the stash for other dealers. If you want calm and cozy time, head for San Agustín, Meloneras or Puerto de Mogan.

reviews.title: Excellent beach
reviews.text: Excellent beach in Maspalomas, near the wonderful dunes. Very good and quiet for families with children or teens.

reviews.title: Lovely place to visit.
reviews.text: Lovely promenade to stroll along and good range of shops including designer shops. Beach clean and not too crammed.

reviews.title: We loved the beach
reviews.text: I think we took the longest walk to the beach, the sand burned our feet, but the experience was amazing! And the waves were nice, the kid had so much fun, and so did we! Is a mixed beach, which was a bit weird as we had to explain the kid why some grownups were naked, but he moved on quick,  understanding is a personal choice.We will deffo return there without the kid ;)

reviews.title: Stunning views
reviews.text: This beach is stunningSand on beach does get very hot so I would recommend wearing flip flops Sun loungers to hire for the day is €7 euros each

reviews.title: Family holiday
reviews.text: Walked down here many times with my family. Lot’s of restaurants, good beach, friendly people. Good taxi links. Clean and well staffed everywhere. I would recommend this resort to anyone.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beach is very beautiful, if you walk alongside the shore in direction of playa de Ingles, you will find way less people there. There is long nudist area as well as gay area. You have beautiful view on dunes from the middle of the beach

reviews.title: Getting to the beach is more fun than the beach
reviews.text: While the Maspolamas beach is just ordinary imo, long one with much shallow water when entering, reaching it was great.You can reach it on foot from the most visited Playa del Ingles, which is quite ordinary, or you can park somewhere around the RIU palace hotel and walk over the dunes.The latter is much more adventurous and you'll make perfect pics along the way.The scenery when walking from the RIU hotel is like you're in Sahara or any real desert (many desert themed movies were shot here). So many dunes with the blue sea in the background make a perfect contrast.Beware, from the hotel to the beach there's at least 30 min to 60 min walk depending on your physical condition and how often you stop for pics. Dress accordingly, is burning there, put a hat, sunscreen and bring water with you.

reviews.title: Well it’s changed!
reviews.text: Not been in years, It’s so much better than it was, high end shops high end restaurants. The front has really been done up, don’t miss a drink in maximillions on the front.

reviews.title: Beach day
reviews.text: Beach is nice and clean however when me and my wife took a walk there was lots of naked men sunbathing on the beach. I was aware that they had a section on the beach but guys standing at the waters edge hands on hips with all on show is not a very nice sight.

reviews.title: Beautiful dunes on the southern tip of GC
reviews.text: Accessible from Playa Ingles, Meloneras and Hotel Riu Palace, it's a spectacular area of natural beauty.  You can set off from either end or in the middle.  The beach is walkable from one end to the other but it is a fair distance and is approximately 5KM from one end to the other (10KM return).  There is an area about half way that has a lot of stones and soft sand that makes walking difficult but generally, it's an easy walk.  There's something for everyone on the walk including beaches with bars/cafes and toilets

reviews.title: Wonderful
reviews.text: Another grand tourist centre with loads of shops, restaurants and bars along its promenade. The beach starts from the lighthouse with its name changing to Playa del Ingles at a turn, where the FKK zone is. Combined with the marvellous dunes of golden sand in the backdrop, the beach is just spectacular with sections where you can rent sun loungers and parasols.

reviews.title: Super
reviews.text: It is a very beautifull beach with fine sand. The ocean in front and the sand dunes in the back make a perfect combination. It was a nice experience

reviews.title: First time Nudist
reviews.text: My wife and I decided to have a reconoitre of the various different parts of the beach to see what was for us and, what wasn't!The next day, we decided to base ourselves just inside the nudist section near kiosk 5. Swim shorts stayed on but the next I day i took the plunge and never looked back! This is a great, chilled beach with people of all different ages, sizes etc. No judgement just chilling... Naked.

reviews.title: Very hot day....
reviews.text: Trip to see the sand dunes in 29 degrees heat. Remember to take lots of water and a big floppy hat. Maspalomas is one way a o the taxi drops you off near the Lighthouse area then you take the promenade past the Nature Reserve and the lagoon area to get to the taxi rank for your return trip. The best place to see the dunes is to the left by walking actually on the beach but it was too hot for us. The shady area near the Nature Reserve was very welcome. You will see the sand art and pebble art along the way but beware of taking photographs without any small change. One woman was very nasty and I only had notes left. The art work will have taken them hours so understandable. A good day out.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Watch out the sand gets really hot! And you have to pay to use the loos ( but at least they are clean and have loo paper) the hire of sunbeds are at a reasonable price. Annoying that you have to keep telling sales/massage ladies no thank you all the time, but you get that everywhere. Overall nice beach, great views. 👍

reviews.title: Great place
reviews.text: Lovely clean beachLoads of shopsGreat foodDefo worth a visit loads to do for all.  Some beautiful buildings .

reviews.title: Big beautiful beach
reviews.text: Playa the Maspalomas is a great beach, a lot of space and big waves, we really enjoined our days there

reviews.title: Very Nice Beach
reviews.text: We have visited several beaches in the two weeks we have been here but have made three trips to this particular beach.  From the beaches we have visited this one has more waves and much more room to enjoy the sun without someone being in your space. Chair rentals are cheaper here as well but parking can be a little expensive.

reviews.title: Scam/con
reviews.text: Caribbean women along the walk to the beach conned me and my boyfriend of 10€ they was horrible and persistent and demanded money they started saying loads of spiritual rubbish and wasn’t happy with a bit of change they wanted 5 euro each. BE AWARE. I hope they get caught and fined!!!!

reviews.title: Dunes
reviews.text: Dunes are not so impressive like those on Fuerteventura but stil lhave a decent desert vibe. Good for walking and wondering. Good tip to have a cash with you- bars on the beach do not accept card payments- you might dry out until you get to closest shop. Also found all beach loungers reallllllyyyy far from road so it might be a bit of challenge to get there in a full sun.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: This area of Gran Canaria is beautiful. The lovely beach with the port and plenty of things to do in the vicinity. It's worth a day trip if you arrive by cruise ship.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text: We went to this place on a recommendation. It was well worth it. Fun to walk through and take pics. The kids did a roll down the dunes and we took a slow motion vid.We managed to get to the beach and there was a hit there selling drinks and snacks at a reasonable price. Not a place to swim though and a few nudes just wondering around.I would recommend wearing shoes as the sand is hot and bring water to drink.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: Went to the beach with my children. You could hire longer and parasols - 2 loungers and 1 parasol for 7.50 euros.The beach was clean and safe to paddle on and many even ventured a lot further from the shore.We spent a few fun hours here.

reviews.title: Very nice!
reviews.text: Got the free bus from our hotel to here. It seems that a lot of hotels offer the free shuttle bus, so defiantly take one to get here. Beach is nice, plenty of shops. There is a shopping Center not far from the light house. There is also plenty of place to sit down to chill for a beer or some food.Only things to watch out are there are plenty of ppl trying to sell you knock off stuff in and around the beach area.Some nice hotels around the beach area whether if I would stay in them I’m not too sure.

reviews.title: Fabulous
reviews.text: What a fabulous beach area, apart from the hassle of people trying to sell cheap knock offs, the area is otherwise lovely to stroll along.

reviews.title: What a Beach
reviews.text: Best Beach I have seen goes on forever ,very clean, very organized,noticed Red Cross/Police patrols,nice bars restaurants close by and not too expensive, well worth a visit..

reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.text: From when I was hear a few years ago some of the beach has gone and is now full of rocks there isn't much on the sea front anymore playa de ingles has best beach front now

reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.text: It is a quite but lively place depending upon what you want to do -dunes and beach is attractive followed by shopping centres and yeah good for water sports too..

reviews.title: Fantastic shopping
reviews.text: What a beautiful place!  Shops are so tempting, with latest fashions, there are so many choices...not only clothes! Cafes and bars and restaurants ! All very well kept! The beach is very long and it can be very crowded ! Dunes are something out of this place...just Wauuu!The promenade is also nice if it is not too hot! Here you spend the whole day....

reviews.title: Holiday
reviews.text: Have been coming to playa de ingles for several years but have started to notice how dirty it is becoming compared to other resorts on the island,pavements are stinking all around resort and the promenade is just as bad the whole lot could do with a good power wash,there is a lot of building work going on all over resort so expect a lot of noise,yumbo center is very clean but the kasbah centre is very run down,overall with the amount of money from tourism you would expect the place to be clean.

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: A great beach people seem to mix up the dune area with this smaller beach just a Melonaris a beautiful cove where relaxation is the key to the enjoyment . unfortunately over the years we have been sunbathing there it has become very popular but this wont stop us coming back

reviews.title: Absolutely stunning area
reviews.text: If you like shopping in quality shops and just lounging about in nice restaurants and cafes, then this is the place to come. Most of the hotels run free buses regularly to this beautiful part of Gran Canaria, and rightly so. The shopping plaza is a leisurely 10 minute walk away from the bus stop, with plenty of cafes and bars scattered along the way. This is probably a good time also to check out some of the other 4 and 5 star hotels in this area as we did, because, I’m sure you will want to return to this area, as we will, in the future.The beach is massively long, and can be very tiring in a hot day, and was absolutely jam-packed when we arrived. The dunes are well worth a look, and you will see plenty of birds in the lagoon area if you are a birdwatcher. It is extremely tiring walking along the fine sand in the dune area, but you must go there to appreciate the beauty of this place.There is also a long promenade, taking you past the shops and the lighthouse. I don’t know if you can go to the top of it though. But it’s a beautiful walk if it’s not too hot when you arrive.Must be in the top 3 areas in Gran Canaria to visit, if not number 1!

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: This is a excellent beach it goes on for milesThere are nice little coves at one end and the dunes at the other in between there is sandy beach.The sunbeds are packed close together but you can always find one and are the cheapest we have come across in are travels 7.50 Euro for two beds and an umbrella

reviews.title: Iconic and impressive dunes
reviews.text: Located between Meloneras and Playa del Ingles, against a backdrop of 10m high dunes, this 8km long 3.5km wide stretch of clean fine golden sand shelves gently into the sea for the most part. It has sunbeds and parasols for hire, showers, pay toilets and several beach bars, plus there are plenty of restaurants and shops in the two resorts at either end. There is a lifeguard and plenty of patrols. Understandably it can get very busy - popular with sun-worshippers, walkers and wind-surfers. There are two designated naturist areas (between beach bars 3 and 6). There are more hawkers here than in the main Melonares resort.

reviews.title: Tired  horrible , tacky Orange loungers ..
reviews.text: Came here for a day .Cheap beds and umbrella  but dear me .they are tatty work out and embarassing. Then a trek to find a toilet .. I asked several bars & restaurants to use theirs " no " as beaches go it's sand but facilities are shocking. Then the constant harassment of foot massage African sunglass sellers. A tired beach for a tired resort. Compare this to say Salou or even ones in Rhodes  , this is a tatty .." let's squeeze every last euro out of the gulible" beach and resort.

reviews.title: Immaculate beach area
reviews.text: Huge sandy beach. Very clean. Early each morning the local council descends on it to clean and rake the beach. The only thing they seem to miss is cigarette butts. Blue flag for 20 years. Yellow sand with some black volcanic specks so it can get hot. Some areas have smooth sand going out to sea. Some have hidden volcanic outcrops hard under foot.  Plenty of beach bars. Serviced by lifeguards and the obligatory coloured flag system. Pair of loungers and umbrella €7.50 for a day.  Quite windy.  One of the best beaches I’ve been on.

reviews.title: Sunbathing spot
reviews.text: Take a walk along the beach.fantastic have a swim then soak up the sun.beware a bit further along the beach towards the dunes the beach is a nudists beach.seemed to be mainly men more like Adam and Steve than Adam and eve.

reviews.title: lovely beach !
reviews.text: Very nice, large beach ! Smooth entry into the oceana lot of restaurants  with good food and good prices, bar on the beach, sunbeds. You'll find everything you need !

reviews.title: Nice sunbeds
reviews.text: I can’t give this beach more than three stars because the shore is extremely rocky, and a little roughThe beach itself was wonderful - very wide with great sandRental of an umbrella and two lounge chairs were around eight euros for the dayTons of great places to eat nearby and great people watching a very nice day

reviews.title: Day trip
reviews.text: Booked this trip locally from tourito through tui the sand dunes here go on for miles we also had a camel ride quite good I felt like Lawrence of Arabia quite good fun and not that expensive

reviews.title: A beach!
reviews.text: Enormous beach.What more does any child want - sun, sand, sea, waves.Great place to spend an afternoon.  Plenty of seafront restaurants.   Showers and sun loungers available.Areas further away from the lighthouse are naturist and LGBT friendly.

reviews.title: Incredible beach!
reviews.text: What can I say, everything you would want from a beach! Plenty of space, shallow water for a long walk out. No pesky pebbles!The sand is extremely fine and so gets into everywhere!!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: During our recent holiday we walked from Maspalomas to Playa del Ingels along the beach- we visited the refreshment huts no 1-7 along the way and also “climbed!” Several dunes then dipping our feet enroute- the beach is beautiful & clean & & was very busy with likeminded people walking along the beach- it is a worthwhile visit if your staying in the area with plenty to do with many beachside bars

reviews.title: lots of space i the sun for all, nudist and textile
reviews.text: we walked the beach from the lighthouse to playa des ingles the day we arrived, enjoying toes in the water as we walked. lots of people around as it was the start of the Easter weekend, Went back the next day to sample the nudist areas, lots of room here and free from the noise of someone else's children! we pitched camp between the gay area and the nudist section, lots of room, clean fine sand, and a nice breeze to keep the heat down a little.  the drinks cabins are very welcome as are the proper toilets at the gay beach.  we have been to a few places on our travels round the island that as soon as you step round the corner there are little piles of toilet paper, very sad really.back there again today so we shall see how it is again.

reviews.title: A nice walk
reviews.text: Lovely sand dunes and a lovely walk along to the lighthouse, some great pics taken from up in the lighthouse and some nice restaurants along the promenade. Lots of people trying to sell you things and keep going on at you and then the same ones will be back! If you like knock off sunnies and watches then that’s fine! Nice place and it’s also a protected nature reserve.

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: Third year I have been back to Masapolomas beach and love it even more. Bonus going later than before as sea warm enough to swim in. The dunes are as spectacular as ever and for the first time we walked all the way to Playa De Ingles which was awesome. There are a lot of people walking but there is so much room! There is a nude beach, gay beach and a large beach where families and others sunbathe. All very liberal, all very chilled and a really nice vibe. Plenty shops nearby if you want a break.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Great beach and facilities.  Do not tackle the sand dunes in flip flops!! A must beach if visiting Gran Canaria.

reviews.title: WARMEST PLACE
reviews.text: This is the best place to be (weather-wise) in the island. With plenty of large hotels and private apartments to stay. Here you will find sandy beach and all facilities that is needed for a nice and relaxed holidays.

reviews.title: An excellent beach backing onto the dunes
reviews.text: When you leave the Faro you pass a plush hotel and many restaurants and bars before you reach the open area of the beach.  There are a number of sand sculptures to extract money from the tourists. I thought the most impressive was the one of Shrek and Fiona and other characters from the films. There are also bag sellers (Tunisian?) pestering the visitors. The beach itself is very extensive and great for a swim.

reviews.title: Golden sands!
reviews.text: Arrived by hire car at Playa de Maspalomas and parked in the under cover municipal car park (half a mile) near the bus terminal, after driving around for a while closer to the beach but not a parking space to be had. I think the car park worked out at about 1€ an hour. Approached the beach by the lighthouse (Faro - worth a visit) and then along the boardwalk past a succession of breach shops, cafes and restaurants. Looking towards Playa del Ingles across the beach you can see the beginning of the famous sand dunes. There are sun beds and shades for hire along the beach and its patrolled by lifeguards. You may need to beware of the nudist beach somewhere between the two resorts as we did come across an elderly gentleman walking along 'au naturel '.

reviews.title: Beachtime
reviews.text: Close to Playa Meloneras and has a lot of stores and restaurants close to the beach. Easy to get here with bus or taxi. It was quite windy on the beach though. The dunes start close to the beach which were funny to fool around on.

reviews.title: Loved the beach, clean and vast!
reviews.text: Great for walking and the small Wales were fun for kids and adults. Sorry we forgot the boogie board! Really peaceful, suggest you bring your own shade! Fantastic shower and feet Washing facilities and lots of nice cafes and shops and restaurants nearby. Felt very safe, kids enjoyed playing on the beach and in the dunes.

reviews.title: A very pleasant beach and very long from Playa de maspalomas all the way to Faro de maspalomas,
reviews.text: When you get to the beach front there's a good size shopping bizzar area and a lot of eateries opposite, you will see a lot being hundreds and hundreds of people walking South along the sand's to a very nice little new resort called Faro de, follow them, But be warned you will pass a couple of nudist beach area's, it's a good hour and 3/5 steady walk and Faro has a lot to offer, shops eateries rest areas, sand castle works of art, the beach is not as the Mediterranean, being Chrystal clear water and white sands but good to walk on, apparently it's a daily ritual from one town to another, keep fit for all, will post some pictures, well worth going to if you get the chance,

reviews.title: Superb sandy beach
reviews.text: Famous for its sand dunes and it is easy to see why. The dunes are part of an extensive beach which is very popular for beach walkers. There are some sun loungers and parasols available for hire at various spots along the beach.As well as sand dunes this area is also well known for its nudist area which is close to the area of the dunes.

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: Lucky to be staying at the RIU Oasis so we could walk every day to the Dunes that are simply stunning. However there is a nudist bathing area you have to pass through were gentlemen of a senior age enjoy wandering around in the buff..!!

reviews.title: M Taylor
reviews.text: Worth a visit but not a great experience to be honest, unless you like sand dunes.  A nature reserve is just around the corner.

reviews.title: Great view of the dunes
reviews.text: Nice place to sit and relax at the beach as well as great views of the dunes. Also plenty of bars and restaurants. We just spent the day on the sun lounger - about €7.50 for 2 sun loungers and an umbrella if I remember correctly! Only downside not much parking nearby, we found a pay and display car park that is about 10/15 minutes walk from the beach in the end.

reviews.title: Nomads on something like Sahara
reviews.text: Here you have a smooth feeling of Africa, warm wind and a lot of space to hide. Be careful of hot sands.

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: Long wide beach, hot sunshine even in March. Singers and umbrellas for hire. Toilets down long flight of stairs -60 cents. Nearby dunes,camels and nature reserve all worth seeing.

reviews.title: Everything you need for a relaxing holiday
reviews.text: This area is absolutely beautiful, the beaches are well maintained, plenty of security patrols to keep you and your belongings safe. The golden sand stretches for miles.The sea is a little choppy but very clean.  There's plenty of restaurants for all tastes, serving qood quality food.Plenty of activities for all ages. There's plenty of good quality hotels and apartments to stay in, to suit your holiday needs.The weather's brilliant all year round.Everyone's really friendly.100% in my opinion.

reviews.title: Avoid  the lookie lookie people
reviews.text: Do not get reeled in by African women who start talking to you ..before you know it they grab you're hand tie a crappy bit of shoe lace round your wrist ,and try to get €10 each of you.. avoid or tell to f**k  right off

reviews.title: Vast beach and dunes
reviews.text: Like a little bit of the Sahara, this beach sits in front of a huge area of sand dunes in front of Meloneras, Maspalomas and Playa del Ingles. You can walk all the way between Meloneras and Playa del Ingles and it's a very pleasant walk, although you will see many naturists. It's a very relaxed, anything goes kind of place.It can get windy though and with all that fine sand it can get a little unpleasant at times but this only affected a single morning of my entire holiday. The rest of the time we had clear blue skies and temperatures in the high 20s even though it was mid-March,

reviews.title: Maspalomas Dunes
reviews.text: Just back from Gran Canaria, we were staying close to the Maspalomas dunes which are definitely worth a closer look. We had absolutely fantastic weather for March with the temperatures everyday between 26°/27° and even hitting 30°. Walking across the dunes is spectacular the nearest thing to being in the desert. We even saw a couple getting married there. Well worth the visit.

reviews.title: Walking in Maspalomas Beach area
reviews.text: Breathtaking views out across the Atlantic ocean, some days the sea had plenty of waves for the surf boarders, on other days, it was fairly calm. The paved walking areas are in good repair. Lots of natural plants & grassed areas. Cafes & restaurants aplenty, along with shops, some souvenir, some more upmarket. Some hotels also along this stretch. A pleasant walk. Taxi's are reasonably priced

reviews.title: Long walk
reviews.text: The beach is fine but walking from the lighthouse it quickly changes from families to naturists and that may not be to everyone’s taste. If the naturist element doesn’t bother you, it’s a lovely walk.

reviews.title: beaufiful food
reviews.text: we found this restauraunt on trip advisor and decided to give it a go. it was fantastic food and very good value for money. ate there twice over a week.thank god got this one spot on with other reviews

reviews.title: Over rated
reviews.text: Supposedly lovely vast sandy beach suitable for everyone. Actually a crowded windy sand blasted hell on earth with dangerous bathing conditions. Sit by your pool with your G & T and save the €15 rip off for faded broken uncomfortable sun beds and ripped umbrella.......miles to the nearest toilet - you can imagine the smell of urine actually makes your eyes water .....

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, especially walking downFrom playa del ingles. Worth a visit. It is a long walk from the dunes to the waters edge though so bring water.

reviews.title: Huge busy beach.
reviews.text: Large beach with lots of people but still room for more. If you want a quiet drink worth walking past the lighthouse onto the promenade. Some good sand sculptures on the way!

reviews.title: Wedding Anniversary Holiday
reviews.text: Lovely place,very clean lovely views over the dunes .  Great restaurants on the esplanade . Nice friendly beach bars . Great views .

reviews.title: Great place,
reviews.text: We went late February early March, great weather, not too crowded,but enough people to create a good atmosphere. Good food, very impressed that the restaurant staff didn’t drag you into place like some resorts.Hopped on and off the local buses found them very reasonable and efficient. Visited Morgan and Last Palmas old town, great days out.

reviews.title: Anniversary Break
reviews.text: Went to Gran Canaria for wedding anniversary this year. Stayed in Maspolomas. New and vibrant town. Very clean. Good soft sandy beach at Playa de Maspolomas with smaller sandy beach further up at Playa de Melonares. Good beaches with plenty of room in March. Could get packed in Summer.

reviews.title: Massive beach
reviews.text: This beach has lovely clean sand and sea. The sunbeds can only be hired in twos for 7 euros so beware if you are on your own or if there are 3 of you. They will still charge you for 2 or 4. We just took towels down to lay on a nd saved our money. If you walk down towards the dunes end of the beach it can be very windy but the dunes are worth exploring. Around the headland there are naked sunbathers and also a gay beach around a small beach cafe, Because there is so much beach there is room for everyone but if you prefer not to be near the nudists, then just don't venture near the headland.

reviews.title: Out of this world
reviews.text: Wonderful beach, clean and peaceful.  Walking the dunes was an eye opener if you went too far in! :-)

reviews.title: Short break away
reviews.text: Maspalomas has a nice beach with lots of bars, restaurants and shops. However, you are hastled constantly while walking around by African men trying to sell tat or African women who corner you and attempt to tie bracelets on your wrist and then force you to give them money. It doesn't stop while you're sat in a bar or cafe either. They will walk up to your table and try and sell things to you. Even if you say no over and over again they keep coming back. I feel like this let the holiday down. It was supposed to be a nice relaxing break away but any time we went for a walk we were constantly hastled and regretted leaving our hotel. I wouldn't revisit Gran Canaria again because of this.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: Beach is beautiful and the nice restaurants overlooking the sea and a few nice designer shops near the lighthouse and taxis are so cheap

reviews.title: Fantastic -  Sahara by the sea
reviews.text: Wonderful walk through the dunes from Playa Ingles to Maspalomas. Great fun scooting down the high sand dunes then dipping your toes in the sea as you walk back. Takes about an hour each way at a steady stroll

reviews.title: FANTASTIC
reviews.text: Visited the dunes of Maspalomas and was really taken by the environment and atmosphere, so much so,I hope to return in 2019.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: Lovely beach and and nice day out walking down the shops and the beach , when u get past the shops the scenery completely changes and looks like a scene out of a movie

reviews.title: great beach to walk and walk and walk
reviews.text: Large beach where one can sit and enjoy the ocean, the sand, the people watching without feeling crammed in

reviews.title: then you're in the dessert, then you're not
reviews.text: Go through there, it's absolutely special. Sometimes you are surrounded by only barren dunes, in a blazing sun and it's like you're in the Sahara And next you are walking among trees & bushes and it's completely different. Only thing were the solitairy men, looking for other men... that was a bit creepy, at times...

reviews.title: The Naturalists & The Perverts
reviews.text: We went to looks at the famous sand dunes at Maspalomas. After reading the guide books we thought it was a must see. We went with our two boys - 7 & 9yrs old. We parked near the Santa Monica suite hotel. It’s beautiful to look out across the dunes - our kids were super excited, they ran towards the water, up and down the dunes. However, when we got close to the shore they said “Mommy some people aren’t wearing any clothes?”  I said “Ya, I think you don’t have to wear clothes on this beach.” THEY WERE TOTALLY NONPLUSSED. We are open with our kids and they don’t care about nudity NOR DO WE. I knew from the guide books there was a nudist area- I didn’t think anything of it.HOWEVER THERE IS DEFINITELY A SEEDY ELEMENT TO THIS PART OF THE BEACH. Single men walking around in various states of arousal is NOT appropriate for children. There was one man in particular that was being quite the exhibitionist. Also there were 1000s of people walking up and down the shoreline. It was like being in Oxford Circus on a Saturday. It was just not a pleasant place to go even if you went without kids. Perhaps we landed at the wrong end of the beach. More research is needed before I’d be tempted back. I am guessing the only reason you might go here is to meet other like-minded people- hey have fun- no judgement but IT’S DEFINITELY NOT SUITABLE  FOR KIDS!

reviews.title: Sahara Dunes and Kitesurf
reviews.text: An amazing walk through sand dunes until you get to Maspalomas or Playa del Inglés (both beaches connected at walk distance).    You can take a sunbath, play paddle, enjoy drinks and cocktails or if you like watersports,  it´s the ideal place to stir up your kite and go Kitesurfing.  The kite community is very open and friendly (specialy open to tourists). You will not find a close beach with such a great space, view, sun and wind to do any activity.   After your beach day, simply walk towards the parking lot and you can find a Mc Donalds with Fast Free Internet. :)

reviews.title: A lovely walk
reviews.text: My husband and I enjoyed a lovely walk from Maspalomas along to Play Del Ingles. The beach is very clean for the amount of people using it. There is A LOT of nudists on the beach but you can still enjoy the lovely walk. If you like sunbathing nude this is the place to be! :-)

reviews.title: It's huge!
reviews.text: Huuuuuuge beach with plenty of space, loved having a look at the dunes. Just wish it wasn't so difficult to walk all the way along and up and down the dunes - it was exhausting in the winter sun.

reviews.title: Dunas de Maspalomas
reviews.text: If you are ever in Grand Canaria, Dunas de Maspalomas it’s a must . Make sure you have water with you and maybe a snak. Great views when you make it to the top

reviews.title: Nice day out
reviews.text: Nice day out. The dunes are impressive and should be seen. It does get extremely busy. If you wander too far keep an open mind as the last third is nudist ( go when it’s cold for a laugh). Various places you can park apart from the pay and display car park if you don’t mind a walk.

reviews.title: Natural phenomenon
reviews.text: The dunes are easily accessible from maspolonas beach. The dunes are impressive and there is a beautiful lagoon to watch birds. The dunes also form part of a nudist beach. If you do not want to walk camel rides are available near by.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Lovely beach and there is an ice cream hut there too. Lots of naked Germans and others there. Its much nicer and quieter than the beaches by the Faro de Maspalomas or the Playa des Ingles

reviews.title: Visiting desert
reviews.text: Pretty cool place. Just magnificent how in such a small island there can be so much different environments. This place as well is just perfect for everyone who would love to make great n outstanding photos. Colours, background and view is just screaming good.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach area, long sandy beaches
reviews.text: Very sandy beach, great for walking. Also with lots of places to sit and sip and watch the world go by.

reviews.title: Depends on what you want
reviews.text: Walked over the dunes from the Rui hotel.It can feel like a lot of effort to get to the shoreline! In the dunes you will see guys ‘lurking’ but they do seem to keep themselves to themselves I only stayed at the beach for around an hour as the wind was so strong it was blowing the sand around.

reviews.title: Stunning.
reviews.text: The sand dunnes are amazing,  you can take the walk way by the rui hotel in maspalomas and walk to playa del ingles and marvel at a wonderful creation.

reviews.title: Fantastic sand dunes
reviews.text: Extreme dunes just by the sea in Maspalomas. Like a small dessert.very Nice to walk in or just to look at.

reviews.title: This place is a Must Do - once in your life experience
reviews.text: We have been to Playa del Ingles several times and each time we have a visit to the dunes.Chill by the beach then wander round to the Dunes area - we tend to do it "Mad Dogs & Englishmen times" - as in early afternoon !January 2019 - this visits attire involved a pair of shorts and a smile - bad idea :)The sand gets warmer the further you go into the dunes !!I was on my own so simply followed a previous explorers footprints - turns out that the tops of the dunes all meet at some point so its hard to retrace your own steps :)After about 1/2 hour of a track I found my way back to civilisation (Kiosk 4 I think it was) - a cold beer and a treck back to the main beach at Playa del Ingles and I was reunited with my wife who welcomed me with a smile and a beer from one of the numerous kiosks along the beach !The dunes are amazing - do it - but wear Flip Flops at least :)

reviews.title: Natural reserved dune area
reviews.text: Beach without any hotel at the coastline. Nice to have a walk from Playa del Ingles to Faro de Maspaloma  at Sunset

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Stunning beach ,well worth a visit if in the areaBeautifully clean and a safe vibe , great presence from Red Cross and life guardsThe food and drink in the huts is quite expensive however, so take your own

reviews.title: Spectacular - but hard work!!!
reviews.text: The beach at Maspalomas seems to be a super highway for walkers along the waters edge. I have never seen so many people walking along a beach. The beach runs from the square at Playa del Ingles to Faro and Melonares. Its about two miles or so and takes about an hour - depending if you stop to take photos. There are a number of areas along the beach for loungers to sit and sunbathe but it is often quite windy. Some of the areas are designated (or at least have a preference for) Nudist areas and there is one area where there is a Gay area (no7 area) so be prepared to see naked bodies on the waters edge. If you like the idea of walking over the dunes you should be prepared for hard walking as the soft sand is difficult to walk on.

reviews.title: Winter Sun
reviews.text: Having been to Gran Canaria several times over the last decade, the beach at Maspalomas is one of my favourites. The wide expanse of clean sand with the dunes behind make this a go to destination. There are good facilities at the Faro end with shops and restaurants and the long walk towards Playa del ingles has beach bars located every half a kilometre. This beach is inclusive and has a large stretch where clothes are optional but you can keep your trunks on and admire the views !There are plenty of sun loungers for hire or you can rest up on the sand and watch the Atlantic waves.

reviews.title: Fine beach
reviews.text: Family place. Lots of clear sand. Clean. Loos near bye. Some shops and cafes. Life guard from Red Cross. Good.

reviews.title: Love it here
reviews.text: Lovley views,lots of waking the kids loved it ,they is toilets just of the beach (kids where busting looked all over finally found them

reviews.title: Unique Experience!!!
reviews.text: Maspalomas beach is simply wonderful! It's huge and you feel like in the desert, but there's also the ocean there to swim if you wish. The sand is simply fantastic!!! A piece of Sahara in the ocean! No crowds, just piece, sun and the charming sound of the ocean waves. Might be quite windy though. :)

reviews.title: dunes
reviews.text: this is a world heritage site famous for its sand dunes all the way from the sahara a natural sun trap

reviews.title: relaxing winter holiday
reviews.text: Maspalomas is a great place to stay beautiful promenade to walk along, with plenty of cafes and restaurants to cater for most tastes.

reviews.title: Not my favourite beach
reviews.text: Long beach and lovely to go for a long walk as well as to walk on the dunes, but it wasn’t my favourite beach in Gran Canaria. To be quite honest, apart from the dunes there is no other reason to go there - you’ll find other lovely and small beaches to go to around the island.

reviews.title: Sun sand sea
reviews.text: Great place to walk and catch the sun as you walk , beautiful scenery, but be aware there’s loads of nakedness but that doesn’t bother me , you to let you no if you don’t like that

reviews.title: wonderfull beach
reviews.text: The beach and dunes of Masplaomas are both spectacular, the beach is soft golden sand. There are also beach bars along the beach for snacks and drinks, also plenty of sun beds and parasols to rent if needed or just chill out on your own towel.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This popular beach behind the sand dunes is a real sand beach with plenty of fine white sand.The beach is divided into areas: for families and kids, and nudist zones.There are all sorts of sports and leisure facilities available including showers, beach bars, and restaurants.

reviews.title: Maspalomas
reviews.text: What a lovely resort.  Built purely for tourists however without the usual touristy nonsense.  Fantastic shops and restaurants.   All ages will enjoy

reviews.title: Great shopping with some fun
reviews.text: One of the most popular places for eat drink and shopping. In here must be like 50 plus bars and restaurants and many shops.there are many LGBTQ bars with great shows.

reviews.title: A desert visit by the sea
reviews.text: What a glorious place to visit if you are in Gran Canaria. The dunes are what you see on TV of how a desert looks. There are fantastic cafés and restaurants on the way there. And a fantastic beach which is perfectly patrolled by lifeguards.Being a high tourist location, the restaurants are a bit more expensive. The dunes are free to enter.There is a tiolet on the beach. But you have to pay to use it.There is a local medical facility for visitors to use if needed.Please remember though that part of the beach is a nudist designated beach which is on the far left facing the sea. Families and those of you like my wife and I remain to the right, nearest to the facilities and amenities.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Great beach for sunbathing and walking/running. Spent many happy sunny hours there over my holiday. Always clean.

reviews.title: Quiet area
reviews.text: Lovely small town easy to get around by bus or taxi. Lovely walks along the promenade.  Quieter than most of the towns on the coastline but just as pretty.

reviews.title: You must go see this!
reviews.text: This is something that cannot be shown on pictures, you must go see it. It's amazing to see how that sand can make theese very big formations. And the sand is so smooth to walk in. We went there on a windy day, that's not the best if you want to sit in the sand and enjoy the view. Cause you'll get sand in the eyes and the mouth no matter how hard you try to avoid it, but even tho, don't skip it, go see it you will be amazed.

reviews.title: A must visit
reviews.text: Beautiful place ! Stunning views and great beach. The dunes are cool and it will fell like a complete workout walking around there. well at the beach there are sunbeams etc you could rent... this is defo one of the places to visit in GC.

reviews.title: sand dunes not for the old and in-firmed
reviews.text: not for the very old, with walking problems, can be a bit scary, but very enjoyable, been many times and loved it, you can get to the dunes by walking from the light house, say about 20mins walk sand is to die for, only problem when you get wind you get sand blasted, like nude bathing this is the place for you, like any other bathing again try this place, for walking its great miles of it,

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: We rented a car and drove to Maspalomas sand dunes. Well worth both money and time! We had a fun time walking and running in the sand. Will definitely do it again.

reviews.title: Nice place to spend a few hours
reviews.text: This is a nice place and does have nice views, but no great wonder of the world.  If you are in the area, go but I wouldn't drive a long time to get there.

reviews.title: UNAVAILABLE TO VIEW
reviews.text: Was lokking forward to visit this beautiful natural site, only to be frustrated with the ability to park anywhere.  The near by shopping venues were the only places we could park, and that meant a long way to walk.  After several attempts on different times of our holiday we gave up and walked it, but only saw the outskirts of it then.  We took a few photographs of the edge.   Everywhere was very packed, and was surprised the many peoples who travel over Christmas.

reviews.title: Rolling Waves of Sand and Sea
reviews.text: The Dunes and Beach of Maspalomas are a surprising sight and something not seen every day. Get lost in the dramatic sweeping dunes, walking along their crest of in the valleys between only to find before you a beautiful beach with inviting waters, even in December I was able to spend 45 minutes in the water! Key Points:1) Bring Sunblock and Water. Not a lot of shade in the area and you don't want to wait for hours in lines a the drink shacks.2) Dunes are gorgeous and fun. Have fun, try running down the dunes and jumping by the edge!3) Be careful of the rip-tide. Maspalomas beach is a place where currents intersect. On some days the riptide is enough to carry you away even if you're in knee-high water.4) Not a nude beach, specifically. But plenty of nude people. However, people are comfortable is how they do the beach there.

reviews.title: Long walks
reviews.text: Is nice to walk along the beach, it’s windy though so not so nice to sunbathing. Take water and snacks with you if you like to have a long walk

reviews.title: Beautiful park and Beach
reviews.text: This beach really is for everyone! If you’ve young babies in pram or disabled/elderly in wheel chairs then follow the wooden path towards shops and cafes. If you want tomgo the nudiest parts dunes or catorgory parts of the beach go along the sand towards the dunes. The sand, sea and nature park are all beautiful, sand can obviously get hot especially dunes so take a good pair of walking foot ware that cover most or all of foot.

reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.text: Cool place to see a natural wonder of the world. Amazing sight to see - must visit if you're in the area!

reviews.title: Not so crowded and large
reviews.text: Kinds really enjoyed the beach and playing in the sanddune. Among different beaches we visited (Puerto rico, Playa de mogan, Ingles) we really loved this one.

reviews.title: Beach
reviews.text: Nice enough - busy most times and nice walks along promenade. Places to eat nice, can get varied costs. Shopping centre further along with free toilets. Toilets near main beach area 6euros and sunbed 12

reviews.title: Beautiful dunes in front of the ocean
reviews.text: The beach is 8 km long and you can walk to the lighthouse in 1.5 hour, the ocean on one side and gorgeous sand dunes on the other. Recharging experience!

reviews.title: Must see and visit
reviews.text: The beach walkabout from Playa del Ingles to Meloneras is at the dawn and sunset great. Just enjoy the nature.

reviews.title: Good Sand but a lot of people
reviews.text: Grabbing a bit of sun between Christmas and new year we were not let down. The beach with its dunes is large taking a good hour to an hour an half to walk along the coast. The sand is soft and feels good on the feet. The beach is very clean and the dunes are the most extensive on the island. There were a large number of people with pockets of nudist which are an integral part of the landscape.

reviews.title: Very big but very crouded
reviews.text: The beach at Maspalomas is huge but it is fully carpeted with sun-loungers and parasols. I was pretty put off by that. The dunes are worth a visit if you are staying there.The good news about this beach is that it is in the Canaries and as such the days are fairly hot and you can comfortably spend time on the beach and in the water. There is nowhere else in Europe that I'm away you can do this in December. That is hard to beat.

reviews.title: Beautiful dunes - a must visit if you are in Maspalomas!
reviews.text: Sand dunes are beautiful in Maspalomas, makes sure you climb them if you are visiting here even if only for the day!

reviews.title: Nice
reviews.text: Great place for photoThe Desert 🌵🐫 long sand desert beach should visit there if you like to walk in the sand and want to see a little desert in EUROPE

reviews.title: Sun in winter
reviews.text: Two weeks in Playa del Ingles/ Maspalomas in December . first impressions were mixed - lovely warm sunshine, but frequent quite strong breezes. The beach - huge and open meant that sand could get whipped up and be irritating. Made for the shelter of the dunes and the gay beach most days. Masses of people - but masses of space. The sea was always turbulent so not good for steady swimming but great fun for jumping and plunging into the waves. Think Hunstanton on a good day in English summer! A very lively resort with wide busy promenade lined with restaurants, bars and shops.

reviews.title: Busier than London
reviews.text: Dunes are exceptional, but the whole place is mad, a constant stream of people walking. I think I expect something else from a beach. Next time we’ll go somewhere else.

reviews.title: congratulations that they thought ahead to protect this wildlife research from development
reviews.text: Long beach walks and wild life sightings for nature lovers.  Also easy access to the beach with lots of kiosks for snacks, lunch or things you may have forgotten to bring.   Kudos to the Spanish government for having the foresight to save this as a wildlife reserve.

reviews.title: Beaches to warm your heart and body.
reviews.text: Sand dunes and beaches are to be visited to be believed. We also took a boat ride on a wonderful motor-cum-sail boat, called The Secret. It is run by a an enterprising woman who bought it from a German designer. It is perfect for small groups to visit various parts of the island or beyond. I love wild beaches which are accessible by boats only.

reviews.title: Lovely walkable stretch of coastline
reviews.text: We enjoyed ourselves walking this stretch of coastline. On some parts there are a lot of pebble/rocks laying around, so that in account. Furthermore there are a lot of nudists. So that's another thing to consider.

reviews.title: A lot of walking
reviews.text: This is a good place to visit as long as your prepared to walk .... ALOT! There are sporadic beach bars every 100 meters or so which charge silly prices so beware.

reviews.title: Amazing dunes but beware
reviews.text: No-one can deny the beauty of Maspalomas dunes, however it is easy to get lost or find yourself having to ascend a large dune. With all the income the local council gets from sunbed and parasol hire (7 euro 50 cent per couple per session) much could be done to mark out pathways and fence the precious environment. Also beware nudists using some dunes for strictly adult purposes.

reviews.title: A truly unique experience
reviews.text: The beach is several miles long & very wide & the sand dunes provide for a truly unique experience...be careful as the waves & current can be strong! there are certain parts of the beach appropriate for families while some areas are geared for the naturists & the dunes for the sexually promiscuous...

reviews.title: Very crowded and crashing waves.
reviews.text: Not too crazy about this place, the beach is long. The waves crashing, tourists everywhere you look. Not my scene personally but I like more pristine places.There is an absence of public washrooms, those you do find charge .50€Many people obviously like it.We were warned not to swim by the lifeguards. Apparently a rip tide.

reviews.title: Buyer Beware!
reviews.text: Superb beach and high quality restaurants and shopping alongside a world  class beach. Excellent  tourist facilities for all budgets.

reviews.title: Amazing...
reviews.text: If you are in Gran canaria it is a 100% must do to go and take in the majestic sites of the sand dunes. What a great photo opportunity for you and your family and friends....

reviews.title: Great beach with facilities close by
reviews.text: A nice sandy beach with safe entry/exit to/from the sea. Plenty of nearby shops and eateries to help meet the needs of the day. Worth a visit....

reviews.title: Clean
reviews.text: Lovely clean beach views amazing walking along this beach you do get a sense of a tropical feel not to be missed.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: The most gorgeous beach, nice eateries and supermarkets close by. Sunbeds and umbrella’s for hire and a great view. So nice 😍

reviews.title: Good
reviews.text: Lots of restaurants and bars but not many bars with entertainment, very little really. Lots of things to see, camel ride was brill, lighthouse, sand dunes.I will be back to visit.

reviews.title: Fantastic beach
reviews.text: A must vist place. Fantastic with the dunes and mountains as a back drop. Take a dip in the sea for a refreshing swim. Sunbeds and kiosks in intervals along the length. So vast room for everybody

reviews.title: Beautiful but can be very windy
reviews.text: My wife and I always walk from the Faro lighthouse through Playa Del Ingles and onto San Augustin.  We always used to walk right next to the sea,  but in recent years we use the paved walkway at the top end of the dunes to avoid being totally sandblasted. It is still a nice walk and an unusual experience for a couple of Bits.

reviews.title: Beautiful sandy beach
reviews.text: Although it was cloudy most days when the sun did come out this place is fantastic. And if you fancy going ‘eau natural’ then there is nothing stopping you. Enjoy and let it all hang out!

reviews.title: Walking on the moon; and it’s free!
reviews.text: Well worth a visit, especially near sunset when it’s cooler to walk on the sand. Can be hard work climbing the dunes but it’s great fun and children (and adults) will love the challenge. Great attraction, and the fact it’s free makes it all the better.

reviews.title: Touristy and overcrowded ....not to bother
reviews.text: My husband and I had this town included as part of a tour and are ever so grateful we didn’t have to spend more than hour there. From windy conditions that resulted in a continuous sandstorm preventing most people from sitting on the beach to enjoy  the seaside views to aggressive vendors who offered us cheap meals in packed restaurants filled only with English speaking patrons . The menus certainly did not include any semblance of traditional Spanish food .There was an over abundance of shops that carried only beach related gear and tacky souvenirs for sale at ridiculous prices and no displays of local Spanish culture. Moving along the streets was virtually impossible without being jostled or pushed ahead so we decided to leave the area as quickly as we could. We had thought we’d like to spend a couple of extra days on our month long holiday here but so happy we are staying put in the beautiful city of Las Palmas.

reviews.title: Poor beach
reviews.text: Gravelly sand, lots of rocks at the shore break and very busy. Be aware that there is a nature preserve behind that is used nudists, particularly men, so not idea to take the kids for a walk there!

reviews.title: Not really for families more for german nudists
reviews.text: Came here a couple of times.Windy and bit of a rip tide so not great for swimming.It makes for a great beach walk.Great if you like to be nude and bend down all the time to adust your sun bed.We even saw mums and dads nude in front of their small children, call social services!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful sandy beach with a few bars and restaurants not too many lucky lucky men! We visited in the day but there's plenty to do at night . Showers provided and sun loungers available

reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.text: Dunes were amazing view..there was a long path to reach the beach that is windy and mostly popular for nudists.

reviews.title: Nice clean Sandy Beach!
reviews.text: This is a nice clean sandy beach. The waves are definitely present! but not dangerously so when I was there. Nice area all round with some sand sculptures in certain areas on the beach, plenty of places to eat and shop to, and a nice promenade to walk down to ward the lighthouse

reviews.title: Clean tidy beach
reviews.text: Clean and tidy beach with beach bars and portable toilets but I cant comment on whether they are clean or not as we didnt use them. Good for walking and swimming.

reviews.title: Nice beach!
reviews.text: This beach is great. During our stay the ocean was a bit wild and the waves were high. We had a great time with our kids and they loved the high waves.

reviews.title: Love it.
reviews.text: Awesome place in the middle of modern buildings and hotels. Perfect for a walk and have some fun. Sucream requaries. Sometimes may meet naked or even having sex gay couples but .... Leave it  without comment 😁

reviews.title: Best Sand Dunes outside the Sahara
reviews.text: These are but a few of the many photographs taken at the time. I promise you its absolute magic to stand looking over the dunes.  My photo's do not do the place justice.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Maspalomas beach is beautiful and has lovely clear sand. You can walk for miles along the beach although be warned the only shelter from the sun is the rentable sun beds with umbrellas.

reviews.title: Amazing sunsets as well as sunrises
reviews.text: We experienced during our holidays the most amazing sunsets as well as sunrises at Mespalomas beach.

reviews.title: Lovely walk
reviews.text: Walked from play de ingles to maspalolmas and it was lovelyWarning though for families nudist beach just at play de inlgles and a gay nudist beach just further round also many walking along the beach so OK for adults but I found it uncomforting to see kids around that were naked whilst their parents were clothed or visit versa..

reviews.title: If you like the waves
reviews.text: Wow! I like the waves! Big fan here! Summer all the year! Hope i will come back again! I love this beach!

reviews.title: Stunning beach
reviews.text: Just spent a week in Maspalomas and spent nearly everyday on this stunning beach,very sandy with stunning dunes and very safe bathing.Also what makes this beach is the variety of people using it - families , naturists ,gays, singles just about everyone you could think of all mixing together in a very stunning surrounding - one of the best beaches i have ever been on - if not the best

reviews.title: Beautiful sandy beach stretching for my miles
reviews.text: Beautiful sandy beach stretching for miles. Loads of sun beds and restaurants and bars all along the coast. Great for families but no if you prefer peace and quiet. Heads for the more secluded beaches.

reviews.title: Exchange the cold days for the sun,a good time and fun !
reviews.text: We went for a walk from our hotel and decided to cross the dunes, finally we found ourselves exactly in the middle of the nudist area !  The atmosphere around the place was so relaxing that we couldn't resist and joined the community in no time ! It's not true that there are only German oldsters hanging around there,we heard people of different ages talking different languages and we aren't Germans too,we come from Ukraine ! Getting naked gave us an incredible feeling of being part of nature ! Too bad some people don't understand that ! So,if you like strolling along Playa de Maspalomas, which is really great, but you get embarrassed seeing naked bodies, just keep your eyes down or turn them towards the ocean when you pass the nudists and keep on walking !

reviews.title: Maspalomas deserttrip
reviews.text: Read a lot of reviews about it being too hot to walk on desert during the day. So i waited until 18-18.30 before i went to visit the desert..I went through the RIU palace hotel entrance and it was truly stunning to see the view from there.The sand dunes were awesome to walk on. The walk from the hotell to the beach takes about 20-25 minutes... I saw the beautiful sunset and I managed to dodge all the nudity I had read about. I only regret that i didn’t visit the earlier so I had more time to enjoy the desert in the daylight. The sun surely went down fast and it was truly awesome.... To think about. Bring scarfs to cover face and hair. It sure blows sand everywhere 😃

reviews.title: Stunning view
reviews.text: On a clear day the dunes are worth a visit and walking along the dunes across to playa . This is a nature reserve and nudist sun bathing so don’t be embarrassed

reviews.title: Walk along the beach
reviews.text: We went to the market on Wednesday and got a taxi to the beach and we ended up at Playa de Ingles. We walked from there all around the dunes back to maspalomas taking us roughly 1 hour 45 mins but we were paddling and chatting so not on a major mission. Most of the walk is a naturalist beach so be prepared to see all and sundry including the 80 year old 🤔 swinging low!

reviews.title: HUGE BEACH NEXT TO A LAGOON
reviews.text: My husband and I travelled here with a Royal Caribbean cruise excursion, Unfortunately, the day was cloudy and the beach was a few hours from the port.  While the ride over was pleasant and we were able to see a lot of the communities on the way we felt that it was too far a distance to travel in such a short period of time and we felt rushed and not able to enjoy our time here.  The water was a bit on the cool side and the facilities were far from the drop off point.  Toilets had a fee.  If you enjoy beaches it was a truly wide and beautiful one and the wildlife in the lagoon was quite amazing.  We would not travel there in the short window provided by a cruise, though.

reviews.title: this is what it's all about
reviews.text: Our fav place to walk later in afternoon then get a coffee. Beautiful scenery and perfect beaches to walk along on the edge of the sea

reviews.title: Good place to stay if you love waves
reviews.text: Okay, the beach is pretty good, however, I would stress mostly cons here. 1st - no toilets. 2nd - impossible to park your car ( I found free 25 minutes from). 3rd - hide waves. Well, it is definitely pros if you like waves, but if you are with a kid - I am not sure this beach is for you.

reviews.title: Dunes are great.. Full frontals not so great!!
reviews.text: Visited this beach as was staying close by in San Agustin.  The beach itself is beautiful and the dunes dramatic and great fun to scale.  Now there is the issue of nudism..  I recognised the fact that people, (mostly the Germans) may want to bare all, which is their freedom, but there seems to be NO section of Maspalomas beach where MY freedom of not wanting to be subjected to breasts, bums and willies is respected, which is unreasonable.  Personally it doesn't impress me as a health care professional, as I see those assets all the time and to be honest, some of what I saw may need urgent medical attention!!  You could  tell those who were just trying to show off what they had 🤔The beach is near several five star hotels that usually would have been on my list of places to stay, but I'm actually very glad that I didn't choose then for that reason alone.It seems to be the place to come if you want to flaunt your bits, so please beware if you are not that way inclined - I suggest you find a quiet, more family friendly  beach, of which there are a few, if you want to enjoy the sights of the sea, sand and landscape, without being subjected to body parts swaying in the wind.. I wish someone had told me before I got there.

reviews.title: A Great Walk
reviews.text: Starting from the busy Playa del Ingles it's a good 3 - 4 mile walk to Playa de Meloneras. There are quiet bits near the spectacular dunes and away from the hotels. If you walk barefoot (recommended) you will have to walk along the waterline as the dry sand is too hot to stand on for any length of time and too soft to walk on.This beach has a lot of naturism on display (and some of it not at all attractive) so you may want to think twice about coming here with children.

reviews.title: Spectacular walk
reviews.text: Walked across the dunes an amazing experience well worth the effort and not as hard as we thought it would be

reviews.title: Shoreline stroll
reviews.text: Playa de Maspalomas is a stunningly beautiful outlook with the white frothing and rolling waves on top of the most azure sea, to the endless sandy beach that stretches out far ahead. Of course the Maspalomas Dunas are there too. Plenty of water based activities to try. Plenty of space to lay in the sun, sunloungers & parasols for €5 a day all along the beach with some having local restaurant nearby on the promenade and along further and away from the shops and restaurants are kiosks that serve the beach goers. Naturism is normal and this has to be expected whilst on the beach, from topless to complete nudity. All very cosmopolitan

reviews.title: Beautiful beach but busy and crowded
reviews.text: Thursday 20th September and we walked from our hotel, RIU Club Hotel Gran Canaria, along the promenade we were on our way to visit the famous Dunas Maspalomas which are situated along side the beach.Maspalomas beach, with its golden & black sands, stretches for around 2 kilometres and has the famous Maspalomas Dunas at its back.There are large areas of the beach where there are rows and rows of sunbeds and umbrellas available for hire. It looked all a bit cluttered and busy.There was space along the beach where visitors can spread out the beach mats and towels, on the sand, and relax and enjoy the glorious sunshine and views of the Dunas.There are lots of restaurants and bars by the beach. We saw a bar offering sunbeds, umbrella, towels and shower for €12 a day.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Spent a few days walking on edge of the sea plenty of space and shops close by also if like us you like walking we were informed of the nude beach area well let’s just say many were mostly men

reviews.title: Very crowded
reviews.text: Not the most beautiful beach I’ve been , very very crowded . Although there are plenty of eating places and bars and shops once your there . It’s not golden sand but not black either . Although the sea is beautiful and actually warm . The beach is clean , but it can be very hard to get a sunbed , which is €7.50 for two and parasol , they get taken very quickly . In saying all this , we did spend a few days there and we did have a lovely time . I think I’m used to golden sands and not so busy beaches where I usually go which is southern Spain.

reviews.title: Nice Beach
reviews.text: Nice beach with lots of bars shops and restaurants. You can walk many hundreds of metres either along the beach or on the promenade.

reviews.title: The best Asian food in Gran Canaria
reviews.text: Was a recommendation ,today we been here MissAsia.the food is lovely and the sushi was amazing,freshly and tasting great. Lovely recommend ,we will come back.

reviews.title: Relaxing
reviews.text: As far as beaches go this was one of my favourites. Mikes upon miles of sand and beautiful sea. Loved the sand dunes, and places to get ice creams and coffees. Great day out for all the family.

reviews.title: Beautiful long sandy beach.
reviews.text: lovely smooth sandy beach with a long slope into the sea so no quick drop into the water. The beach is very long but does have kiosks along the way for a rest and a cold beer or ice cream.The people we met at kiosk 7 were very friendly and we had a lovely time on the beach

reviews.title: I spent 4 days out of 14 days at the beach
reviews.text: The wind was a bit extreme on one of the days. but otherwise this was a lovely sandy beach to spend some quality sun bathing time on. I went a bit further onto the beach, away from the masses, towards the nudist sections, where the crowds thin out and you can  get a fair sized bit of beach all to yourself. The water was also wonderful. Back on dry land, the area of Faro Maspalomas, around the beach has some wonderful restaurants and up-market shopping. All in all a lovely part of the resort to visit

reviews.title: Nice dunes and good for families
reviews.text: Came here and really enjoyed the beach. One of the best in Gran Canaria. The dunes are beautiful and worth a hike up and down. Deck chairs are EUR 2.50 each and umbrella EUR 2.50

reviews.title: Gay beach
reviews.text: The gay section of the beach at Hut 7 seems to have disappeared. Very disappointed to find the beach in a right mess

reviews.title: Amazing Beach
reviews.text: If you like a white sandy beach with huge dunes this is the place to go. Dotted with refreshment huts it is perfect day to do nothing.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: We couldn't wait to walk from our hotel to this famous beach in Gran Canaria.Our journey began on the far East where a delicious ice cream seemed mandatory.There were many bars , restaurants and shops en route towards the western part of this ca. 2 1/2 kilometre stretch of endless dunes and sand !Within minutes, we left the shops and hustle and bustle of the commercial area .The sand invited us to sit down for awhile and take in the view of the vast Atlantic ocean and the many people promenading past us. We became part of the crowd thatcelebrates this wonderful coastline.It wasn't too long before we were enticed towards a westward excursion. It began to seem endless. The occasional nudists couldn't really bother us but dehydrationwas the menace. There are a few beach huts along the way .Didn't that mineral water quench our thirst !!It had taken about 45 minutes in 33 degree temperatures , the lighthouse was now clearly visible and we knew a taxi would have to take us back to the hotel! In November , we plan on returning to this friendly island to do it all over again. When in Gran Canaria head down to Maspolomas beach!

reviews.title: Sun, sand & Dunes
reviews.text: A very large beach with fine sand and an ocean that attracts you and at the same time calms you.  In the back the dunes look at you.

reviews.title: Wonderful but beware nudists!
reviews.text: Lovely plaza and boulevard with restaurants and shops. Beach is spotless and very popular however go too far and expect nudists. Didn't bother me but not to all tastes. Do the whole walk and it's about 90 mins and only 3€ taxi back. Beautiful spot!

reviews.title: A desert in Gran Canaria
reviews.text: It worth being seen. Not easy to park before getting to the dunes of Maspalomas but once arrived the view is something surrealistic.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: Lovely beach very clean and looked after, plenty of bars and places to eat, always feel safe here with several life guard and first aid stations

reviews.title: Grill El Toro
reviews.text: You must try their chataubriand. It’s excellent. Next door to Lili supermarket just off the beach. Excellent service, good chef and great food. Have eaten chataubriand in lots of places but this beats them all . At €32 it’s good value. Try it.

reviews.title: Sandy beach
reviews.text: We 2 adults and 2 kids (12 and 10) came here for the kids to play on some soft sand! There are plenty of loungers and parasols to rent which are reasonably priced.  The kids had fun jumping over the waves in the sea.  There are toilets/ showers nearby for a small charge in addition to the free shower stand on the beach.  Just behind the beach are a few shops/ bars/ restaurants.  There are a few “looky looky” women about trying to sell massages but politely walked on when we said no thank you.

reviews.title: beautiful beach
reviews.text: lovely beach refreshing atlantic ocean waves great bars and restaurants along the beach and the beautiful lighthouse lighting your way in the evenings

reviews.title: Worst beach ever
reviews.text: There are hardly any facilities such as changing rooms, wcs, showers or water fountains. Only by the entrance to the beach you will find something, which is the only ones to use even if you have chairs 10minute walk away. Overcrowded. Too many waves to be able to swim and too much sand whirled in the water to bathe. For the first time in my life we left the beach after one hour. Very disappointed.

reviews.title: Nice beach walk.
reviews.text: We walked across the dues passing the nudists some distance away.Really enjoyed sitting near the sea people watching other walkers and then walking in the waters to Playa del Ingles to get a well deserved drink.

reviews.title: Overcrowded
reviews.text: I came from the playa del ingles side so did not witness the nudist beach area but there's plenty of topless bathing.  The place is ridiculously overcrowded even mid week off season.  Bits of the beach is covered with rocks.  In the mid section plenty of shops and restaurants.  It's ok perhaps less people would've made it more pleasant

reviews.title: Nice and near the city center
reviews.text: I went there with a friend a couple of times during my holiday in Gran Canaria, on the days in which we decided not to explore the island.It's a nice beach, but it's quite crowded, and when we had enough time we preferred other places.

reviews.title: Great sand dunes
reviews.text: A great walk it takes about 20 to walk and then we walked along the beach but!!!! It’s a nudist beach 🤣 the sand is so hot make sure you wear a full shoe not flip flops

reviews.title: 💩Hole
reviews.text: What a dump. Tourist trap, can’t walk down the road without being ask if you need any drugs. Sitting at a bar watching football and constantly getting the smell of weed.

reviews.title: nature at its best
reviews.text: This is a beautiful area to walk across the sand is beautiful and shines in the sun. There are areas of natural plants with lizards darting about.

reviews.title: Still for the well of
reviews.text: We went down on the free bus from our hotel, not a lot of changes from last time we was here a few more shops in the shopping centre, but the main shops are still for the Rich,Rolex, Cartier,and the rest

reviews.title: Strange Atmosphere
reviews.text: I walked the beach twice and found the atmosphere strange especially around nudist area. I witnessed many sights for sore eyes and felt uncomfortable walking on my own on the beach and that is from someone who has seen a lot in his 55 years of living.

reviews.title: Maspalomas Beach 🏖 Mid section nudist
reviews.text: What a beautiful place. 6km of sparkly sand and lovely see (very hot sand you’ll need yo wear flip flops. Each end of the beach is family very relaxed very common for topless women with partners families etc.Mid section is nudist with a short walk and then 🏳️‍🌈 . It’s all very relaxed and comfortable and the nudist section is mainly I big further back but expect some nudism on beach and in the sea.Don’t forget your sun cream - drinks and snack at pop up bars.

reviews.title: Warning - naked old men
reviews.text: The dunes are a must sea. Waking across them is hard work and I’d strongly recommend trainers over flip flops or sandals. Also don’t go past 11 as the heat can get scorching! Be warned. The dunes are also a nudest beach and you will see some sights!

reviews.title: Day out
reviews.text: Love maspalomas, bit of shopping, cinema, eats, amazing beach, and the sand dunes are something else

reviews.title: Day trip to beach
reviews.text: Day trip to beach, lovely sand, take towels and don’t pay for sun beds, can buy a beach umbrella for 12 Euro’s, good cafe and shops near light house, lovely walk along promenade

reviews.title: Family holiday
reviews.text: The beach is a nice beach with sand dunes bars restaurants a really nice pleasant walk. There is a lovely shopping centre within the area of Maspalomas has lots of shops bars and restaurants also souvenir shops.

reviews.title: Upper flass
